issues.issue: The texture model cannot hold a complete game's art: each image is one whole layer of a square tier array (64/128/256/512 px; resized to that square; anything larger shrunk to 512), quads have no UV sub-rectangle (no atlas, no sprite sheet), each array holds 255 images, and nothing is ever unloaded.
issues.gameImpact: Every animation frame, tile and UI piece costs a layer: about 1020 PNG/JPEG images per session over the four arrays (on BC7/ASTC desktops all PNGs share the four rgba8 overflow arrays), shared by every level, with no way to free a finished level's art. Sheets from Aseprite/TexturePacker/Tiled are unusable as is, backgrounds wider than 512 px must be cut into tiles or are downscaled, non-square art is resampled twice. A load at the cap reallocates and copies the whole array (about 341 MiB on tier 3) before it throws 'is full'.
issues.evidence: quad.wgsl:5-7; prim-params-schema.ts:32; texture-manager.ts:5-7, :684-702, :706-760 (throw after ensureOverflowCapacity/ensureTierCapacity), :349-433 and :442-536 (realloc + copy + destroy), :191 (cache never evicted), :715, :741; no unload method in TextureManager; hyperion.ts:675-680 (compact() calls a non-existent shrinkUnusedTiers); demo/lighting-sprite.ts:14-18, :552-553 (the harness must reload the page at the cap); docs/plans/hyperion-engine-design-v3.md:500-509 (arrays chosen over atlases).
issues.roundFix: Not fixed. The step-8 plan lists texture unloading and tier mips out of step (docs/plans/2026-10-14-step8-sprite-light-plan.md:48); 8b, 8c, 10 and 9 do not touch the texture manager. The realloc-before-throw at the cap is only recorded for step 9 with a candidate fix (step-8 plan :4482, note (3)); the masterplan has no atlas or unload item.
issues.workaround: Slice sheets at runtime (canvas → blob: URL → loadTexture, which accepts blob:/data: URLs) at one layer per frame, budget layers per tier and per level, or destroy() and re-create the engine between level sets. Engine fix: a UV rect for quads in primParams (slots unused today), a layer free-list/unload API, larger or non-square tiers.

issues.issue: Mirrored sprites disappear: a negative x or y scale (scale(-1, 1), the usual way to face a character left) reverses the unit quad's winding, and every entity pipeline culls back faces.
issues.gameImpact: A flipped character, enemy or prop is not drawn, casts no shadow and gets no outline, while the cull still counts it and picking still hits it. Every left/right-facing sprite of a platformer or action-adventure would need a pre-flipped copy of each frame, doubling its layer use under rendering-1's cap.
issues.evidence: forward-pass.ts:271, :285 (cullMode 'back', uber and opaque pipelines); render/passes/occluder-seed-stage.ts:96; render/passes/selection-seed-pass.ts:107; CCW unit quad forward-pass.ts:156-168; only the light pipeline uses cullMode 'none' (render/passes/light-accum-stage.ts:164-166); verified on the device per the round plan's step-8 sub-decision 2 (docs/plans/2026-09-27-open-items-round-plan.md:73, 'una scala negativa lo fa scartare'); step-8 plan :4482 note (1b).
issues.roundFix: Not fixed. Step 8 explicitly leaves it (step-8 plan :48); it is recorded for step 9 as point (1b) with a candidate fix (cullMode 'none' in the four pipeline families), 'da decidere col proprietario'. Step 9 is a close-out (docs, reviews, GPU legs) and does not commit to it.
issues.workaround: Set cullMode to 'none' in those four pipelines (the recorded analysis says no pixel changes without a mirroring transform) — a few lines of engine work — or ship pre-flipped textures.

issues.issue: No per-sprite colour, tint, opacity or visibility: a quad draws exactly its texel (white when untextured), lines and beziers are white or textured, gradients are always opaque, and the protocol has no colour, alpha or visibility command.
issues.gameImpact: Hit flashes, fade in/out, team or palette colours, darkening, ghost trails, invulnerability blinking and hiding pooled sprites need baked texture variants (more layers) or extra entities.
issues.evidence: quad.wgsl:11-17; line.wgsl:119; bezier.wgsl:139; gradient.wgsl:49; ring-buffer.ts:15-93 (CommandType list); entity-handle.ts:354-563 (no tint/opacity/visible method).
issues.roundFix: None: not in the round nor in the masterplan.
issues.workaround: Texture variants; box shadows (rgba primParams, blur 0) as translucent coloured rectangles for screen fades; a sprite on its own light layer tinted by a masked global light (needs the lit graph, at most 16 layers); scale(0, 0) or off-screen to hide.

issues.issue: Text has no working path: the MSDF glyph shader exists, but TextManager is a placeholder and unexported, layoutText handles one line with no wrapping, newlines, kerning or alignment, no EntityHandle method sets glyph parameters, and MSDF has never been checked on a GPU.
issues.gameImpact: HUD counters, menus, dialogue, damage numbers and localisation have no in-engine route; each glyph would be a hand-configured entity, the atlas is resized to a ≤512-px square at load, and the AA parameter appears to behave as a UV-unit range rather than the screen pixels it is named for (code reading, unverified).
issues.evidence: text/text-manager.ts:17-20 (bitmap closed, textureLayer = 0 placeholder); index.ts:17-20; text/text-layout.ts:13-50; prefab/registry.ts:126-137 (only public route to SDFGlyph primParams, via the private producer); msdf-text.wgsl:12-26, :46-52; demo/primitives.ts:293-294 ('MSDF text' skipped: no font atlas); no font asset in the repo; hyperion-masterplan.md:261-264, :309 claim shelf packing, LRU and zoom validation.
issues.roundFix: None; the MSDF atlas-rect convention is out of step 8 (step-8 plan :48).
issues.workaround: DOM/CSS overlay for HUD, menus and dialogue (project world anchors with cam.viewProjection each frame); or a glyph layer on prefabs with an offline msdf-atlas-gen atlas of at most 512 px, validated on a GPU first.

issues.issue: No mipmaps, one linear sampler, and FXAA that cannot be switched off: tiers allocate full mip chains but only mip 0 is written, and every primitive samples LOD 0.
issues.gameImpact: Sprites drawn smaller than their tier (zoom-out, 512-px art on small sprites) shimmer while moving; pixel art is bilinearly blurred, FXAA-smeared and lit from a half-resolution light buffer; there is no nearest filtering, integer scaling or pixel snapping; unused mips cost about a third more VRAM.
issues.evidence: texture-manager.ts:216-220, :375-389, :469-483 (mips allocated), :716-720, :742-749, :796-801, :840-845 (mip 0 only); prelude.wgsl:151-171 (textureSampleLevel at LOD 0); fxaa-tonemap.wgsl:107-150; render/passes/light-groups-pass.ts:30, :99.
issues.roundFix: None; 'mip dei tier' is out of step 8 (step-8 plan :48).
issues.workaround: Author images at their displayed size and keep zoom near 1; snap camera and sprites to texels in TS; for pixel art, upscale offline with nearest to the tier size; or patch the sampler and the composite.

issues.issue: No sprite animation, tween or timeline system.
issues.gameImpact: Frame animation, animation state machines, frame events and eased motion or UI transitions are all game-side code, and frames cannot come from an atlas (rendering-1).
issues.evidence: No animation/tween/keyframe/timeline code in ts/src or crates/hyperion-core/src (grep hits only requestAnimationFrame); entity-handle.ts:492-496 (`.texture()` is the only lever, SetTextureLayer 9 bytes, ring-buffer.ts:105); hyperion-masterplan.md:33-37 (a rendering primitive, not a complete engine).
issues.roundFix: None; not in the masterplan either.
issues.workaround: A TS animator in a preTick hook calling `.texture()` per frame; a JS tween library driving position()/scale()/rotation().

issues.issue: No tilemap renderer or map import.
issues.gameImpact: A level is one entity per tile inside the 100 000-entity budget shared with sprites, glyphs and lights; outside Mode C every row is re-uploaded every frame even for a static map (124 B per entity); the fixed 64 KB ring buffer spreads a big level spawn over many frames; RawAPI cannot set depth or transparency; each tile image takes a layer (rendering-1).
issues.evidence: No tilemap code; types.ts:78; raw-api.ts:52-82; worker-render-state.ts:211-214 and renderer.ts:956-996 (full upload outside Mode C); worker-bridge.ts:12 with types.ts:125 (commandBufferSize never read).
issues.roundFix: None.
issues.workaround: EntityHandle per tile with chunked spawn/despawn by camera distance, Mode C for dirty-only scatter uploads, or a plugin RenderPass that draws the map.

issues.issue: Motion advances only on the fixed 60 Hz tick, without render interpolation, the fixedTimestep config is ignored, and a camera set from hooks lags the drawn state by one update.
issues.gameImpact: On 120/144/165 Hz displays (ProMotion MacBooks, gaming monitors) entities move in irregular 0/1-tick steps while a TS camera scrolls every frame, so sprites judder against the background; at 60 Hz the accumulator still runs 0 or 2 ticks on some frames; a camera following a physics- or velocity-driven player trails it by one update and jitters when tick counts vary.
issues.evidence: crates/hyperion-core/src/engine.rs:19 (FIXED_DT const), :197-217, :407-411 (interpolation_alpha, no caller in ts/src or crates); types.ts:127; game-loop.ts:166-172 (preTick sees the previous views, the render runs inside tickFn) with hyperion.ts:876-909.
issues.roundFix: None; not in the round nor in the masterplan.
issues.workaround: Drive the camera from positions the game itself commands, or step it on tickCount changes. Real fix is engine work: keep previous transforms and blend by interpolation_alpha before upload.

issues.issue: Mode A, which preferredMode 'auto' picks on Chrome and Chromium desktop shells, cannot run a content game: no textures, the main-thread camera never reaches the render worker, and particles, bloom, outlines and plugin render passes are unavailable.
issues.gameImpact: With default config a Chrome/Electron build shows untextured entities through a fixed camera at the origin (20 units tall, zoom 1); sprite lights light nothing; the masterplan names desktop embedding as always Mode A.
issues.evidence: capabilities.ts:47-55; types.ts:128; hyperion-masterplan.md:45; hyperion.ts:210-217, :564, :791, :813, :847; plugin-context.ts:126-133; render-worker.ts:18, :41, :66; worker-bridge.ts:370-375.
issues.roundFix: Partly: step 10 renders Mode A's empty world and forwards device loss (round plan §3 row 10). Textures in Mode A are a declared limitation of step 8 (round plan :70, :217); camera sync is scheduled nowhere.
issues.workaround: Force preferredMode: 'B' (needs COOP/COEP) or 'C'.

issues.issue: GPU particles are minimal and composited outside the scene: untextured circles from a point emitter at a continuous rate, alpha blend only, drawn on the swapchain after the whole graph (after tonemap, FXAA and bloom), without depth or lighting, and unavailable in Mode A.
issues.gameImpact: No smoke, sparks, dust or magic sprites, no additive glow, no bursts or one-shots, no emitter shapes; particles always cover every sprite (foreground, in-engine HUD) and ignore lights; destroying an emitter kills its live particles; with any emitter alive the renderer rebuilds a Map of every entity's position each frame. The harness never checks their pixels.
issues.evidence: particle-render.wgsl:57-66; particle-simulate.wgsl:107; particle-types.ts:12-23; particle-system.ts:296-310; renderer.ts:1116-1142 (Map per frame :1118-1130); hyperion.ts:845-850; demo/particles.ts:48, :104, :117-121 (checks passed with literal true).
issues.roundFix: None.
issues.workaround: Sprite particles as transparent entities (sorted and lit, but each an ECS entity and a layer), or a custom plugin pass.

issues.issue: A lost GPU device is never recovered: the renderer logs and calls config.onDeviceLost; texture bitmaps are not retained and the renderer cannot be rebuilt under a live engine.
issues.gameImpact: A driver reset, GPU-process crash or sleep/resume leaves a dead canvas; the game must recreate the whole engine, reload every texture and rebuild its world from its own save.
issues.evidence: renderer.ts:270-273, :285; texture-manager.ts:206-215 (retainBitmaps off by default, no re-upload path); hyperion.ts:73 (renderer readonly); hyperion-masterplan.md:232, :247 (claim transparent recovery).
issues.roundFix: Step 10 forwards Mode A device loss to config.onDeviceLost and corrects masterplan lines 232 and 247; no recovery is planned.
issues.workaround: onDeviceLost → destroy() + Hyperion.create(), reload textures, respawn from a game-side save; autosave often.

issues.issue: One orthographic world camera with position and zoom only: no rotation, follow, bounds, shake, screen/world conversion, second camera, viewport, screen-space layer or render-to-texture; zoom() resets near/far and resize() resets the view to 20 world units tall.
issues.gameImpact: In-engine HUDs, minimaps and split views are unsupported; follow, shake and clamping are game code; mouse aiming needs hand-written inverse-VP math; a custom near/far or virtual resolution must be re-applied after every zoom and resize; nothing draws until resize() or setOrthographic() is called.
issues.evidence: camera-api.ts:1-56 (defaults near -1, far 1000 at :51-56); camera.ts:224 (zero projection until set); index.ts (Camera, screenToRay, mat4Inverse not exported); hyperion.ts:614-626; renderer.ts:104-109, :915.

surveys.afterRound: What the remaining round steps change in this dimension. Step 8 (in progress on feat/step8-sprite-light; GPU gate on the M2 in 9637ee8): the sprite light (a cookie taken from the texture tiers, a square of half-side range turned with its +x axis, culling radius range·√2, shadows from its centre, mirrored by a negative scale); every tier image now drawn upright on quads, lines and beziers (prelude sampleTierOrWhite turns v); sprite lights with layer 0 or an unloaded layer draw nothing, with a dev warning; shadowed lights that cannot draw stop opening SDF sets; engine.debug.textureTiers(); five new harness checks. Step 8 explicitly leaves out texture unloading, textures in Mode A, tier mips, the vanishing mirrored quad, KTXorientation and the MSDF atlas-rect convention (step-8 plan :48). Step 8b (PhysicsAPI) changes nothing here. Step 8c decides SDF padding from the step-6 edge-pop measurement (implemented only if chosen, pixel-identical by default) and makes point/spot marches stop at the SDF exit. Step 10 makes Mode A render its empty world and forwards Mode A device loss to config.onDeviceLost, correcting the masterplan's 'transparent recovery' lines; it adds neither camera sync nor textures in Mode A. Step 9 is documentation, the claude-md-auditor, an adversarial review of steps 6-10 and /gpu-check in Chrome and Safari (Modes B, C, A) on the Mac; the step-8 findings recorded for it (mirrored quads (1b) with a candidate cullMode fix to decide with the owner, KTX2 format mismatch, the realloc at the 256-layer cap, ASTC layer 0, stale handles, CameraAPI.zoom near/far, the opaque() doc) carry no commitment to a fix. The WebKit audio step does not touch rendering. Net: the round completes the lighting feature set, fixes image orientation and widens verification; it closes none of the blockers or majors listed here.
missingForCompleteGame: UV sub-rectangles for quads (texture atlases, sprite sheets) and an atlas-aware asset pipeline
Texture unloading / per-level asset lifetimes, a larger texture budget, textures above 512 px and non-square textures without resampling
Mirrored sprites that draw (cullMode 'none' or equivalent) so characters can face left
Per-sprite tint/colour, opacity and visibility
Mipmap generation and sampling, a selectable nearest sampler, an FXAA switch and a pixel-perfect/integer-scaling mode for pixel art
Sprite animation (frames, state machines, events) and a tween/timeline facility
A tilemap renderer with chunked static upload and Tiled/LDtk import
A text path: font atlas loaded into the tiers, layout with wrapping, newlines, alignment, kerning and full Unicode, glyph entities or a batched text primitive, verified on GPU
Render interpolation between fixed ticks (smooth motion at 120/144 Hz), a configurable timestep and a camera-update point between simulation and render
Camera follow/bounds/shake/rotation helpers, screen-to-world conversion, a screen-space HUD layer, extra cameras/viewports and render-to-texture
Camera sync and texture loading in Mode A, or Mode A removed from the 'auto' default
Particles with textures, additive blending, bursts, emitter shapes and layering inside the scene (depth/sorted with sprites, optionally lit)
Working tonemapping/post-processing controls, background colour, and a supported custom post-effect API
Device-lost recovery (retained textures, renderer rebuild under a live engine)
A verified KTX2/Basis production texture path (real assets on BC7 and ASTC GPUs, mips, size checks with errors)
Normal-mapped 2D lighting, light on text and particles, and a full-resolution light-buffer option
A WebGL 2 fallback or at least a loud failure when WebGPU is missing; a Firefox GPU verification pass
surveys.summary: After the round the renderer is a strong, GPU-verified core but not yet a content pipeline for a complete 2D game. Ready or close to it: GPU-driven culling and indirect draws, 2D depth, a deterministic GPU transparent sort (up to 100 000, oracle-checked on the M2 and an AMD iGPU), five of the six primitives (MSDF text excepted), bloom and selection outlines, and, after step 8, a 2D lighting system unusually complete for the web (point, spot, directional, global and sprite-cookie lights, soft SDF shadows, light layers, a fixed draw order). Two blockers stand between it and a shippable platformer or action-adventure. First, the texture model: every image is one whole square layer of at most 512 px, quads have no UV sub-rectangle (so no atlases or sprite sheets), each array holds 255 images and nothing is ever unloaded, so a multi-level game's art does not fit. Second, mirrored sprites (scale(-1, 1)) are back-face culled and vanish; the fix is a few lines and is recorded, but nothing schedules it. Around them sit majors that every such game hits: no per-sprite tint, opacity or visibility; no text path (TextManager is a stub, MSDF has never been checked on a GPU); no mipmaps, nearest sampling or FXAA switch (pixel art and zoom-out shimmer); no animation, tween or tilemap layer; motion stepped at the 60 Hz tick with no interpolation (judder at 120/144 Hz, a one-update lag for a follow camera); minimal untextured particles drawn on top of everything; no device-lost recovery; and Mode A, the 'auto' default on Chrome and Electron, has no textures and no camera. The remaining steps fix none of these. Step 8 adds sprite lights and upright textured images, 8c may pad the SDF, step 10 renders Mode A's empty world and forwards device loss, and step 9 documents and re-verifies in Chrome and Safari. Realistically, the engine supports a Mode B prototype or vertical slice with a DOM HUD and text, a few hundred textures and no sprite flipping, or a local cullMode patch. A complete game first needs an engine-side content layer: quad UV rects, texture unloading, tint and alpha, mirroring, mips and a sampler choice, animation and tilemap support, and a text path, plus render interpolation.

issues.issue: There is no working production build. `npm run build` (tsc + vite build) fails with the repo's config: Vite bundles workers as IIFE by default, both workers reach dynamic import() calls, and Rollup refuses to split IIFE output into chunks. No production bundle (`__DEV__` false, minified worker chunks, WASM and transcoder assets) has ever been built and run. The engine is also not a package: ts/package.json is private and has no exports or library build, so a game imports the TS source and has to reproduce the Vite setup (`?raw` WGSL, `new URL(…, import.meta.url)` workers). The WASM flavour is a hardcoded import path, so the physics build in ts/wasm-physics is never loaded.
issues.gameImpact: The first deploy fails at build time. After the config is fixed, the production path runs for the first time in front of players. A physics game cannot select its WASM without editing engine source.

issues.issue: Fault handling contradicts the masterplan's 'the application never dies, it degrades'. In Mode B, Hyperion.create hangs forever if the engine worker posts an error: the ready promise has no reject. No Worker in A or B has an onerror handler, so a worker or WASM load failure also hangs. A Mode A failure after transferControlToOffscreen leaves a canvas that the B and C fallback cannot use; the renderer error is swallowed and the engine reports Mode B over a blank canvas. A throw in render() or a WASM trap stops the main loop for good because tickFn is not isolated; the Mode A render loop is the same. There is no uncapturederror handler and no panic hook. The supervisor only warns, and onModeChange is never called.
issues.gameImpact: A deploy mistake leaves players on an endless loading screen instead of a Mode C fallback: a wrong .wasm MIME type, a CSP without wasm-unsafe-eval or worker-src, a 404 on a worker chunk. A single runtime exception freezes the game and gives the app no callback to report it or save.
issues.evidence: worker-bridge.ts:117-120 (resolve only), :131-132 (an 'error' message is only logged). No onerror or 'error' listener in ts/src (grep). worker-bridge.ts:223; hyperion.ts:195-200, :211-216; docs/handoff/2026-09-29-mac-m2-handoff.md:502, :705. game-loop.ts:166-176: tickFn at :169 is outside any try, and rAF is re-armed at :176 only if it returns. render-worker.ts:70-80; engine-worker.ts:68-89. worker-bridge.ts:101-107, :215-221 and supervisor.ts:14-17, :33-46 (warn only). types.ts:14. Masterplan :57, :72, :124, :211 ('[x] Supervisor … degrada A→B→C').
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: Wrap Hyperion.create in an app-side timeout and retry with preferredMode 'C' on a new canvas element. Add window 'error' and 'unhandledrejection' handlers. Never force 'A'.

issues.issue: Device loss is reported but never recovered. In Modes B and C the renderer logs it and calls onDeviceLost(message); in Mode A it is only logged in the worker. Nothing rebuilds the device, the pipelines or the textures. onDeviceLost also fires on every engine.destroy(), because renderer.destroy() destroys the device and the handler does not check info.reason ('destroyed').
issues.gameImpact: A GPU reset, driver update, GPU-process crash or mobile background eviction freezes the picture while the simulation keeps running. The app must recover on its own by destroying and recreating Hyperion. That loses the ECS world (production builds have no snapshot), reloads every texture, and in Mode A needs a new <canvas> element. An app that recreates the engine from onDeviceLost will also loop after its own destroy().
issues.evidence: renderer.ts:270-273 (no reason check), :1200 (device.destroy(), reached from hyperion.ts:648). render-worker.ts:37; worker-bridge.ts:223. crates/hyperion-core/src/lib.rs:808-835 (snapshot and reset only with feature dev-tools). The only test checks that the callback is stored: hyperion.test.ts:422-426. masterplan:232, :247 mark 'device.lost recovery trasparente' as done.
issues.roundFix: Partly. Step 10 forwards Mode A's loss to config.onDeviceLost and corrects masterplan lines 232 and 247 (round plan:81-82, :108). Recovery and filtering out 'destroyed': no step.
issues.workaround: Ignore an onDeviceLost call that follows your own destroy(). Otherwise persist game state, then reload the page or recreate the engine on a new canvas and restore from the save.

issues.issue: Mobile is unverified and the input model is desktop-only. InputManager tracks a single pointer with no pointerId, handles no pointercancel, sets no touch-action, and has no gamepad support. Android Chrome lands in Mode A through the UA guess. The ASTC texture path that most mobile GPUs need has never run, and no mobile device appears in any measurement.
issues.gameImpact: A touch control scheme (virtual stick plus buttons) cannot read two fingers. When a browser gesture cancels a touch, isPointerDown(0) stays true. Without touch-action:none the page pans and zooms. Mobile performance (the masterplan targets 20k entities at 60 fps) is unknown.
issues.evidence: input-manager.ts:15-20, :30-37, :84-98, :197-210, :250-267. No getGamepads, pointercancel or touch-action in ts/src (grep). capabilities.ts:34. docs/handoff/2026-09-29-mac-m2-handoff.md:1060 (M11 ASTC skipped). Round plan:75: layer 0 on ASTC decodes to the error colour, 'from the spec, not measured'. Masterplan :41, :1035-1036, :1041-1050.
issues.roundFix: No. The WebKit audio step after the round adds a first-gesture unlock hook, which helps iOS audio only.
issues.workaround: Write an app-side pointer layer on the canvas: a pointerId map, pointercancel, setPointerCapture, CSS touch-action:none. Poll navigator.getGamepads() in a preTick hook. Force Mode B or C on Android.

issues.issue: Desktop embedding exists only as deployment-guide prose, and that prose contradicts the engine. No Electron, Tauri or WebView2 template, build or test exists. The guide says SharedArrayBuffer is available without headers, but the engine requires crossOriginIsolated === true, which the guide's `win.loadFile` recipe (a file:// page) does not establish. Where isolation does hold, Electron and WebView2 get Mode A (their UAs contain 'Chrome/' or 'Edg/'), the mode without textures and the masterplan's 'always Mode A'. Tauri on macOS and Linux (WebKit UA) never gets Mode A. The Tauri JSON uses v1 keys while describing v2, and the guide itself doubts WebGPU in macOS WKWebView. A blank window follows, since there is no fallback.
issues.gameImpact: The 'desktop app' target is unproven. Following the guide gives Mode C (no isolation) or the texture-less Mode A (isolation), plus first-time integration work: asset base path, WebGPU switches per OS, a custom protocol serving COOP/COEP.
issues.evidence: deployment-guide.md:276-308, :312-344 (v1 keys at :318-337 against 'Tauri v2' at :342; WKWebView at :343). capabilities.ts:19-25, :33-36; ring-buffer.ts:366. git ls-files has no electron, tauri or webview file. Masterplan :45, :969, :1037. vite.config.ts sets no `base`, and Vite's default emits root-absolute /assets/ URLs that do not resolve under file:// (general Vite behaviour).
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: Electron: serve the build through a privileged custom protocol that adds COOP/COEP, or accept Mode C. Force 'B' or 'C', set Vite `base: './'`, and verify WebGPU on each OS before committing.

issues.issue: Firefox has never been run. The Phase 17 research says it exposes no optional WebGPU features. Without 'indirect-first-instance', every indirect draw with a non-zero firstInstance is a silent no-op. Among opaque entities only tier-0 quads would then draw, and only they would cast shadows or get outlines. That leaves out opaque lines, MSDF text, beziers, gradients, box shadows, and quads textured from tiers 1-3 or overflow.
issues.gameImpact: On Firefox (Mode B when isolated) most of a game's opaque art could vanish, with a single console warning. Firefox has no WebGPU at all on Linux, Android and macOS Intel. Unverified: inferred from code plus the design's research.
issues.evidence: capabilities.ts:31-32, :227 (the feature is requested only if offered), :246-251 (the warning's text). ts/src/shaders/cull.wgsl:99-104 (bucket 1 for tier > 0 or overflow). docs/plans/2026-08-04-phase17-lighting-2d-design.md:178-183, :1066. docs/plans/2026-09-26-cull-temporal-firstinstance-brief.md:11, :32. Firefox coverage so far is the naga CLI only (docs/plans/2026-09-27-transparent-sort-uber-design.md:658, :706).
issues.roundFix: No. Step 9's GPU legs are Chrome and Safari on the Mac; Fedora Chrome is non-blocking (round plan:109).
issues.workaround: Mark sprites .transparent() so they go through the sorted uber draw (firstInstance 0), at the cost of the sort and of depth writes; or do not support Firefox.

issues.issue: Verification covers two machines: one Mac (Chrome 154/155 and Safari 27, Modes B, C, A) and one Linux box running Chrome with WebGPU flags. Windows on D3D12, where most players are, has never run the engine. Neither have Edge, Android, iOS, Firefox or any desktop shell. On Linux, the engine's own diagnostic says stock Chrome needs flags for a hardware adapter.
issues.gameImpact: Backend- and driver-specific defects would be found by players. Past examples: the subgroup cull that was wrong on AMD, the BC7 tier growth that failed on Metal (M10). Linux players may get no adapter or a software one.
issues.evidence: docs/plans/assets/2026-09-29-mac-m2/README.md:29-46, :344-411. No Windows or D3D12 run in docs/ (grep). capabilities.ts:193-198. Round plan:109 (step 9: Mac Chrome B/C/A, Safari B/C/A, Fedora B/C at the next session, non-blocking).
issues.roundFix: Partly: step 9 re-verifies Chrome and Safari on the Mac, plus Fedora B/C (non-blocking), at the end state. Nothing for Windows, mobile or Firefox.
issues.workaround: Run the harness (?mode=B and ?mode=C) on every target platform before committing to it.

issues.issue: Modes A and B have no tick backpressure and no partial upload. The main thread posts one tick per requestAnimationFrame whether or not the worker has finished the last one. On every tick message, even one that runs no fixed tick, the worker copies all SoA columns into fresh ArrayBuffers, and Mode A copies them again on the main thread. The scatter (dirty-only) upload exists only in Mode C. The main thread also renders the state of an earlier tick, which adds at least one frame of latency.
issues.gameImpact: When one worker tick costs more than a display frame (8.3 ms at 120 Hz, 4.2 ms at 240 Hz; heavy physics or slow CPUs), tick messages pile up without bound. The displayed state and audio then drift further and further behind real time, while garbage grows with the entity count. Inferred from code; not measured at game scale.
issues.evidence: game-loop.ts:166-169; worker-bridge.ts:174-177 (B), :342-345 (A). tick-sequencer.ts:9-13 ('a lagging worker handles an older tick'). engine-worker.ts:68-89 (capture after every message); worker-render-state.ts:135-155 (new arrays every tick), :211-214 (no staging). worker-bridge.ts:277-301 (Mode A's second copy). Mode C reads staging at worker-bridge.ts:480-500. Round plan:124 (the scatter upload runs only in Mode C).
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: Use Mode C, or keep the worker's per-tick cost well below the display interval. An app cannot throttle the bridge without engine changes.

issues.issue: Rendering shows the last fixed 60 Hz tick with no interpolation, and the fixed step cannot be changed. On 120, 144, 165 and 240 Hz displays motion advances in 1/60 s steps, with uneven cadence whenever the refresh rate is not a multiple of 60.
issues.gameImpact: Visible judder while scrolling and in fast action on gaming monitors and 120 Hz Macs and phones; Chrome on the test M2 runs rAF at 120 Hz. Inferred from code; not measured. This may overlap with a game-loop dimension.
issues.evidence: crates/hyperion-core/src/engine.rs:19 (FIXED_DT, the constant 1/60), :207-216, :407-410 (interpolation_alpha() never exported or called; grep). types.ts:12 (fixedTimestep has no consumer). README:346.
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: Interpolate app-driven visuals such as the camera on the app side. Sprites driven by the ECS cannot be interpolated without engine work.

issues.issue: Mode and platform diagnostics are silent, part of the config surface does nothing, and the guide has errors. logCapabilities, which holds the COOP/COEP warning, is never called, and the chosen mode is never logged, although PROJECT_ARCHITECTURE.md promises 'a clear warning'. Seven HyperionConfig fields have no consumer: onModeChange, onOverflow, commandBufferSize, backpressure, fixedTimestep, textureStreaming and streamingBudgetBytesPerFrame. The guide's Mode B condition is wrong (B also needs navigator.gpu) and so is its Node version (18+, against the pinned ^24).
issues.gameImpact: A team that gets the headers wrong silently lands in Mode C or A and only finds out through engine.mode. Options it sets have no effect.
issues.evidence: capabilities.ts:57-76 (no caller; hyperion.ts:151 calls only detectCapabilities). PROJECT_ARCHITECTURE.md:130. deployment-guide.md:527-535 against capabilities.ts:51; deployment-guide.md:52 against ts/package.json engines. types.ts:9-22, with no consumer outside types.ts (grep). worker-bridge.ts:12 (ring buffer size hardcoded at 64 KB).
issues.roundFix: Partly: step 9 fixes CLAUDE.md drift, including the Mode B condition (round plan:180). The deployment guide and PROJECT_ARCHITECTURE.md are not in the §5 list (round plan:219-244), and no step covers the dead options.

issues.issue: Hosting guidance stops at first-party hosts. Portals and itch.io-style iframes are not covered; there a cross-origin isolated page is normally unavailable (a general platform fact, not checked in the repo), which means Mode C. The Mode C path without isolation (a plain ArrayBuffer ring buffer) has never run in a GPU session. The guide does cover two side effects of the headers: COEP require-corp blocks third-party scripts and assets that lack CORP or CORS, and COOP same-origin cuts window.opener for popups.
issues.gameImpact: Portal builds run single-threaded on an unverified path. A build with COOP/COEP can break ad, analytics or portal SDKs and OAuth or payment popups.
issues.evidence: deployment-guide.md:89-101, :119-433, :472 (the only mention of iframes). ring-buffer.ts:364-370. .claude/skills/gpu-check/scripts/gpu-infra.sh:334. vite.config.ts:4-15.
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: Build portal versions with preferredMode 'C' and smoke-test them on a host without the headers.

issues.issue: Canvas size and device-pixel ratio are left to the app in Modes B and C; only Mode A's init applies devicePixelRatio, and nothing watches for resize or DPR changes. engine.picking.hitTest divides by the canvas backing-store size, while InputManager reports CSS pixels.
issues.gameImpact: On DPR-2 and DPR-3 screens (Macs, phones), hitTest(input.pointerX, input.pointerY) misses unless the app scales the coordinates. If the app never calls resize(), B and C keep a blurry 300×150 backing store.
issues.evidence: worker-bridge.ts:325-331; hyperion.ts:614-626, :388-401 (canvas.width/height at :395-398); input-manager.ts:59-67, :250-253 (offsetX/offsetY). No ResizeObserver; devicePixelRatio only at main.ts:82 and worker-bridge.ts:325 (grep). The harness's 'Hit testing' check only calls hitTest(0,0) (demo/input.ts:85-99).
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: Call resize() with clientWidth×dpr on every resize and DPR change (as main.ts:81-88 does), and multiply pointer coordinates by devicePixelRatio before hitTest.

issues.issue: GPU buffers are always sized for MAX_GPU_ENTITIES (100 000), whatever maxEntities says: about 25-27 MB before any canvas-sized texture. The lit backend honours only shadowSteps: bufferScale stays at 0.5 and sdfOversize is ignored.
issues.gameImpact: Low-memory mobile GPUs pay for 100k rows. On weak GPUs the only ways to cut lighting cost are fewer shadow steps or a smaller backing store. Measured lighting cost at 1080p: about 2.3 ms on an AMD iGPU and about 4 ms on the M2.
issues.evidence: renderer.ts:291-364 (every size from MAX_GPU_ENTITIES; visible-indices alone is 11.2 MB at :306-309). types.ts:78, :115-121. render/lighting-backend.ts:42-45; lighting-api.ts:33, :220-221. CLAUDE.md phase rows 17-D and M9.
issues.roundFix: Partly: step 8c decides the SDF padding, sdfOversize (round plan:107). Buffer sizing: no step.
issues.workaround: Lower the canvas backing-store resolution and shadowSteps on weak devices.

surveys.afterRound: After the round (steps 8, 8b, 8c, 10, 9 and the WebKit audio step) the picture for modes and platforms barely moves. Step 10 gives Mode A two things: an empty world now renders, and a device loss reaches config.onDeviceLost. Every other Mode A gap stays. Textures remain excluded, as a declared limitation of step 8. No step adds camera sync, particles, bloom/outlines, selection, overlays, positionImmediate or the scatter upload. Auto-selection still picks Mode A on any cross-origin isolated Chromium page, so a game must keep forcing 'B' or 'C'. Step 8b wires PhysicsAPI to the WASM. That is straightforward in Mode C; for Modes A and B the shape is still open (async, a snapshot one tick old, or Mode C only), and so is how an app gets the physics WASM build. Step 10 removes the masterplan's claim of transparent device-lost recovery, but builds no recovery. Step 9 re-verifies Chrome and Safari on the Mac in B, C and A, with Fedora B/C non-blocking. Its gate is preflight --full, which still never builds the production bundle. The WebKit audio step makes suspend() resolve before the first gesture and adds audio.state and a first-gesture unlock hook, which helps Safari and iOS. Untouched by any step: the failing vite build, the missing WebGL fallback, the fragile boot and runtime fault handling, tick backpressure in A/B, the desktop-only input model, verification on Windows, Firefox, mobile and desktop shells, and render interpolation. Net result: a desktop web game in Chrome, Edge or Safari, forced into Mode B or C with a hand-fixed build config and WebGPU-only reach, is feasible. Mobile and desktop-app shipping remain experimental.
missingForCompleteGame: A default mode selection that never lands in a mode without textures and camera, or a Mode A with texture loading, camera sync, particles, bloom/outlines, selection, overlays and immediate mode in the render worker
A production build that works and has been validated: worker.format 'es' or equivalent, a packaged library entry instead of importing the TS source, and a supported way to select the physics WASM
A WebGL 2 fallback renderer, or at minimum an explicit 'no renderer' signal or event and a documented unsupported-browser path
Device-lost recovery (recreate device, pipelines and texture tiers), or at least ignoring the 'destroyed' reason plus a production save/restore path for the ECS world

Robust boot and runtime fault handling: worker errors and load failures that reject and fall back to Mode C, Worker onerror handlers, an A→B fallback that keeps the canvas usable, isolation of tick and render exceptions, uncapturederror reporting, a supervisor that actually restarts or degrades, and an onModeChange that fires
Tick backpressure (an in-flight cap) and partial scatter uploads in Modes A and B
Mobile input: multi-touch with pointerId, pointercancel and pointer capture, touch-action handling; plus Gamepad API support and key release on blur (shared with the input dimension)
Verified mobile targets (Android Chrome, iOS Safari), including the ASTC path and measured frame budgets per mode
Desktop shell templates (Electron, Tauri, WebView2) with cross-origin isolation, file/asset loading and WebGPU switches, each verified
GPU verification runs on Windows (D3D12), Edge and Firefox
Render interpolation, or a configurable fixed step, for displays above 60 Hz
Hosting guidance for game portals and iframes, and a GPU-verified run of Mode C without cross-origin isolation
Engine-handled HiDPI and resize, with consistent pixel units between input and picking
surveys.summary: Hyperion has three execution modes, but only B and C can run a real game. Mode selection is driven by the browser's UA string. Behind the COOP/COEP headers that the deployment guide prescribes, every Chromium browser picks Mode A: Chrome and Edge on desktop and Android, Electron and WebView2. Chrome on macOS was measured picking A. Mode A cannot load textures (loadTexture throws), and its render-worker camera never follows engine.cam. It also has no particles, bloom, outlines, selection, plugin overlays, immediate mode or profiling. Safari and Firefox pick B. Pages that are not cross-origin isolated (plain hosts, portal iframes) get C, which is in fact the most complete mode. The engine itself never logs the mode or the missing headers. An app can and must force the mode with preferredMode, as the harness does with 'B'. A game shipped today with default settings on Chrome would not even build: `vite build` fails with the repo's config, because workers are bundled as IIFE while they contain dynamic imports. Once the config is fixed, a host with the headers gives Mode A: untextured shapes and lighting at a fixed view, no sprites, no text, no scrolling. A host without them gives Mode C: everything works, single-threaded and unmeasured at game scale. There is no WebGL fallback: without WebGPU (about 15% of users per the design's caniuse figure) the canvas stays black with no signal to the app. Device loss is only notified: in Modes B and C now, in A after step 10. It is never recovered, and the callback also fires on every destroy(). Fault handling is fragile: a worker failure hangs Hyperion.create in Mode B, a failed Mode A leaves a blank canvas, and one exception stops the loop for good. Verified so far: Chrome 154/155 and Safari 27 on a single Apple M2 Pro (B, C and A), plus Chrome with flags on one Linux box. Windows, Edge, Firefox, Android, iOS and the desktop shells have never run. Firefox may lack 'indirect-first-instance', in which case most opaque draws vanish. Input is single-pointer, with no pointercancel, no touch-action and no gamepad. Electron and Tauri exist only as guide prose that contradicts the engine's own isolation and UA checks. Modes A and B also have no tick backpressure, and nothing interpolates on displays above 60 Hz. The round changes little here: step 10 (empty world and device-lost forwarding in A), 8b (physics wiring, with the A/B shape undecided), step 9 (re-verification on Mac Chrome and Safari) and the WebKit audio step. Readiness for a complete 2D game after the round: possible as a desktop-web game in Chrome, Edge or Safari, forced into Mode B or C, with an app-side build fix and WebGPU-only reach. Mobile, Firefox, Windows confidence and the desktop app remain experimental.

issues.issue: No sprite-sheet path. A quad always samples its whole texture layer, with no UV or frame rect and no per-sprite tint or opacity. Texture capacity is per session, square and at most 512 px, and nothing can be unloaded.
issues.gameImpact: Sprite animation needs one loaded texture per frame. On a BC7/ASTC desktop every PNG/JPEG goes to the rgba8 overflow arrays: 4 × 255 = 1020 images for the whole session (KTX2 can add the primary arrays). Every image is squashed into a 64/128/256/512 square, and nothing can be freed between levels. A multi-level game with animated characters, tilesets and backgrounds exceeds this. Hit flashes, fade-outs and damage tints have no control.
issues.evidence: quad.wgsl:5-7, :11-13; prim-params-schema.ts:32 ('Quad has no schema'); prelude.wgsl:191-198 (whole-layer sample); shaders read only renderMeta word 1 (cull.wgsl:93, light-accum.wgsl:131, line.wgsl:81), so MeshHandle is inert; texture-manager.ts:5, 7; hyperion.ts:545-561; no unload method in texture-manager.ts
issues.roundFix: No. Step 8 only makes tier images upright (prelude.wgsl:196). Its plan lists texture unloading and tier mips as out of scope (docs/plans/2026-10-14-step8-sprite-light-plan.md:48), and no later step covers UV rects, tint or unloading.
issues.workaround: Write a custom sprite-batch pass with the plugin API (ctx.rendering.addPass and ctx.gpu, plugin-context.ts:113-120), with its own atlas, camera, depth and lighting handling. That is a large job. The alternative is one PNG per frame within the cap, re-creating the engine between chapters.

issues.issue: Mirrored sprites disappear. scale(-1, 1), the standard 2D way to make a character face left, reverses the triangle winding, and every entity pipeline culls back faces.
issues.gameImpact: A character, enemy or projectile flipped to face left is not drawn, casts no shadow and gets no outline. Culling still counts it and picking still hits it.
issues.evidence: forward-pass.ts:271, 285; occluder-seed-stage.ts:96; selection-seed-pass.ts:107 (cullMode 'back'; no frontFace override anywhere); a det<0 model matrix in unitQuadVertex (prelude.wgsl:142-145) reverses the screen winding; recorded at round plan:72 and step-8 plan:48
issues.roundFix: No. Step 8 explicitly leaves it (round plan:72). The step-8 plan records the candidate fix (cullMode 'none' in the four pipeline families) as 'da decidere col proprietario', and no step owns it.
issues.workaround: Load a pre-mirrored copy of every directional texture. This doubles texture use and makes gameplay-1 worse. A y-flipped camera is no escape: it mirrors every quad and culls the whole scene.

issues.issue: Physics is unreachable from a game: PhysicsAPI is never connected to the WASM, and no bridge can load the physics build.
issues.gameImpact: onCollisionStart/End, onSensorEnter/Exit and onContactForce never fire. raycast returns null, queryAABB/queryCircle return [] and isGrounded is always false, with no warning. Hyperion.create always loads ts/wasm, built without physics-2d, so bodies and colliders are not even simulated.
issues.evidence: physics-api.ts:130-132 (_init) has no caller; only hyperion.ts:124 (_initProducer) touches the API; physics-api.ts:242, 282, 296, 304, 175, 193; engine-worker.ts:41 and worker-bridge.ts:384 (hard-coded ../wasm/hyperion_core.js); ts/package.json:9 vs :12; physics-api.test.ts covers only the no-WASM path; no physics in ts/src/demo
issues.roundFix: Yes, step 8b (round plan:106). It brings wiring in every mode, a bridge protocol for events and queries in Modes A/B, a way for apps to get the physics build, and possibly the collider-generation fix. Its exit criteria are tests per mode and a harness check on the physics build. Still open: whether Mode A/B queries are async, synchronous on a one-tick-old snapshot, or Mode C only.
issues.workaround: None through the public API today. A forked Mode C bridge could load ts/wasm-physics and call physicsApi._init itself.

issues.issue: Physics units and axis convention do not match the renderer, and they cannot be configured from TS.
issues.gameImpact: With the defaults, a dynamic body accelerates at 980 units/s² toward +y, which is up on screen, in a view 20 units tall. Rapier's tolerances assume 100 units per metre. A character controller's 'up' (-gravity) points down the screen, so ground detection is inverted unless overridden.
issues.evidence: physics.rs:298-307 (gravity (0, 980) 'down in pixel coordinates', length_unit 100); physics.rs:286-293 (up = -normalize(gravity)); camera.ts:240 (bottom -hh, top +hh: y-up); entity-handle.ts:107 ('the world is y-up'); hyperion.ts:617 (20-unit view); lib.rs:567-577 (engine_physics_configure) has no TS caller; the Rust tests set gravity directly (tests/verify_physics.rs:339)
issues.roundFix: No. Step 8b's stated scope (round plan:106) is wiring, the A/B protocol, build delivery and the collider-generation fix. Gravity and units are not listed: a physics config option might come with 8b decision (2), but that is not guaranteed.
issues.workaround: Set gravityScale(-1) on every dynamic body and characterUp(0, 1) on every controller. Pick a world scale where 100 units is about 1 m (setOrthographic in pixel-like units, re-applied after every resize()).

issues.issue: Platformer and action body controls are missing: no velocity set or get, no rotation lock, no one-way platforms, only three collider shapes, and unfiltered raycasts. CCD, torque, angular damping and body/collider removal are not public.
issues.gameImpact: Jumps and knockback need velocity changes, but only impulses are available and the body's mass is unknown in TS. A dynamic player capsule tips over. One-way platforms are impossible. Tilemaps need a box per tile (no polygon, segment, polyline or heightfield). A ray cast from the player hits the player's own collider and every sensor. Fast bullets tunnel because CCD has no public setter. Rotating kinematic platforms rotate only by teleport.
issues.evidence: command_processor.rs:763 (SetVelocity writes only the ECS Velocity); systems.rs:75-80 (velocity systems skip PhysicsControlled); no SetVelocity arm in physics_commands.rs; physics.rs:9-15 (no lock flags); no PhysicsHooks or one-way code in crates (git grep: 0); physics.rs:801-822 (ball/cuboid/capsule only); physics.rs:381-387 (QueryFilter::default(), solid ray); backpressure.ts:485-528 (destroyRigidBody, destroyCollider, setAngularDamping, setCCDEnabled, applyTorque) have no EntityHandle or RawAPI method; physics.rs:664-676 (kinematic sync is translation only)
issues.roundFix: No. 8b wires the existing API, and none of these items is in any step.
issues.workaround: Tune impulses by trial instead of setting velocity. Call (handle as any)._producer.setCCDEnabled(...), as prefab/registry.ts:132 already does for primParams. Use a box per tile, start rays outside the player's collider, and use a kinematic body with the character controller for the player.

issues.issue: The default mode on Chromium and Electron, Mode A, cannot run a typical game: the camera never moves, textures do not load and particles are unavailable.
issues.gameImpact: preferredMode 'auto' picks Mode A on every cross-origin-isolated Chromium page, including Chrome, Edge, Electron and WebView2. There the render worker draws with its own camera fixed at the origin, so a scrolling level is impossible. loadTexture throws, createParticleEmitter returns null and selection is null. Picking uses the main-thread camera and a stale canvas size.
issues.evidence: types.ts:128; capabilities.ts:33-36, 48-49 (isChromium = /Chrome\//); render-worker.ts:18, 41, 66, 73 (no camera message); hyperion.ts:564, 773-775, 847; demo/preferred-mode.ts:5-16 (the harness forces Mode B for this reason); docs/deployment-guide.md:531 (presents Mode A as the automatic choice)
issues.roundFix: Partly. Step 10 fixes only the empty world and forwards device loss to config.onDeviceLost in Mode A (round plan:108). Textures in Mode A are a declared limitation (round plan:70), and no step syncs the camera.
issues.workaround: Set preferredMode: 'B' (or 'C'), giving up the separate render worker.

issues.issue: There is no render interpolation and no fixed-rate gameplay hook. The image changes only on 60 Hz simulation ticks, while TS game logic runs once per display frame with variable, unclamped dt.
issues.gameImpact: Motion is uneven on 144/165 Hz monitors and 75/90/100 Hz displays, which alternate between two and three refreshes per tick. Gameplay code in hooks runs at a different rate from physics, must clamp dt itself after a tab switch, and cannot be deterministic. There is no slow motion or hit-stop (time scale).
issues.evidence: engine.rs:19 (const FIXED_DT); engine.rs:207-218 (whole ticks only); engine.rs:409-411 (interpolation_alpha, absent from the lib.rs exports); game-loop.ts:139-177 (one hook pass per RAF, raw dt at :146); types.ts:12, 127 (fixedTimestep never read)
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: None for bodies the engine moves. For TS-driven entities, run your own accumulator in a preTick hook and push positions every frame, losing the physics integration.

issues.issue: Input covers only the keyboard, one pointer and the wheel, and has correctness bugs. There is no gamepad, touch/multi-touch or action map. Keys stick when focus is lost, and auto-repeat re-fires key callbacks.
issues.gameImpact: The use case's gamepad and touch targets need a custom input layer. A key held during alt-tab stays down, so the character keeps running. A jump bound with onKey repeats while the key is held. A button released outside the canvas stays pressed. Once a DOM HUD element takes focus, the game stops receiving keys. Picking at the pointer is wrong on HiDPI screens unless the game multiplies by devicePixelRatio.
issues.evidence: input-manager.ts:205-210 (canvas listeners for keydown/keyup/pointermove/pointerdown/pointerup/wheel only); input-manager.ts:240-243 then :47-50 (no repeat check); input-manager.ts:15-20 (single pointer state, buttons keyed by button number); input-manager.ts:250-253 (CSS px offsetX/Y); git grep in ts/src for getGamepads, touch-action, pointercancel, pointerId, 'blur', visibilitychange and setPointerCapture: all 0; hyperion.ts:395-398 with camera.ts:283-284 (normalised by the backing store); the harness Input tab only calls hitTest(0, 0) (demo/input.ts:87)
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: Write an input layer on the Gamepad API and Pointer Events: window-level listeners, a blur reset, edge detection and an action map. Pass DPR-scaled coordinates to picking.hitTest.

issues.issue: There is no level lifecycle: no way to clear the world, no cascade destroy, a compact() that does nothing, no tilemap or level format, and no per-level asset release.
issues.gameImpact: Unloading a level means tracking and destroying every handle yourself. Destroying a parent leaves its children alive at their local offset from the world origin. Textures and audio buffers from past levels keep their slots. In a tile level, every tile counts against the 100 000 live-entity cap.
issues.evidence: no clear or despawnAll in hyperion.ts; lib.rs:808-817 (engine_reset, dev-tools only, no TS caller); command_processor.rs:405-419 (children orphaned); hyperion.ts:675-680 (compact calls a non-existent shrinkUnusedTiers through 'as any'; the lib.rs:423-441 exports are never called); hyperion.test.ts:412-419 (only checks that compact() does not throw); types.ts:78 (MAX_GPU_ENTITIES 100 000); git grep for tilemap/tileset: 0
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: Keep a per-level registry of handles and destroy children before parents (PrefabInstance.destroyAll does this for prefabs). Stream tile chunks in and out around the camera. Destroy and re-create the engine between chapters, which means a new GPU device and reloading every texture.

issues.issue: There is no production save/load. Snapshots are dev-tools only and unwired, and the engine exposes no state readback a game could build one from.
issues.gameImpact: A save system must keep the authoritative game state in TS and rebuild the world on load. Physics body positions can be read only by scanning SystemViews; velocities and angular state cannot be read at all, so a save made mid-air or on a moving platform cannot restore exact physics. The same rebuild is the only recovery from a GPU device loss.
issues.evidence: lib.rs:808-844 (#[cfg(feature = 'dev-tools')]); crates/hyperion-core/Cargo.toml:10; ts/package.json:9; no TS caller of engine_snapshot_* (git grep: 0); hyperion.ts:281-282 (debug is null in production); system-views.ts:9-17; renderer.ts:270-272 (device lost: a log line and the callback, no recovery; the 'recupero trasparente' of hyperion-masterplan.md:232, 247 is false)
issues.roundFix: No. Step 10 only forwards device loss in Mode A and corrects the masterplan lines (round plan:108).
issues.workaround: Save game-level data (player, inventory, level id, checkpoint) and respawn the level on load. Avoid saving in the middle of physics.

issues.issue: Audio is SFX-grade. There is no music streaming, no bus, no fade, no per-sound pause or end callback; pause() silences everything, and nothing unlocks audio on the first gesture today.
issues.gameImpact: Each music track is decoded whole into memory, minutes of stereo float PCM per track. There are no separate music/SFX/UI volumes and no crossfade between level themes. engine.pause() stops pause-menu music and UI clicks. In Chrome, a context created before a user gesture stays suspended until the game calls audio.resume() from one. On Safari, pausing before the first gesture hangs suspend().
issues.evidence: audio-manager.ts:33-37, :86-94; playback-engine.ts:26-27 (one master gain), :30-61; hyperion.ts:598-607; hyperion.ts:864, 912-915 (listener set to the camera every tick); git grep for MediaElementAudioSource/AudioWorklet/fade: 0; round plan:83-87, :213
issues.roundFix: Partly. The post-round audio step makes suspend() resolve on a never-started context, adds audio.state and a first-gesture unlock hook verified in Safari, and files a WebKit bug. Streaming, buses and fades are in no step.
issues.workaround: Play music through an HTMLAudioElement or Web Audio graph (or a library such as Howler) beside the engine. Call engine.audio.resume() right after engine.pause() when UI sounds must keep playing.

issues.issue: In-canvas text is unfinished, and there is no UI/HUD or localization layer.
issues.gameImpact: Score, health, dialogue, damage numbers and menus need one of two paths. One is an entity per glyph, through a pipeline never verified on GPU: TextManager never uploads the atlas, and layout is a single line with no wrap or kerning, in UTF-16 units. The other is a DOM overlay positioned by hand from world coordinates (there is no world-to-screen helper), which then takes keyboard focus from the canvas (gameplay-8). Localization (plural rules, CJK, RTL) is entirely the game's.
issues.evidence: text-manager.ts:19; text-layout.ts:26, 47; index.ts:18-19; demo/primitives.ts:293-294; prim-params-schema.ts:48-51 (atlas rect plus rgb, no alpha); camera-api.ts:29-55 (no projection helper); hyperion-masterplan.md:35
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: Build the HUD and menus in DOM/HTML (or a UI framework) over the canvas, with an app-side i18n library. Compute screen positions from engine.cam.viewProjection.

issues.issue: Game logic cannot live in the engine's ECS: there are no custom components or systems. TS systems see only render rows indexed by GPU slot, and there is no per-entity readback.
issues.gameImpact: Health, inventory, AI state and timers live in a separate TS object model keyed by entity id that the game must keep in sync. Finding where an entity is means scanning entityIds every frame (O(n)), one frame late in Modes A/B. There is no query by component, and none of this data is in snapshots.
issues.evidence: hyperion-masterplan.md:629-633; engine.rs:340-378; ring_buffer.rs:124, 304-315 (no plugin opcode range despite hyperion-masterplan.md:239); system-views.ts:9-17; entity-handle.ts (no getter); plugin-context.ts:60-80 (side tables not cleared on release; the facade emits 'entity:released' at hyperion.ts:873); event-bus.ts:3-33 (untyped); git grep for getPosition/getVelocity/idToSlot: 0
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: Keep a TS entity store (Map<id, GameObject>) updated in hooks, and build an id-to-slot index from views.entityIds once per frame.

issues.issue: There is no gameplay helper layer: no timers, tweens/easing, state machines or AI/pathfinding.
issues.gameImpact: The team writes or imports all of it. It runs in per-frame hooks with variable dt (gameplay-7).
issues.evidence: git grep over ts/src and crates/hyperion-core/src: every hit is a false positive; hyperion-masterplan.md:661 (logic plugins only as expected patterns)
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: JS libraries, or game code in hooks.

issues.issue: Prefabs are flat and defined only in code, and they cannot carry physics, lights, depth or transparency.
issues.gameImpact: An enemy prefab with a collider, a light and a z-order needs post-spawn code per instance. Nested rigs (weapon on hand on arm) cannot be templated, and there is no data-file loading for a level editor.

issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: A factory function per prefab that spawns the entities and then configures the handles.

issues.issue: Facade stubs and dead configuration fields look functional but do nothing.
issues.gameImpact: Teams tune options that are never read (fixedTimestep, commandBufferSize, backpressure, onOverflow, onModeChange, textureStreaming, streamingBudgetBytesPerFrame) and read memoryStats zeros. They get no error callback when a worker stalls or crashes.

issues.issue: The camera API is thin, and resize() discards the game's projection.
issues.gameImpact: Follow/lerp, shake, level bounds and world/screen conversion are game code. Calling resize() on a window resize snaps the view back to 20 units tall, and zoom drops a custom near/far.
issues.evidence: camera-api.ts:29-55; hyperion.ts:614-626; camera-api.ts:41-55
issues.roundFix: Only the zoom/near-far item is registered for step 9 (round plan:192); the rest, no.
issues.workaround: Re-apply setOrthographic after every resize(), and implement follow and shake in a preTick hook.

issues.issue: Collision events can name the wrong entity once a collider index is reused, because the generation is ignored.
issues.gameImpact: A Started/Stopped event attributed to a despawned entity's successor produces spurious trigger enters or exits (pickups, doors).
issues.evidence: physics.rs:471-474 (index only)
issues.roundFix: Undecided: step 8b decision (3) (round plan:106).
issues.workaround: Ignore sensor events for entities spawned in the current frame.

issues.issue: Determinism and replay tooling is dev-only and not wired to the facade.
issues.gameImpact: A shipped game gets no replays, ghosts, kill-cams or lockstep netcode, and physics is bit-exact only on one target.
issues.evidence: lib.rs:876-885; hyperion.ts:281-308; replay-player.ts:3-7; snapshot-manager.ts:6-10; crates/hyperion-core/tests/verify_determinism.rs
issues.roundFix: No.

issues.issue: There is no networking of any kind.
issues.gameImpact: Not needed for a single-player action-adventure or platformer. Any online feature needs a separate stack.
issues.evidence: git grep for WebSocket/RTCPeerConnection/WebTransport in ts/src: 0; docs/plans/2026-03-06-phase14b-loro-results.md (Loro FAIL, 664 KB gzipped); hyperion-masterplan.md:728
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: An app-side networking library feeding engine commands from hooks.

issues.issue: Mode A/B tick messages have no backpressure, and simulation state arrives at least a frame late.
issues.gameImpact: If a frame's simulation outgrows the frame budget, ticks queue up in the worker and input-to-screen latency grows without bound. Even when healthy, hooks read state one or more frames old.
issues.evidence: worker-bridge.ts:174-177, 342-345 (one postMessage per RAF regardless of the worker's progress); worker-bridge.ts:126-166 (latestRenderState replaced when tick-done arrives)
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: Use Mode C for latency-critical games and keep the per-frame simulation cost low.

issues.issue: The particle API offers continuous emitters only.
issues.gameImpact: An explosion or impact needs an emitter created and then destroyed on a timer (live particles vanish with it). There is no texture field and no burst, and createParticleEmitter returns null in Mode A.
issues.evidence: particle-types.ts:11-37; hyperion.ts:845-859
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: Pool emitters and destroy them after their maximum lifetime.

missingForCompleteGame: Sprite sheets: a per-entity UV/frame rect with an animation system on top, per-sprite tint/opacity, texture unloading, and images larger than 512 px or non-square (today a quad samples its whole layer, quad.wgsl:5-7)
Mirroring without culling (cullMode 'none' or winding-aware pipelines), so that scale(-1, 1) flips a sprite instead of hiding it
Gamepad, touch/multi-touch, an action map, pressed/released-this-frame edges, a focus-loss reset and window-level keyboard listening
Render interpolation between fixed ticks, a fixed-rate gameplay hook and a time scale

Physics configuration from TS (gravity, units) consistent with the y-up camera; velocity get/set, rotation lock, one-way platforms, polygon/segment/tilemap colliders, filtered scene queries and public CCD/torque; Mode A/B events and queries (step 8b)
A level lifecycle: clear world, cascade destroy, per-level asset release, a level/tilemap data format and a compact() that works
Per-entity state readback (position, rotation, velocity by id) and a production save/load
Music streaming, audio buses, fades/crossfade, per-sound pause/seek/onEnded, and a pause that keeps UI audio
A working text pipeline (atlas upload, multi-line layout, full Unicode) or supported DOM-overlay helpers (world-to-screen), UI widgets and localization
Mode A parity (camera sync, textures, particles), or a default that does not pick Mode A on Chromium/Electron
Gameplay helpers: timers, tweens, state machines, pathfinding (these can be game-side)
A consumable package and game-developer documentation: ts/package.json is private 0.1.0 with no main/exports, and there is no README or API guide

capabilities.feature: Consuming the engine source from a game's own Vite project

The WASM location cannot be overridden.

capabilities.evidence: ts/package.json:9-15 has build:wasm, :release (wasm-opt), :physics, :physics:dev and check:wasm-size (a 200 KB gzip gate). rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.97.1 plus wasm32. scripts/preflight.sh runs the Rust feature matrix, clippy, tsc and vitest locally. capabilities.feature: TypeScript types and in-code API reference (JSDoc)

capabilities.feature: User documentation (README, getting started, guides, API reference)
Examples, sample game or starter template

10 tabs of probe-based checks, with a JSON report (main.ts:124 ReportBuilder). It needs a real GPU browser (WebGPU has no headless adapter) and defaults to Mode B (demo/preferred-mode.ts:5-15). The Debug Tools tab checks only that the plugins install (demo/debug-tools.ts:46-121).

capabilities.evidence: ecs-inspector.ts:115 calls `engine.selection.selectedIds()`, but SelectionManager.selectedIds is a getter that returns an iterator (selection.ts:69). The first update with the panel open therefore throws. `engine.selection` is null in Mode A (hyperion.ts:773-775). It is not exported.

The plugin and DebugLinePass exist, and the lines travel through every bridge (worker-render-state.ts:158-159, worker-bridge.ts:540-543). They require a physics-debug WASM that nothing loads. The plugin is a no-op without a main-thread renderer (physics-debug.ts:53). The harness check only verifies that it installs.

capabilities.evidence: It works in every mode (profiler.ts:22-44), but shows only the main-thread requestAnimationFrame dt. Its entity count excludes RawAPI spawns (hyperion.ts:469-481). memoryStats returns zeros (hyperion.ts:455-461). There are no per-hook timings, and nothing measures the worker's tick time.

enableGpuProfiling, getGpuTimings and getGpuFrameTiming (hyperion.ts:717-767) work in Modes B and C on a device that has the feature, and return false or empty in Mode A. Chrome quantises timestamps without flags, and the entries are intervals rather than costs, both documented in the JSDoc. It was measured on the M2 and in Safari (docs/plans/assets/2026-09-29-mac-m2/README.md).

capabilities.feature: Replay, snapshot rewind and state hash

Only mock tests exist (replay-player.test.ts). The harness skips the state hash (demo/debug-tools.ts:123-128).

renderer.ts:1205-1269 has the accept handlers. Each source is validated by the GPU before it goes live (graph-requests.ts:200-237). This covers the engine's own shaders only: a game cannot add a primitive shader without changing the engine.

capabilities.evidence: hot-system.ts:23-50 keeps a shallow TS object across HMR. It does not keep ECS entities, and it does not unregister the old hook. Nothing in the repo uses it.

It scans one directory, non-recursively, for image files only (scanner.ts:54). PNG/JPEG sizes come from `require('image-size')` (scanner.ts:39) inside an ESM package (ts/package.json:5), and image-size is neither declared nor installed, so the sizes come out 0×0. The test mocks it and asserts no size (scanner.test.ts:29-46). The plugin emits only paths (codegen.ts), and the repo's own vite.config.ts does not use it.

The vendored transcoder glue is UMD/CommonJS: its footer assigns `module.exports` or calls AMD `define`. basis-transcoder.ts:85-87 imports it as an ES module default, and the glue locates its .wasm from document.currentScript. From the code, this should fail under Vite's ESM; it was not run. Step 8 found two more defects (step-8 plan :4482): a BC7/ASTC file on an rgba8 tier fails silently, and KTXorientation is never read.

Every image is resized to the 64-512 px square of its tier (texture-manager.ts:5, 684-693), so larger or non-square art is squashed without a warning. A tier array holds 255 textures. Quads have no sub-rect parameters ('Quad has no schema', prim-params-schema.ts). Loading throws in Mode A (hyperion.ts:564, 578). Step 8 makes every image upright (prelude.wgsl:188-197).
