issues.issue: The documented production build fails, and no validation runs it
issues.gameImpact: The web build cannot be produced with the documented command (CLAUDE.md:69, docs/deployment-guide.md:56-66). Even once it builds, the production bundle (`__DEV__` false, bundled workers, an emitted .wasm) has never been run on a GPU in any mode.
issues.evidence: ts/vite.config.ts:1-23 has no `worker` option, so workers use Vite's default iife format, which cannot code-split. The worker graphs use dynamic import: engine-worker.ts:41 imports the WASM glue, and render-worker.ts → renderer → texture-manager → basis-transcoder.ts:85-87 imports the transcoder. The 5b plan records that `npm --prefix ts run build` 'fallisce già su aa9ee92 (worker.format iife con code-splitting nei worker)' (docs/plans/2026-09-27-transparent-sort-uber-plan.md:9340). vite.config.ts is unchanged since 75fecc7. scripts/preflight.sh never runs `npm run build`, and no GPU session record mentions a production bundle. Not re-run here (read-only task).
issues.roundFix: Not in the round. The failure is recorded only in the 5b plan, not in round plan §2-§4, CLAUDE.md or step 9's list.
issues.workaround: Probably `worker: { format: 'es' }` in the Vite config, since the engine already creates module workers. This is unverified. Then run a GPU pass over the production bundle in Modes B and C.

issues.issue: No licence grant and no third-party notices
issues.gameImpact: A team that does not hold the copyright has no right to use or ship the engine. Every shipped build also owes the licence texts of what is compiled in. For the owner's own team this is a compliance chore; for anyone else it stops adoption. The fix is one file plus a manifest line.
issues.evidence: git ls-files has no LICENSE, COPYING or NOTICE. Cargo.toml:6-8 declares `license = "MIT"` under [workspace.package], but crates/hyperion-core/Cargo.toml:1-4 inherits only version and edition, so neither the crate nor the generated ts/wasm/package.json carries a licence. ts/package.json has no license field. ts/vendor/basis_transcoder.js and .wasm (Basis Universal, Apache-2.0, added in fb6eb08) contain no licence text (`grep -c license` returns 0) and record no version. The locked dependency closure is permissive (MIT, Apache-2.0, Zlib, Unlicense), but rapier2d 0.34, parry2d 0.29, nalgebra 0.35, simba and approx are Apache-2.0 only.
issues.roundFix: Not in the round. Round plan §2-§3 have no licensing item, and step 9 only refreshes docs and CLAUDE.md.
issues.workaround: The owner adds a LICENSE, `license.workspace = true` in the crate, a generated notices file (e.g. cargo-about) and the Basis Apache-2.0 text.

issues.issue: No installable or versioned distribution: a game has to vendor the source and build the WASM itself
issues.gameImpact: Setting up a game means a git submodule of the engine and a path import of ts/src/index.ts into a Vite project. That project must re-create the engine's own config: COOP/COEP headers, the `__DEV__` define, raw WGSL imports and module workers. Every dev machine and CI runner needs Rust 1.97.1, wasm-pack and binaryen. Each engine update is a source merge plus a WASM rebuild, and there is no version to pin. Non-Vite bundlers and a CDN-hosted .wasm are not supported.
issues.evidence:
- ts/package.json:2-5: private 0.1.0, with no main, exports, types or files; it is the only package.json in git.
- No `build.lib` in vite.config.ts, and no declaration emit in tsconfig.json.
- ts/wasm is gitignored (.gitignore:3).
- The WASM path is hard-coded (engine-worker.ts:41, worker-bridge.ts:384), and `default()` is always called without arguments (engine-worker.ts:42, worker-bridge.ts:390), so the URL comes from the glue (hyperion_core.js:562-568).
- renderer.ts has 22 `?raw` imports.
- No git tags.
issues.roundFix: None. No step touches packaging. The masterplan puts an npm scope for plugins after Phase 10 (§14.6) and lists framework and Electron/Tauri templates as long-term vision (§20, :969).
issues.workaround: A submodule plus a Vite alias, with a scripted `build:wasm:release` in the game's build, or commit the built WASM. Pin an engine commit.

issues.issue: No documentation for engine users, and the one user guide is stale
issues.gameImpact: A new team has to learn the engine from JSDoc, an agent instruction file and a verification harness. Mode policy, asset limits, physics builds and deployment pitfalls must be rediscovered by reading code, and the deployment guide misleads on Node, Tauri and diagnostics.
issues.roundFix: Partial and internal only. Step 9 refreshes CLAUDE.md and the stale docs listed in round plan §5, and step 10 corrects masterplan :232/:247. No step writes user documentation or examples.
issues.workaround: Read the JSDoc in hyperion.ts and entity-handle.ts and the harness sections, and write an internal getting-started guide.

issues.issue: Dev tools are half-wired, and most do nothing in Mode A
issues.gameImpact: A complex game needs an inspector and a free camera. The inspector throws on first use and could show only position and radius. In Mode A the debug camera, the bounds and physics overlays, GPU profiling and the probe are all absent. The harness cannot catch this, because its Debug Tools checks pass as soon as a plugin installs.
issues.evidence:
- ecs-inspector.ts:115 calls the getter `selectedIds` (selection.ts:69) as a method: TypeError on the first update. The loop removes the failing hook after 60 throws (game-loop.ts:16).
- `engine.selection` is null without a renderer (hyperion.ts:773-775).
- The WASM channel is a stub (ecs-inspector.ts:136).
- The debug camera moves only the main-thread camera (debug-camera.ts:54), while the Mode A render worker's camera is never synced (render-worker.ts:18, 41, 66).
- Both overlays return early without a renderer (bounds-visualizer.ts:93, physics-debug.ts:53).
- In Mode A GPU profiling returns false and the probe rejects (hyperion.ts:732-735, 317-319).
- debugCameraPlugin and ecsInspectorPlugin are not exported (index.ts).
- demo/debug-tools.ts:46-121 passes on 'plugin installed'.
issues.roundFix: None. Round plan §4 (:122) calls the inspector bug out of scope, and no step owns it. Mode A camera sync and the main-thread-only overlays are not part of step 10, which covers the empty world and device lost only.
issues.workaround: Develop in Mode B or C, patch the one-line inspector bug locally, read state from SystemViews, and use browser devtools for the rest.

issues.issue: An app cannot select the physics or dev-tools WASM build
issues.gameImpact: Today a physics game gets no collision events, raycasts or grounded state from the facade. The dev-tools features (state hash, snapshots, component inspection) need a hand-run wasm-pack into ts/wasm.
issues.evidence: Nothing imports ts/wasm-physics. The only dev-tools script writes into wasm-physics (ts/package.json:13). PhysicsAPI._init (physics-api.ts:130) has no caller: hyperion.ts:124 wires only the producer. stateHash resolves null without dev-tools (hyperion.ts:378-380, and the harness skips it at demo/debug-tools.ts:123-128).
issues.roundFix: Step 8b (round plan §3 row 8b) wires PhysicsAPI in every mode and decides how an app and the harness get the physics build: a config option, a build alias, or the harness on the physics build. A dev-tools variant and a runtime option for the WASM URL are not in its scope.
issues.workaround: Until 8b: build physics into ts/wasm by hand and call `_init` locally (Mode C only).

issues.issue: No supported way to test game code headlessly against the real engine, and no CI
issues.gameImpact: Gameplay regression tests (movement, physics, spawn/destroy churn, save/load) need home-made scaffolding around private seams. Rendering cannot be tested at all without a GPU browser. Nothing runs the engine's own suites on each change.
issues.evidence:
- Hyperion.create needs an HTMLCanvasElement (types.ts:111-114), navigator (capabilities.ts:17-45) and DOM input (hyperion.ts:220).
- The loop advances only through requestAnimationFrame (game-loop.ts:99, 176); there is no public step(dt).
- createDirectBridge's default loader fetches the .wasm by URL (worker-bridge.ts:384-391).
- createRingBuffer reads the `crossOriginIsolated` global (ring-buffer.ts:366), which Node does not define.
- The types that fromParts needs (EngineBridge, Renderer) are not exported.
- engine_init overwrites the static ENGINE with a raw write (lib.rs:30-35): one engine per JS realm, and creating another leaks the previous one.
- No TS test loads the real WASM.
- No .github/ or other CI.
issues.roundFix: None.
issues.workaround: Use fromParts with a custom loadWasm that passes `{ module_or_path: bytes }`, as scripts/determinism-cross-version.mjs:51-58 does. Stub `crossOriginIsolated` and requestAnimationFrame, as hyperion.test.ts:742-757 does. Run one engine per test worker. For visual tests, use engine.debug.probe on a GPU runner, and set up your own CI.

issues.issue: Failures are silent, hang, or stop the engine instead of being reported
issues.gameImpact: A misdeployed or stale .wasm, a NaN in game code, or one exception in a collision callback gives one of four results: a startup that never finishes, a blank canvas, entities that silently stop updating, or a game frozen for good. At most one console line appears, and there is no hook to recover.
issues.evidence:
- Mode B's ready() never rejects, because the worker's error is only logged (worker-bridge.ts:117-133, 184-186). Hyperion.create therefore awaits forever at hyperion.ts:193, with no fallback, and no Worker sets onerror.
- A failure to create the renderer is swallowed (hyperion.ts:212-216).
- If Mode A fails after `transferControlToOffscreen` (worker-bridge.ts:223), the fallback lands on a canvas that can no longer draw.
- The WASM counts rejected commands and dropped bytes (lib.rs:78-97), and an unknown opcode drops the rest of the batch (ring_buffer.rs:315-319). TS only declares those counters and never reads them (worker-bridge.ts:397-403), and there is no TS↔WASM protocol version check.
- NaN/Inf payloads are dropped without being counted (command_processor.rs:16-39).
- A throw inside tickFn (render, or the user collision callbacks dispatched inside it, physics-api.ts:256-277 via hyperion.ts:867) skips the requestAnimationFrame re-arm (game-loop.ts:166-176), after which start() is a no-op (game-loop.ts:88).
- With COOP/COEP missing, the engine runs in Mode C without a word.
- WorkerSupervisor only warns (worker-bridge.ts:101-106, marked 'TODO(Phase 5)').
- There is no uncapturederror handler.
issues.roundFix: Only step 10: a Mode A device loss will reach config.onDeviceLost (round plan §3 row 10). Step 8b wires the physics callbacks, but isolating them is not in its exit criteria.
issues.workaround: Wrap your own callbacks in try/catch, put a timeout around Hyperion.create, treat `engine.selection === null` as 'no renderer', and patch in a dev poll of the WASM counters.

issues.issue: Public options and methods that silently do nothing
issues.gameImpact: A team that sets a 120 Hz simulation, a larger command buffer, an overflow callback or texture streaming gets no effect and no warning. So does a team that relies on compact() or memoryStats in long sessions. The fixed tick rate is a Rust constant.
issues.roundFix: None. Step 9 lists only the opaque() comment (round plan §4 :191), and the tonemap stub stays a declared skip (§3 row 3).
issues.workaround: Do not rely on these options and methods. For a different tick rate, fork engine.rs.

issues.issue: The asset pipeline only generates texture paths, and the compressed-texture path has never run with a real asset
issues.gameImpact: Sprite sheets, tile sets, audio, fonts and levels get no build-time support. Art larger than 512 px, or non-square, is silently squashed into a 64-512 px square. KTX2/Basis, which mobile memory budgets and large atlases need, is unproven and probably fails when the transcoder loads.
issues.evidence:
- The scanner reads one directory, non-recursively, and only image files (scanner.ts:54).
- PNG/JPEG sizes come out 0×0: image-size is loaded with `require` (scanner.ts:39) inside an ESM package and is not installed.
- The generated module contains paths only, and the repo itself does not use the plugin.
- Images are resized to their tier square (texture-manager.ts:5, 684-693), and a quad cannot sample a sub-rect.
- No KTX2 asset exists (Mac README:330).
- The Basis glue is UMD/CommonJS but is imported as an ESM default (basis-transcoder.ts:85-87). From the code this should fail; it was not run.
- Step 8 found that a BC7/ASTC file on an rgba8 tier fails silently and that KTXorientation is never read (step-8 plan :4482).
issues.roundFix: None. Step 8 only makes tier images upright, and it explicitly leaves KTXorientation, the texture-manager fixes and textures in Mode A out of scope (step-8 plan :48).
issues.workaround: Keep art in PNG squares of 512 px or less (one texture per animation frame), and write your own manifest and loaders for audio, fonts and levels.

issues.issue: Behaviour changes from round to round with no versioning, changelog or deprecation path
issues.gameImpact: A game that updates the engine mid-production gets visual and semantic changes with no release notes. Recorded tapes, snapshots and authored scenes render differently. Code that compensated for an old behaviour breaks: for example, art pre-flipped to correct the old upside-down sampling now comes out inverted.
issues.roundFix: None, and step 8 itself adds one more visual breaking change. Masterplan principle 5 (:59) calls the API near-irreversible after the first external user, but defines no mechanism for that.
issues.workaround: Pin a commit, read CLAUDE.md gotchas and round plan §4 before each update, and re-record tapes and snapshots.

issues.issue: No editor or level-design tooling, and prefabs cannot describe a full game object
issues.gameImpact: A game with many levels needs authored data. The team must write its own level format and an importer (for Tiled or LDtk), and keep lights, bodies, colliders and depth in code.
issues.evidence: ts/src contains no scene serialization or importer. PrefabNode (prefab/types.ts:12-23) has no fields for lights, rigid bodies, colliders, depth or transparency, its children cannot nest, and its texture is a session-scoped number (types.ts:4). Masterplan §1.3 (:35) excludes a visual editor, the 'Hyperion Canvas' level editor (§18.1, :909) is not started, and §20 (:969) mentions a light editor only as long-term vision.
issues.roundFix: None.
issues.workaround: Tiled or LDtk, plus a custom loader that maps layers and objects to spawn(), light(), rigidBody() and collider() calls.

issues.issue: The default `preferredMode: 'auto'` picks Mode A on Chromium and desktop shells, where textures, camera control and the dev tools do not work
issues.gameImpact: The web build on Chrome/Edge lands in Mode A, and so does a desktop build on Electron or WebView2 once it is cross-origin isolated. There, loadTexture throws, the camera never scrolls, particles return null, and outlines and bloom throw: a sprite game cannot run. The error messages say 'no renderer available' without naming the mode or the fix. Browsers without WebGPU get no rendering at all, because there is no fallback.
issues.evidence:
- capabilities.ts:31-36 and :47-50 choose Mode A from a Chrome/Edge user-agent test.
- hyperion.ts:564/578 (textures throw), :847 (particles return null), :791/:813 (outlines and bloom throw), :211 (no WebGPU means no renderer).
- render-worker.ts:18/41/66 keeps an unsynced camera.
- The harness defaults to Mode B to avoid exactly this (demo/preferred-mode.ts:5-15).
- The WebGL 2 fallback sits in the masterplan §19 backlog.
issues.roundFix: Partial. Step 10 makes an empty Mode A world render and forwards device loss. Step 8 declares 'no textures in Mode A' a limitation (round plan §2 :70, §4 :217). No step owns camera sync or texture loading in Mode A.
issues.workaround: Always pass `preferredMode: 'B'` and serve COOP/COEP. In Electron and Tauri, set the headers in the protocol handler.

issues.issue: Replay, snapshot rewind and game-state HMR are libraries that nothing wires in
issues.gameImpact: Recording works. Reproducing a bug from a tape, stepping back in time, or keeping entity state across a code edit needs custom plumbing into a separately loaded dev-tools WASM.
issues.evidence: engine.debug records (hyperion.ts:288-308) but cannot replay. ReplayPlayer's callbacks (replay-player.ts:3-7) are not exposed by the facade, and it is only mock-tested. The snapshot exports are dev-tools only (lib.rs:819-835) and are never called from TS. createHotSystem (hot-system.ts:23-50) keeps only a TS object. Masterplan §13.8-13.10 still mark all of these 'non iniziata'.
issues.roundFix: None.
issues.workaround: Load a dev-tools WASM in a Mode C test page and drive ReplayPlayer and SnapshotManager there.

issues.issue: Dev and production switches must be replicated by hand, and the two halves can disagree
issues.gameImpact: A game that forgets the `__DEV__` define loses every dev warning but keeps engine.debug. The WASM half of dev mode (dev-tools, physics-debug) is a separate manual build choice, so TS and WASM can be in different modes.
issues.evidence: Only the engine's own vite.config.ts:17-19 defines `__DEV__`. Engine code tests `typeof __DEV__` at 7 sites, so an undefined value turns the warnings off (entity-handle.ts:341), while engine.debug returns null only when `__DEV__` is defined and false (hyperion.ts:282). The Rust features are chosen per wasm-pack run (ts/package.json:9-15).
issues.roundFix: None.
issues.workaround: Add the define and the matching wasm-pack features to the game's build.

issues.issue: Plugin guarantees promised in the masterplan are missing, and the debug key defaults collide with the browser
issues.gameImpact: Plugin and tool authors must purge per-entity data themselves, and slow hooks produce no warning. The inspector's default key, F12, is the browser's devtools key.
issues.evidence: PluginStorageAPI maps are never purged (plugin-context.ts:61-78), although masterplan :654 promises automatic cleanup on destroy. The facade emits `entity:released` instead (hyperion.ts:873). game-loop.ts has no hook time budget, although masterplan :650 promises a 2 ms warning. The default keys are F12 (ecs-inspector.ts:49) and F1 (debug-camera.ts:14).
issues.roundFix: None.
issues.workaround: Subscribe to 'entity:released' and remap the keys.

missingForCompleteGame: A production build that works and is validated: the Vite worker format fixed (likely `worker.format: 'es'`), the bundle built in preflight, and the production bundle checked on a GPU in each supported mode
A LICENSE for the engine, `license.workspace` in the crate, and third-party notices: the Apache-2.0 crates in the physics build and the vendored Basis Universal transcoder
An installable, versioned distribution: a library build with .d.ts and an exports map, prebuilt WASM variants (standard, physics, dev-tools) and a loader option for their URL, with semver tags

User documentation: a README and getting-started guide; an API reference generated from the JSDoc; guides for execution modes, assets, physics, lighting and web and desktop deployment; a changelog with migration notes
A starter template or sample game, outside the verification harness
A supported headless test path for game code: a Node loader for the WASM, a public step(dt), exported fake bridge and fixtures, and CI running the Rust and TS suites
Dev tools that work in every mode: the ECS inspector fixed and given a real component channel, camera sync to the Mode A render worker, and overlays and GPU profiling available in Mode A
Replay and rewind wired into engine.debug, with tape save/load and a dev-tools build switch

Error surfacing: a Mode B init that rejects, a reported renderer failure, dev warnings fed from the WASM rejection and drop counters, a TS↔WASM protocol version check, and isolation of the frame tick and user physics callbacks

Config and API that do what they say: wire or remove fixedTimestep, commandBufferSize, backpressure, onModeChange, onOverflow and textureStreaming; implement or remove compact(), memoryStats and enablePostProcessing

A real asset pipeline: recursive scans and image sizes; sprite sheets and atlases with sub-rect drawing; textures above 512 px and non-square; audio and font assets; KTX2/Basis encoding and a verified ESM transcoder
Level and scene tooling: a serializable scene and prefab format that can describe lights, physics, depth and nesting, plus importers for an external editor (Tiled, LDtk)
A verified desktop packaging recipe (Electron/Tauri), with a mode policy that keeps textures and camera control working
surveys.summary:
Tooling, DX and distribution is the least ready part of Hyperion for an outside game team. The repo is a well-tested source tree with a verification harness for engine development, not a product a team can adopt.

**Blockers**
- The documented production build fails: Vite's default iife worker format cannot code-split the workers' dynamic imports. This is recorded only in the 5b plan, and no validation runs the build.
- There is no licence. This blocks any team that is not the owner, and it is a one-file fix.

**Major gaps**
- **Distribution:** no package or library build (private 0.1.0, no exports, no .d.ts, no prebuilt WASM, hard-coded WASM paths, Vite only).
- **Documentation:** no user docs or examples. There is one stale deployment guide, Italian design docs and an agent-oriented CLAUDE.md.
- **Testing:** no headless test path and no CI.
- **Versioning:** none, while behaviour changes every round (step 8 turns every textured image upright).

**Dev tools are uneven**
- GPU profiling, the debug probe, shader hot-reload and the CPU overlay work in Modes B and C.
- The ECS inspector throws on first use, and its WASM channel is a stub.
- In Mode A the debug camera, the overlays, textures and camera control do nothing, and `preferredMode: 'auto'` picks Mode A on Chromium and desktop shells.
- Replay, snapshot rewind and createHotSystem are libraries nothing wires in.
- The asset pipeline only generates texture paths, reporting 0×0 sizes for PNG/JPEG, and the KTX2/Basis path has never run with a real asset.

**Silent behaviour**
- Seven config fields and several methods (compact, memoryStats, enablePostProcessing) do nothing.
- Some failures are silent or kill the loop: a Mode B init hang, a renderer failure, commands the WASM rejects or cannot decode, a throw in the frame.

**What the round changes:** only the selection of the physics build (step 8b) and Mode A device-lost reporting (step 10).

A team can still start. It would vendor the repo as a submodule, fix the worker format, force Mode B, build the WASM in CI with the pinned toolchain, write its own test seams and loaders, and budget engine work for the inspector, error surfacing and asset tooling.

capabilities.feature: GPU culling and draw submission at 100k entities
capabilities.evidence: Stateless compute cull, then a fixed draw count whatever the entity count: 12 opaque indirect draws plus 1 uber transparent draw (forward-pass.ts:266-290). Measured: 42-47 µs at 100k on an RTX 4060 laptop (Linux/Vulkan, subgroup path), 37-41 µs on the atomic path at 50% visible, 337 µs at 1M (docs/plans/2026-09-26-cull-temporal-firstinstance-brief.md:106-118). 0.155-0.160 ms (an interval) at 100k on the Apple M2 Pro (docs/plans/assets/2026-09-29-mac-m2/bench-head.json, passes.cull). On the M2 the subgroup path files every index in the right bucket (README §M5, 120/120 cases).
capabilities.note: Meets the masterplan target compute-cull-100k < 0.5 ms (hyperion-masterplan.md:1047) on both GPUs. The subgroup path is gated to subgroups of exactly 32 lanes; every other device uses the atomic path (renderer.ts:265-268).

capabilities.feature: Transparent back-to-front sort (GPU radix) and one uber draw
capabilities.evidence: D3 (< 1 ms at 100k visible transparents) holds. AMD RDNA3 iGPU: 0.787 ms (equal depths) and 0.869 ms (distinct depths), 2026-09-27-transparent-sort-uber-design.md:765. M2 Pro: the sort chain averages 0.70-0.76 ms, maximum 0.995 ms (README §M8, m8-diag-sort-timeline-100k.json). With 100k transparent 16-px quads, the M2 frame span is 4.5-5.7 ms at 120 fps in Mode B (bench-head.json, bench-*-run2.json).
capabilities.note: The M2 margin is thin: with equal depths, 42 of 181 frames are above 0.9 ms. The uber draw adds +0.21/+0.23 ms at 10k on the M2, whatever the depths (README §M8).

capabilities.evidence: AMD iGPU at 1080p: about 2.3 ms in total (SDF chain 1.77 ms, light-accum 0.22 ms for 3 lights, seed 0.03 ms, forward +0.30 ms). Each extra SDF set adds 1.84 ms and each extra group 0.34 ms (2026-08-04-phase17-lighting-2d-design.md:986-1010). M2 Pro: about 4.06 ms of frame span on the Lighting tab (lit 4.84 ms against off 0.79 ms; design :1019-1029, lighting-cost.json). A sun as the only shadowed light costs 2.552 ± 0.056 ms, of which its march is 0.344 ± 0.070 ms (design :1037-1040). bufferScale and sdfOversize cannot be changed (render/lighting-backend.ts:42-45, renderer.ts:880-881).
capabilities.note: There is no cap on SDF sets, and the GPU cost with many lights was never measured. shadowSteps is the only quality setting that lowers the cost.

capabilities.evidence: A hard constant of 100 000 rows sizes every GPU column (types.ts:78), and validateConfig rejects a larger maxEntities (types.ts:115-121). Lights count against it. Raw spawns are not counted, and above the cap every upload fails validation (render/frame-inputs.ts:98-103). The buffers are allocated for 100k at startup (renderer.ts:291-322).
capabilities.note: There is no tilemap or batched primitive, so each tile is one entity of the budget.

capabilities.evidence: The coalescing queue loses nothing and stays fair: keys keep their first-write order (backpressure.ts:151-318). The SharedArrayBuffer is hard-coded to 64 KB (worker-bridge.ts:12), while config.commandBufferSize is resolved and never read (types.ts:125). About 3 855 SetPosition commands of 17 bytes fit per frame (ring-buffer.ts:222-226). The '22 % peak utilization' benchmark used a 1 MB buffer (ring-buffer-bench.test.ts:36).
capabilities.note: Bulk updates beyond the buffer are spread over several frames. See robustness-9.

capabilities.feature: CPU per-frame cost (ECS tick, SoA copies, uploads)
capabilities.evidence: Never measured. The only data point: 100k static entities hold 120 fps in Mode B on the M2 Pro (bench-head.json, fps field), with the renderer process at 200-230 % CPU while the 100k are created and destroyed (README §M8 'Carico'). Every frame does O(N) work whether anything changed or not: the transform systems, a HashMap of every mapped entity (engine.rs:222-231), the legacy matrix collect that nothing reads (engine.rs:242, render_state.rs:258-263), the worker copies (worker-render-state.ts:135-155), and the full upload in Modes A/B (renderer.ts:956-996). The light list costs +0.04, +0.15 and +1.9 ms at 300, 1000 and 10 000 lights (Node, M2; CLAUDE.md phase table, step 7).
capabilities.note: The masterplan §22 benchmarks (ecs-tick-10k/100k, gpu-upload-100k, full-frame-100k, mode-c-10k, spawn-despawn-churn; hyperion-masterplan.md:1039-1050) were never run.

capabilities.evidence: Only Mode C reads the dirty staging (worker-bridge.ts:480-500). The worker path never carries any (worker-render-state.ts:183-214), so Modes A and B rewrite 124 bytes per entity every frame (renderer.ts:956-996).

capabilities.feature: Allocation-free frame loop (masterplan §3: 'no GC pressure in the game loop')
capabilities.evidence: Per-frame allocation sites: the worker allocates new SoA arrays every tick (worker-render-state.ts:135-155), and the main thread copies them again in Mode A (worker-bridge.ts:279-300) and out of WASM memory in Mode C (worker-bridge.ts:519-524). Every command allocates a typed array and a queue entry (backpressure.ts:166-190, 403-476). The particle system builds a Map of N tuples (renderer.ts:1119-1130), and deriveLightGroups builds arrays, sets and maps (light-groups.ts:239-253, 273-338). The constraint itself is at hyperion-masterplan.md:71.

capabilities.feature: Frame pacing: configurable fixed step and render interpolation
capabilities.evidence: FIXED_DT = 1/60 is hard-coded (engine.rs:19), and config.fixedTimestep is resolved (types.ts:127) but never read. interpolation_alpha() (engine.rs:406-411) is not exported to WASM. The facade renders the latest state as it is (hyperion.ts:876-909).

Hooks are isolated and removed after 60 consecutive failures (game-loop.ts:179-220). tickFn is not isolated (game-loop.ts:166-176). The render graph rethrows any exception a pass throws, plugin passes included (render-graph.ts:210-225). Mode A's render loop has no catch either (render-worker.ts:70-80). See robustness-3.

On device loss the renderer only logs and calls onDeviceLost (renderer.ts:270-273); nothing rebuilds it. Snapshot and restore exist only in dev-tools builds (lib.rs:807-835). Mode A passes no callback at all (render-worker.ts:37); round step 10 adds forwarding.

capabilities.feature: Worker supervision and runtime mode degradation
capabilities.evidence: WorkerSupervisor reports one timeout and then stays silent; reset() has no caller (supervisor.ts:33-52). The bridges only log it, with TODO(Phase 5) comments (worker-bridge.ts:101-106, 215-220). onModeChange is never invoked. No bridge limits the number of ticks in flight (worker-bridge.ts:174-177, 342-345). The masterplan claims restart and degradation (hyperion-masterplan.md:124, 191).

capabilities.feature: Startup capability fallback A → B → C
capabilities.evidence: The fallback chain is in hyperion.ts:161-217. Mode A transfers the canvas before WebGPU is tested in the worker (worker-bridge.ts:223). Main-thread renderer failures are swallowed without a log (hyperion.ts:212-216). Mode B's ready promise has no reject path (worker-bridge.ts:117-120). Mode A is chosen by user-agent sniffing (capabilities.ts:31-36, 47-50).

Four square tiers, 64 to 512 px, each of 256 layers with layer 0 reserved (texture-manager.ts:5-7, 18). Every PNG or JPEG is resized to its tier's square and capped at 512 px (texture-manager.ts:684-702). On BC7/ASTC devices PNG and JPEG go to the rgba8 overflow tiers (texture-manager.ts:707-730). Loads of the same URL are not deduplicated while in flight (texture-manager.ts:545-557). Quads have no UV sub-rectangle (prim-params-schema.ts:32; quad.wgsl:5-7). The sampler is linear only (texture-manager.ts:216-218).

No texture unload API exists. compact() calls a shrinkUnusedTiers method that does not exist and never calls the WASM engine_compact_entity_map / engine_compact_render_state exports (hyperion.ts:675-680; lib.rs:423, 434). memoryStats returns zeros (hyperion.ts:455-462). Mip levels are allocated (texture-manager.ts:258, 477) but sampled only at LOD 0 (prelude.wgsl:153-171). texture-streaming.ts is not reachable from the engine (round plan §4, line 199).

ts/wasm/hyperion_core_bg.wasm: 199 970 B raw, 70 689 B gzip -9 (built on this branch on 2026-10-16). ts/wasm-physics: 872 277 B raw, 337 512 B gzip -9 (2026-10-10). The handoff measured 200 294 / 71 067 B and 873 310 / 339 781 B on Linux (docs/handoff/2026-09-29-mac-m2-handoff.md:422). The < 200 KB gzip gate applies only to the core build (ts/package.json:15).
capabilities.note: The production JS bundle has never been measured (no ts/dist; nothing builds one). The Basis transcoder is loaded lazily.

capabilities.evidence: No measurement exists. The facade and the harness load the non-physics WASM (worker-bridge.ts:384, engine-worker.ts:41). PhysicsAPI._init has no non-test caller (physics-api.ts:130); round step 8b wires it.

Rust, counted statically: 347 #[test] in src and 100 in tests/. CLAUDE.md:23-24 recorded 340 + 98 at step 7, and the step-8 plan expects 347/447. TypeScript: 116 test files; CLAUDE.md:66 recorded 2125 + 7 skipped at step 7, and the step-8 plan expects 2215 + 7 (2026-10-14-step8-sprite-light-plan.md:4626). Not run here. There is no CI (no .github); 'validated' means a local scripts/preflight.sh run. WebGPU behaviour is covered only by the manual harness.

10 tabs: 63 checks at step 7 (CLAUDE.md:497, 794) and 68 after step 8 (step-8 plan:4626). It is driven by hand through chrome-devtools MCP, with an M4 pixel-baseline gate on the Mac. The 4 Input checks wait for real input. In Safari, an automated run hangs on Audio (README §M12).

capabilities.feature: Hardware / OS / browser matrix actually verified
capabilities.evidence: Apple M2 Pro on macOS 27: Chrome 154/155 in Modes A, B and C (README M0-M10, then steps 6-8); Safari 27.0.1 in A, B and C, but only at a4708c8, before the step 6-8 shaders (README §M12). AMD RDNA3 iGPU on Fedora with Chrome/Vulkan: Modes B and C, up to phase 5b (round plan §4, lines 134-143). RTX 4060: compute timings only, since it cannot present (phase17 design:984). Never tested: Windows, Firefox (naga static validation only), Android, iOS, Electron/Tauri, ASTC (M11 skipped, README:503).

GpuProfiler (timestampWrites on the real passes) validated on M2 Chrome and Safari with 0 discards (README §M7, §M12). On the M2 its entries are intervals that overlap, so the per-pass costs cannot simply be added. engine.debug.probe is dev-only. There is no CPU-phase timing: stats.frameTimeAvg is the rAF interval (game-loop.ts:150-164), and memoryStats is a stub.

issues.issue: The texture model caps a complete game. Each tier array holds at most 255 images (4 square tiers, 64-512 px), every PNG or JPEG is resampled to its tier's square, nothing is kept above 512 px, quads have no UV sub-rectangle (so no atlas, sprite sheet or tileset), and a loaded texture can never be freed during the session.
issues.gameImpact: A multi-level game with sprite animation and tilesets runs out of layers, because every animation frame and every tile takes a layer of its own. On BC7/ASTC desktops all PNGs share the 4 × 255 rgba8 overflow layers. Backgrounds and atlases above 512 px are downscaled, non-square art is stretched, and pixel art is resampled with resizeQuality 'high' and a linear sampler. Changing level cannot release GPU memory: tier 3 in rgba8 at 256 layers is about 358 MB, counting the mips it allocates and never uses.
issues.evidence: texture-manager.ts:5-7 (TIER_SIZES, MAX_LAYERS_PER_TIER), :18 (GROWTH_STEPS up to 256), :684-702 (resize to the tier square), :707-714 and :733-740 (overflow or primary tier full: throw), :216-218 (linear sampler), :258 and :477 (mips allocated); prelude.wgsl:153-171 (LOD 0 only); prim-params-schema.ts:32 ('Quad has no schema'); quad.wgsl:5-7 (uv = position + 0.5); hyperion.ts:675-680 (compact() calls a shrinkUnusedTiers that does not exist).
issues.roundFix: Not fixed. Step 8 only makes tier images draw upright (16f5a9c, prelude.wgsl:191-198) and documents the limits in the loadTexture JSDoc. The step-8 plan lists texture unloading and tier mips as out of scope (2026-10-14-step8-sprite-light-plan.md:48). The masterplan has only 'sized binding arrays' (§17.3 #12), with no schedule.
issues.workaround: Slice all art into square images of at most 512 px, one layer each. Budget at most 255 per size class per session. Destroy and re-create the engine between levels, which in Mode A needs a fresh canvas.

issues.issue: Mirrored sprites disappear. Every entity pipeline culls back faces (cullMode 'back' with the default frontFace 'ccw'), so a negative scale, the usual way to flip a 2D character, reverses the winding and the quad is not drawn. Its occluder and selection seeds are not drawn either. There is no per-entity UV flip.
issues.gameImpact: A character turned to face left vanishes, and a rig flipped with scale(-1, 1) loses every child sprite. Lines and beziers behave the same way.
issues.evidence: forward-pass.ts:271 (uber transparent pipeline) and :285 (opaque pipelines); occluder-seed-stage.ts:96; selection-seed-pass.ts:107; no frontFace anywhere in ts/src. The defect is recorded in the round plan §2, line 72, and in the step-8 plan, line 4670.
issues.roundFix: Not fixed. Step 8 sets cullMode 'none' only on the light pipeline (light-accum-stage.ts:164-166) and records the entity defect in §4 as point '(1b)'. No step owns it.
issues.workaround: Ship pre-mirrored copies of the images, which doubles the layers they use under robustness-1.

issues.issue: A single exception anywhere in the frame stops the engine for good. GameLoop.frame calls tickFn outside any try/catch, so requestAnimationFrame is never armed again. _running stays true, so start() does nothing. A throw from Hyperion.tick, renderer.render, any render-graph pass (plugin overlays included) or a WASM trap in Mode C is fatal. Mode A's render worker loop has the same flaw.
issues.gameImpact: A bug in a plugin pass, a bad parameter that makes a pass throw, or a Rust panic freezes the game for good, with no event the game can catch to restart the loop.
issues.evidence: game-loop.ts:166-176 (tickFn not isolated, rAF armed after it) and :88 (start() returns when already running); render-graph.ts:210-225 (catch, then rethrow); renderer.ts:1090-1096 (rethrow); render-worker.ts:70-80 (no catch); no panic hook in crates/hyperion-core (no set_hook or console_error_panic_hook).
issues.roundFix: Not fixed by any step. Round step 1 isolated only hooks (game-loop.ts:179-220).
issues.workaround: Wrap your own code defensively. Watch stats.tickCount for a stall, then destroy and re-create the engine.

issues.issue: GPU device loss is not recovered. The renderer logs the loss and calls config.onDeviceLost. No API rebuilds the renderer or re-uploads textures, and production builds have no ECS snapshot (snapshot and restore are dev-tools only). In Mode A the loss stays inside the render worker. The masterplan still says 'device.lost recovery trasparente'.
issues.gameImpact: After a driver reset, a GPU process crash or GPU switching, the canvas freezes or goes black while the simulation keeps running. Recovering means rebuilding the whole world from the game's own state, or reloading the page.
issues.evidence: renderer.ts:270-273; lib.rs:807-835 (#[cfg(feature = "dev-tools")] on engine_reset/snapshot_create/snapshot_restore); render-worker.ts:37 (createRenderer without a callback); hyperion-masterplan.md:232, 247; no uncapturederror handler in the engine (only the harness has one, demo/probe-checks.ts:110).
issues.roundFix: Partial. Step 10 forwards Mode A's device lost (worker → bridge → config.onDeviceLost) and corrects masterplan lines 232 and 247 (round plan §3, row 10). Recovery itself remains missing after the round.
issues.workaround: In onDeviceLost, save the game state and reload the page, or destroy and re-create the engine (with a new canvas in Mode A) and respawn the world.

issues.issue: Startup failures are silent, and some hang. (a) Mode A transfers the canvas with transferControlToOffscreen before it knows WebGPU works in the worker. If the render worker fails, the fallback to Mode B calls createRenderer on the transferred canvas, the error is swallowed, and the canvas stays blank with no message. (b) Any main-thread createRenderer failure is swallowed without a log. (c) Mode B's ready promise can never reject, and no bridge listens to worker onerror, so a worker or WASM load failure leaves Hyperion.create pending forever. (d) The 'auto' mode chooses Mode A by user-agent sniffing.
issues.gameImpact: On some Chromium configurations, or after a CDN hiccup that loses the .wasm, players get a blank canvas or a loader that never finishes, and the engine reports nothing the game can surface.
issues.evidence: worker-bridge.ts:223 (transfer before any worker check); hyperion.ts:174-201 (fallback chain), :212-216 (catch { renderer = null }, no log); worker-bridge.ts:117-120 (Mode B ready has only a resolve) and :131-132 (an 'error' message is only logged); no onerror in ts/src; capabilities.ts:31-36 (webgpuInWorker guessed from the UA). In M12 Safari 27 did not hit the fallback defect, because it runs WebGPU in the worker (README §M12).
issues.roundFix: Not fixed. Step 10 covers only the empty world and device-lost forwarding.
issues.workaround: Pin preferredMode to 'B' or 'C'. Put a timeout around Hyperion.create. Check renderer availability indirectly, for example compressionFormat is null when there is no renderer.

issues.issue: Modes A and B have no flow control and no working supervision. The main thread posts a tick message every requestAnimationFrame whether or not the previous tick is done (TickSequencer counts ticks in flight but never gates them). The 10-tick spiral cap applies per message, not per unit of real time. The supervisor reports a single heartbeat timeout and never resets: no restart, no A→B→C degradation, and onModeChange is never called. Mode B always draws a state at least one frame old.
issues.gameImpact: When the simulation is heavier than a frame (physics, many entities, a slow device), the worker's message queue and the input-to-display latency grow without bound instead of the game slowing down. A crashed worker leaves a frozen game, the queued critical commands keep accumulating, and the only trace is a console warning. A pause longer than 3 s raises a false timeout and silences later ones.
issues.evidence: worker-bridge.ts:174-177 and :342-345 (one postMessage per tick); tick-sequencer.ts:15-41; engine.rs:207-218 (cap per update call); supervisor.ts:33-52 (reset() has no caller); worker-bridge.ts:101-106 and :215-220 (TODO(Phase 5): only console.warn); engine-worker.ts:68-89 (no try/catch around engine_update). The masterplan promises restart and degradation (hyperion-masterplan.md:124, 191).
issues.roundFix: Not fixed: no step covers it.
issues.workaround: Keep the per-tick simulation cost well under one frame on the slowest target, or use Mode C, which is synchronous and slows down instead of queueing.

issues.issue: The simulation runs at a hard-coded 60 Hz and nothing interpolates between ticks. config.fixedTimestep is ignored, interpolation_alpha() is never exported, and every frame shows the latest tick unchanged. On frames where no tick ran, the engine still copies and re-uploads the full state.
issues.gameImpact: Motion and camera follow judder whenever the display rate is not exactly 60 Hz: at 120 Hz each state stays for 2 frames (Chrome ran rAF at 120 Hz on the M2), at 75 or 144 Hz the cadence is uneven, and even at 60 Hz timing jitter gives 0 or 2 ticks per frame. A camera moved from TS every frame drifts against sprites stepped at 60 Hz. Physics cannot run at another rate.
issues.evidence: engine.rs:19 (FIXED_DT), :207-218, :406-411 (interpolation_alpha in Rust only); config.fixedTimestep is resolved (types.ts:127) and read nowhere else; hyperion.ts:876-909 (the state is rendered as is); README:18 (rAF at 120 Hz in Chrome on the M2).
issues.roundFix: Not fixed, and not in the masterplan.
issues.workaround: None inside the engine. A game could compute its own interpolation and drive it with positionImmediate for the few entities whose motion matters.

issues.issue: Every frame copies the whole SoA (about 128 bytes per entity) and allocates in the hot path, in every mode. This breaks the masterplan's 'no GC pressure in the game loop' constraint. The engine worker allocates 6 new typed arrays per tick. The Mode A main thread copies all of them again. Mode C copies every column out of WASM memory each frame. Each command allocates a payload typed array and a queue entry. With any particle emitter alive, the renderer builds a Map of N tuples every frame. Rust builds a HashMap of every mapped entity each frame, and fills a legacy matrix buffer that TS never reads.
issues.gameImpact: At 100k entities that is about 12.8 MB of fresh buffers per frame (twice that in Mode A), and about 1.3 MB at 10k. The likely result is GC pauses and jank on mid-range and mobile devices. CPU frame cost has never been measured. The only data point is 100k static quads at 120 fps in Mode B on an M2 Pro.
issues.evidence: worker-render-state.ts:135-155; worker-bridge.ts:279-300 (Mode A copies), :494-499 and :519-524 (Mode C copies); backpressure.ts:166-190 and :403-476 (new Float32Array per command); renderer.ts:1119-1130 (particle Map); engine.rs:228-229 (per-frame HashMap) and :242 with render_state.rs:258-263 (legacy collect); engine_render_state_* exports are only declared in TS (worker-bridge.ts:405-407); hyperion-masterplan.md:71; bench-head.json (fps 120 at N = 100000).
issues.roundFix: Not fixed.
issues.workaround: Keep entity counts well below the cap on low-end targets, avoid particle emitters in large scenes, batch commands, and profile GC in the target browsers.

issues.issue: The ring buffer is fixed at 64 KB, and the related config is ignored: commandBufferSize, backpressure 'drop' and onOverflow are never read. About 3 855 SetPosition commands, or roughly 1 000 fully configured sprite spawns, fit per frame. Beyond that the queue defers the rest round-robin, with a single dev-only warning. Spawn commands drain before any setter, and a spawned entity is drawable at once as a white unit quad at the origin. There is no visibility toggle to spawn an entity hidden.
issues.gameImpact: A level load that spawns thousands of entities in one frame flashes white quads at the origin for several frames while positions, scales and textures trickle in. TS-driven motion above about 3.8k entities per frame quietly updates each entity at a fraction of the frame rate.
issues.evidence: worker-bridge.ts:12 (RING_BUFFER_CAPACITY = 64 * 1024); types.ts:125-126 (resolved but unused, no consumer in ts/src); ring-buffer.ts:97-125 (payload sizes) and :222-226 (5 + payload bytes); backpressure.ts:269-286 (criticals first; setters wait while any critical remains); command_processor.rs:530-544 (default quad, white texture, origin, scale 1); components.rs:64, 91, 489-492; no visibility command among types 0-16 (ring_buffer.rs:35-52); ring-buffer-bench.test.ts:36 (the bench used 1 MB).
issues.roundFix: Not fixed.
issues.workaround: Spawn large levels in chunks of under about 1 000 entities per frame behind a DOM loading overlay. Move entities with velocity or physics in Rust instead of per-frame SetPosition.

issues.issue: The default 'auto' mode picks Mode A on any Chromium user agent (Electron included), and Mode A is a reduced engine. The main-thread camera never reaches the render worker, which keeps a fixed orthographic camera. loadTexture throws. Particle emitters return null, and bloom and outlines throw. Probes are unavailable. Today the empty world and device lost are also broken in Mode A.
issues.gameImpact: A game shipped with default settings would be unable to scroll the camera or show any textured sprite in Chrome and Electron, and nothing would fail loudly enough to be noticed early.
issues.evidence: capabilities.ts:31-36 and :47-50; render-worker.ts:18, :40-41, :65-66 (worker camera fixed at init and resize); hyperion.ts:862-916 (tick sends only the listener position, no camera); hyperion.ts:564 (no renderer: throw) and :847 (null emitter); worker-bridge.ts:272 and render-worker.ts:72 (empty world); README §M6 (?mode=auto picks A on Chrome/macOS).
issues.roundFix: Partial. Step 10 fixes the empty world and forwards device lost. Step 8 declares 'textures do not load in Mode A' a limitation (round plan §2, line 70). Camera sync, textures, particles and effects in Mode A stay missing.
issues.workaround: Always set preferredMode: 'B', or 'C' where there is no SharedArrayBuffer.

issues.issue: The verified platform matrix is narrow, and there is no CI. The current code runs on hardware only on an Apple M2 Pro: Chrome in Modes A, B and C, and Safari last verified before steps 6-8. The AMD iGPU on Linux was verified in Modes B and C up to phase 5b, and the RTX 4060 only for compute timings. Nothing ran on Windows/D3D12, Firefox, Android, iOS, Electron or Tauri, or on an ASTC device. The deployment guide's Electron and Tauri setup is untested. It contradicts the detection code: SharedArrayBuffer is detected only when crossOriginIsolated, so a page loaded with loadFile would run in Mode C. GPU checks are run by hand through MCP on one Mac.
issues.gameImpact: A web and desktop release depends on platforms where no frame of the engine has ever been looked at. Windows and Chromium on D3D12 is the main desktop market. Driver-specific failures of the kind found on Metal and AMD (subgroup widths, indirect-first-instance, compressed copies) are likely to exist elsewhere.
issues.evidence: docs/plans/assets/2026-09-29-mac-m2/README.md:31-46 (M0-M12) and :503 (M11 ASTC skipped); README §M12 (Safari at a4708c8); round plan §4, lines 134-143 (AMD verification of steps 4-5b), line 149 and line 189 (Safari legs deferred to step 9); phase17 design:984 (NVIDIA cannot present); capabilities.ts:19-25 (SharedArrayBuffer requires crossOriginIsolated) against deployment-guide.md:276-310 ('No HTTP headers need to be configured'); no .github directory; scripts/preflight.sh (local).
issues.roundFix: Partial. Step 9 re-runs /gpu-check on the Mac in Chrome A/B/C and Safari A/B/C, with a committed safaridriver driver. Fedora B/C is non-blocking, 'at the next session' (round plan §3, row 9). Nothing is planned for Windows, mobile, Firefox, desktop shells or CI.
issues.workaround: The team builds its own device lab and CI and runs the harness on every target before committing to it.

issues.issue: Modes A and B upload every SoA column in full on every frame, because the worker path never carries the scatter staging. Only Mode C uploads the dirty rows alone.
issues.gameImpact: About 12.4 MB per frame at 100k entities, roughly 0.74 GB/s at 60 fps and 1.5 GB/s at 120 fps, even for a static scene. It was fine on the M2 Pro (120 fps at 100k); bandwidth-limited GPUs were never measured.
issues.evidence: worker-render-state.ts:183-214 (dirtyCount 0, stagingData null); engine-worker.ts:84-88; renderer.ts:940-996 (the useScatter test, then five writeBuffer calls); round plan §4, line 124.
issues.roundFix: Not fixed.
issues.workaround: Use Mode C for mostly static scenes on weak GPUs, or keep entity counts low.

issues.issue: Texture loading has three defects. loadTexture does not deduplicate a URL already in flight, so concurrent loads of one URL fetch it again and each takes a new layer. loadTextureWithPriority called again for a URL still queued overwrites jobByUrl, so the first promise never settles and 'total' is counted twice. When a tier is already at 256 layers, ensureTierCapacity reallocates and copies the whole tier before the load throws. Separately, loadTextures ignores 'concurrency'.
issues.gameImpact: Promise.all over the same sprite burns scarce layers (robustness-1). A loader awaiting a priority load can hang. Each failed load into a full 512-px tier allocates and copies about 358 MB of GPU memory, enough to risk device loss.
issues.evidence: texture-manager.ts:545-557 (only the cache is checked), :565-580 (jobByUrl.set overwrites), :68-77 (the queue keeps one entry per URL), :442-536 with :733-740, :709-714, :788-791 and :824-827 (grow, then check the cap); hyperion.ts:573-590 (sequential loop).
issues.roundFix: Not fixed: step 8 only adds pendingLoads (texture-manager.ts:607-615).
issues.workaround: Preload each URL exactly once, with your own cache of promises, and check the tier fill (engine.debug.textureTiers in dev) before loading.

issues.issue: The KTX2 and ASTC paths are unverified and partly wrong. The KTXorientation key is never parsed. KTX2 dimensions are not checked against the tier: an image smaller than its tier lands in a corner, and one larger than 512 px fails validation silently while the load still resolves. The format check accepts any vkFormat on an rgba8 tier. Only mip 0 is uploaded. The repository has no KTX2 asset. On ASTC devices, layer 0 and unfilled layers are all-zero blocks that decode to the error colour, and msdf_shade's raw sampleTier reaches them.
issues.gameImpact: A compressed-texture pipeline, the one mobile would use, can show flipped, cornered, blank or magenta textures with no error. ASTC has never run on hardware.
issues.evidence: No key/value-data parsing in ktx2-parser.ts or texture-manager.ts (the only kvd references are in ktx2-stream-loader.ts:78-79); texture-manager.ts:769-772, :811-816, :831-845; msdf-text.wgsl:41 (raw sampleTier); prelude.wgsl:191-194 (index 0 answered white only through sampleTierOrWhite); git ls-files has no .ktx2; README:503 (M11 skipped).
issues.roundFix: Not fixed. Step 8 extends the index-0 and unloaded-layer guards to sprite lights only (light-accum.wgsl:232; light-groups.ts untexturedPredicate, 75edceb). KTXorientation is out of step 8's scope (step-8 plan:48).
issues.workaround: Use PNG/JPEG, or KTX2 files authored at exactly the tier size with 'rd' orientation, and test on the target GPUs.

issues.issue: Two light-shader edge cases. Rim NaN: with falloff 0, pow(1 − d/range, 0) is pow(0, 0) wherever d/range rounds to 1; that value is undefined in WGSL and it also passes through a mix light's clamp. Light types 5-7: Rust masks the type to 3 bits instead of rejecting it, and the shader draws such a light as an unrotated square at full intensity, culled at radius = range.
issues.gameImpact: Flat-falloff lights can leave NaN specks in the light buffer, which bilinear sampling spreads. Types 5-7 are reachable only through raw commands, tapes or snapshots: the TS LightType has 5 values and the default falloff is 1.
issues.evidence: light-accum.wgsl:519-523 and :551-559; entity-handle.ts:117 and :757 (falloff ?? 1); command_processor.rs:1029-1043 (masked, not rejected); light-accum.wgsl:206-245 and :491-549 (types 5-7 take the generic branches); systems.rs:286-292 (radius = range).
issues.roundFix: Not fixed. The falloff-0 NaN is registered for step 9 (round plan §4, line 190), but step 9's exit criterion (§3, row 9) does not require a fix. Types 5-7 are out of step 8's scope (step-8 plan:48 and :4656) and no other step covers them.
issues.workaround: Use falloff > 0, and never send raw light types above 4.

issues.issue: Memory never goes back, and the engine cannot report it. compact() is a no-op, memoryStats returns zeros, the WASM compaction exports are never called, and WASM linear memory never shrinks. The TS id allocator and the Rust EntityMap grow to the highest id ever used, up to 1 048 576 entries, because fresh ids are handed out first.
issues.gameImpact: Long sessions keep their peak memory, and a team has no telemetry to see it grow.
issues.evidence: hyperion.ts:666-680 (compact), :455-462 (memoryStats); lib.rs:423, 434 (exports never called from TS); entity-id-allocator.ts:50-70 and :37 (state array grown on demand); command_processor.rs:61-70 (Vec indexed by external id).
issues.roundFix: Not fixed.
issues.workaround: Measure with browser tools (performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory, about:gpu). Restart the engine between long sessions if needed.

issues.issue: Diagnostics are broken or silent. The ECS inspector calls the selection.selectedIds getter as a method, so it throws a TypeError on every postTick while the panel is open, and the hook is dropped after 60 failures; a mock in the test hides it. The inspector's WASM detail channel is a stub. TS never reads the engine_rejected_command_count or engine_dropped_command_bytes counters, so protocol skew and rejected commands go unseen.
issues.gameImpact: The F12 inspector does not work, and a TS/WASM version mismatch from stale caching silently drops the rest of every command batch.
issues.evidence: ecs-inspector.ts:63 and :115 against selection.ts:69 (get selectedIds); ecs-inspector.test.ts:26 (vi.fn mock); ecs-inspector.ts:136-138 (stub); worker-bridge.ts:396-403 (counters declared, never called).
issues.roundFix: Not fixed. The inspector bug was found in step 1b (round plan §4, line 122) and assigned to no step.
issues.workaround: Version the .wasm and .js together with cache-busting file names, and read the counters directly from the WASM in debug builds.

issues.issue: Raw entity ids alias after reuse. After 1 048 576 cumulative spawns, freed ids come back oldest first, and a stale raw id then addresses the new entity, because the wire format has no generation.
issues.gameImpact: Games that keep raw ids, for example bullet hells using RawAPI, can mutate the wrong entity after long sessions. EntityHandles are protected because a destroyed handle is dead for good.
issues.evidence: entity-id-allocator.ts:17-33 and :50-67; types.ts:62-68.
issues.roundFix: Not fixed: it is a design limit and needs a protocol change.
issues.workaround: Do not keep raw ids past a despawn. Use EntityHandle for long-lived references.

issues.issue: The 100 000-row cap is a compile-time constant. It includes lights, and raw spawns bypass maxEntities. Above the cap every upload of a frame fails GPU validation and the image freezes, with only a one-time warning.
issues.gameImpact: Large tilemaps (one entity per tile) or big raw-spawned crowds can hit the cap, and the result is a frozen image rather than an error.
issues.evidence: types.ts:78 and :115-121; render/frame-inputs.ts:98-103; renderer.ts:925-931 (warning only); hyperion.ts:472-476 (only handles are counted).
issues.roundFix: Not changed: it is by design.
issues.workaround: Chunk levels and stream entities, keeping well below 100k live rows including lights.

issues.issue: Lighting cost grows with layer configuration and resolution, and the engine offers few ways to reduce it. Each distinct caster set is a full SDF flood with no cap. The light buffer and the SDF are fixed at half resolution (bufferScale and sdfOversize are rejected), so shadowSteps is the only quality setting. The GPU cost of many shadowed lights was never measured.
issues.gameImpact: About 2.3 ms on an AMD iGPU and about 4 ms on the M2 Pro at 1080p for a small scene. Each additional caster set adds about 1.8-2.2 ms. On a full-screen Retina canvas or a low-end GPU, the lit backend can take most of the frame.
issues.evidence: phase17 design:986-1010 and :1019-1040; render/lighting-backend.ts:42-45; renderer.ts:872-883; lighting-api.ts:94-100.
issues.roundFix: Partial. Step 8 stops shadowed lights that cannot draw (range ≤ 0, or a sprite without a texture) from opening an SDF set (2e507fe). Step 8c only decides SDF padding, which would add cost. bufferScale stays fixed.
issues.workaround: Keep light layers and caster sets few, lower shadowSteps, and render to a smaller canvas backing store on weak GPUs.

missingForCompleteGame: Texture atlases and UV sub-rectangles for quads (sprite sheets, tilesets), textures above 512 px and non-square textures without resampling, per-level texture unload and memory release, mip generation, and a nearest-filter option for pixel art
Rendering of mirrored sprites: no back-face culling on 2D entity pipelines, or a flip flag
Error isolation of tickFn, render-graph passes and plugin overlays, so that one exception does not kill the loop, plus a restart path
GPU device-loss recovery: rebuild the renderer, re-upload textures, keep the ECS. Also a production (non-dev-tools) snapshot/restore for recovery and save games

Flow control between the main thread and the worker (limit the ticks in flight), worker crash detection with restart and A→B→C degradation, and startup timeouts with reported failures (no silent blank canvas)
Render interpolation between fixed ticks, or a configurable fixed timestep honouring config.fixedTimestep, for 75/120/144 Hz displays

An allocation-free frame path: reused or pooled SoA buffers, command encoding without per-call typed arrays, the scatter upload in Modes A/B, and removal of the unused legacy matrix collect and the per-frame HashMap
A configurable ring buffer (honour commandBufferSize), atomic spawn-with-components or a hidden-until-configured state, and a visibility toggle
Mode A parity, or a safe default: camera sync to the render worker, texture loading, particles and effects. Until then 'auto' should not pick Mode A
Working compact() and memoryStats, CPU-phase timings, and reading of the WASM rejected/dropped command counters

Benchmarks for the masterplan §22 targets (ecs-tick-10k/100k, gpu-upload-100k, full-frame-100k with moving entities, mode-c-10k, spawn-despawn churn, physics bodies at scale) on low-end desktop and mobile hardware
Hardware verification on Windows (Chromium/D3D12, Electron/WebView2), Android and iOS, Firefox and Tauri, plus an ASTC device, and a CI pipeline that at least runs preflight on every change

surveys.dimension: Roadmap and the gap to a complete game. Read: hyperion-masterplan.md in full; the open-items round plan §2-§5; the step-8 plan's scope; the Phase 17 design's deferred items. Compared at feature-checklist level with Phaser 3/4, PixiJS 8, Excalibur.js, Godot 4's web export and Defold. Every Hyperion claim was checked in the code at feat/step8-sprite-light 4d1940f. Peer features come from their public documentation and were not re-checked in this session.

capabilities.feature: GPU-driven 2D rendering at scale (compute culling, indirect draw, up to 100 000 entities)
capabilities.evidence: ts/src/shaders/cull.wgsl:22,69 (compute cull over 7 primitive types); ts/src/types.ts:78,119-120 (MAX_GPU_ENTITIES = 100 000, and validateConfig rejects more); cull measured at 37-47 µs for 100k on an RTX 4060 (docs/plans/2026-09-26-cull-temporal-firstinstance-brief.md)
capabilities.note: AHEAD. Phaser and Excalibur batch on the CPU over WebGL. PixiJS 8 culls and batches on the CPU (WebGL/WebGPU). Godot's web export runs the WebGL 2 Compatibility renderer and Defold HTML5 runs WebGL. Caveat: 100 000 is a hard ceiling, not a target.

capabilities.feature: Transparent sprite ordering (GPU radix sort, one uber draw) and 2D depth
capabilities.evidence: ts/src/render/passes/transparent-sort-pass.ts:96; transparent-sort-constants.ts:24,70 (7 passes, CAP 100 000); crates/hyperion-core/src/components.rs:275-280 (Depth is the z of a 2D row); 0.787/0.869 ms at 100 000 visible transparents on the AMD iGPU (docs/plans/2026-09-27-transparent-sort-uber-design.md §11, docs/plans/assets/2026-09-27-transparent-sort-bench-step4.json)
capabilities.note: AHEAD of the web peers, which sort on the CPU. Caveat 1: any sprite with transparent pixels MUST be .transparent(), because the opaque pipelines have no blend and quad_fs never discards (ts/src/render/passes/forward-pass.ts:275-286, ts/src/shaders/primitives/quad.wgsl:15-17). Caveat 2: opaque sprites at equal depth overlap in no defined order. Caveat 3: the .opaque() JSDoc promises a front-to-back sort that does not exist (ts/src/entity-handle.ts:475).

capabilities.evidence: crates/hyperion-core/src/systems.rs:133 (propagate_transforms, arbitrary depth); crates/hyperion-core/src/command_processor.rs:45 (MAX_HIERARCHY_DEPTH 64)
capabilities.note: On par with the peers' display trees.

capabilities.evidence: ts/src/texture-manager.ts:5,684-701 (every PNG/JPEG is resized to a SQUARE of 64/128/256/512 px; anything larger goes down to 512); :216-219 (the only sampler is linear); :7,733-740 (255 textures per tier array, then it throws); no unload API (destroy() at :882 is the only release); ts/src/shaders/primitives/prelude.wgsl:151-167 (always LOD 0, so the allocated mips are never sampled); :191-198 (images upright since step 8, already on this branch)

Here pixel art blurs (upscaled by a 'high' resize, then sampled linearly), HD backgrounds lose resolution, and non-square art is stretched unless the entity's scale restores the aspect.

capabilities.feature: Sprite animation (sprite sheets, texture atlases, frame sequences, tweens)
capabilities.evidence: ts/src/shaders/primitives/quad.wgsl:5-7 and prelude.wgsl:142-145 (a quad's uv is always the full 0..1 square); ts/src/prim-params-schema.ts:31 ('Quad has no schema (all 8 slots unused)'); no public primParams setter (ts/src/entity-handle.ts:537-571 covers only line/gradient/boxShadow/bezier; ts/src/raw-api.ts:47-82); no animation or tween module in ts/src

The only workaround is one texture per frame swapped with .texture(), which the 255-per-tier cap and the missing unload exhaust quickly.

capabilities.feature: Per-sprite tint, alpha/opacity, visibility, horizontal flip
capabilities.evidence: crates/hyperion-core/src/ring_buffer.rs:35-119 (57 commands, none for colour, alpha or visibility); crates/hyperion-core/src/command_processor.rs:530-544 (every spawn is a drawn quad plus Active, and no command removes Active); scale(-1,1) reverses the winding and cullMode 'back' drops the quad (ts/src/render/passes/forward-pass.ts:271,285; occluder-seed-stage.ts:96; selection-seed-pass.ts:107)

capabilities.evidence: git grep 'tilemap|TileMap|tileset' over ts/src and crates: 0 files; not mentioned anywhere in hyperion-masterplan.md
capabilities.note: Shipped by Phaser, Excalibur (Tiled/LDtk plugins), Godot (TileMapLayer plus editor) and Defold (tilemap plus editor); PixiJS has it via @pixi/tilemap. Here a level is one entity per tile, each tile type its own texture layer.

capabilities.evidence: Prefabs only: ts/src/prefab/types.ts:12-37 (one level of children; transform, texture, primitive, primParams and data, no body, collider or light fields) and ts/src/prefab/registry.ts:62. No scene or level module. reset and snapshot exist only with dev-tools (crates/hyperion-core/src/lib.rs:808-878).
capabilities.note: Peers: Phaser's Scene manager, Excalibur scenes with transitions, Godot's scene tree, Defold collection proxies; PixiJS has none. A level switch here means destroying every handle by hand, and textures cannot be unloaded.

capabilities.evidence: No UI module in ts/src. hyperion-masterplan.md:35 says 'Non è un framework UI'. The only camera is the world camera (ts/src/camera-api.ts:15-46). Particles are drawn on the swapchain after the whole graph, so they cover any in-canvas HUD (ts/src/renderer.ts:1116-1141).
capabilities.note: Godot Control nodes and Defold GUI are full UI systems; Phaser and Excalibur have screen-space and DOM elements; PixiJS has @pixi/ui. Workaround here: HTML/CSS over the canvas. But keyboard input listens on the canvas (ts/src/hyperion.ts:220, ts/src/input-manager.ts:189-211), so clicking a DOM button stops keyboard input until the canvas is clicked again.

capabilities.evidence: ts/src/text/text-layout.ts:14-51 (single line; no wrapping, alignment or kerning; iterates UTF-16 code units); ts/src/text/text-manager.ts:17-23 (closes the atlas bitmap and records layer 0 as a 'Placeholder'); no public glyph setter (ts/src/prefab/registry.ts:130-136 reaches into the private _producer); the harness skips 'MSDF text' (ts/src/demo/primitives.ts:293-294)

capabilities.evidence: ts/src/input-manager.ts:42-98 (isKeyDown, one pointer, click on pointerup); :47-50 and :240-243 (onKey fires on every keydown, OS auto-repeat included); :205-210 (no keyup callback and no blur/pointercancel listener, so a key held while focus leaves stays down)

capabilities.evidence: git grep -i gamepad over ts/src: 0 files; not in hyperion-masterplan.md
capabilities.note: Shipped by Phaser, Excalibur, Godot and Defold. A team can write it on navigator.getGamepads() in a preTick hook.

capabilities.evidence: ts/src/audio-manager.ts:29-122 (load/loadAll with progress, play/stop, volume, pitch, master volume, positions); ts/src/audio-types.ts:8-15 (playback options are volume, pitch, loop)

capabilities.feature: Music streaming, audio buses/groups, fades, per-sound pause
capabilities.evidence: Every file is fully decoded to an AudioBuffer (ts/src/audio-manager.ts:33, ts/src/sound-registry.ts:23-24). The graph is one master GainNode plus a gain per playback (ts/src/playback-engine.ts:14-39). No MediaElement source, crossfade, bus or per-playback pause.

capabilities.feature: 2D physics (Rapier2D: bodies, colliders, joints, character controller, events, queries)
capabilities.evidence: Today PhysicsAPI._init (ts/src/physics-api.ts:130) has no caller, only _initProducer does (ts/src/hyperion.ts:123-124), so events, queries and isGrounded do nothing (physics-api.ts:174-195). The engine always loads the build without physics (ts/src/engine-worker.ts:41, ts/src/worker-bridge.ts:384). Colliders are ball, cuboid and capsule only (crates/hyperion-core/src/physics.rs:801-822). Gravity is (0, +980) 'down in pixel coordinates' with length_unit 100 (physics.rs:297-306). engine_physics_configure (crates/hyperion-core/src/lib.rs:569) has no TS caller.
capabilities.note: This status assumes step 8b lands as scoped: events, queries and isGrounded wired in every mode, plus a way to load the physics build (round plan :106). Still missing after that: polygon, polyline and heightfield colliders, one-way platforms, and a gravity setter. Gravity points +y while the default camera is y-up, and physics has never run in the browser harness. Peers: Phaser Arcade/Matter, Excalibur and Godot built-in, Defold Box2D; PixiJS none. Once wired, Rapier (CCD, joints, character controller) in the same WASM as the ECS is a quality edge.

capabilities.evidence: ts/src/particle-types.ts:12-22 (rate, lifetime, velocity range, start/end colour and size, gravity); ts/src/particle-system.ts:113-121 (fixed alpha blend) and :166-244 (create/destroy only, no burst or runtime update); ts/src/renderer.ts:1116-1141 (drawn on the swapchain after everything; a Map of every entity's position is rebuilt each frame while any emitter exists); ts/src/hyperion.ts:845-848 (returns null in Mode A)

capabilities.feature: 2D lighting with SDF soft shadows and light layers
capabilities.evidence: Light types point/spot/directional/global/sprite (ts/src/entity-handle.ts:117; the sprite cookie landed in step 8, commit 95800b3). Soft shadows marched on a signed SDF (ts/src/shaders/light-accum.wgsl:300,367,409). Light layers in one graph node (ts/src/render/passes/light-groups-pass.ts:52). Only quads and gradients receive light (ts/src/render/primitive-shaders.ts:37-42). No normal maps (git grep: 0; docs/plans/2026-08-04-phase17-lighting-2d-design.md:1074 calls them 'the only table stake excluded').
capabilities.note: AHEAD of Phaser (Light2D with normal maps, no shadows) and of PixiJS, Excalibur and Defold (no built-in lighting); behind Godot only on normal maps. Verified on an Apple M2 Pro (Chrome, Safari) and an AMD iGPU; about 4 ms of frame time at 1080p on the M2 (CLAUDE.md phase table, 17-D). Sprite cookies cannot load in Mode A. Step 8c decides the SDF padding for casters entering from the sun's side of the screen.

capabilities.feature: Post-processing (HDR, bloom, FXAA, tonemap, selection outlines)
