issues.issue: The owner's roadmap ends without a game layer. After Phase 17 and the round, hyperion-masterplan.md schedules nothing a complete 2D game needs: animation, tilemaps, scenes, UI, gamepad/touch, save data, music. Its status is also stale.
issues.gameImpact: A team adopting Hyperion for a complete game must design, build and maintain the whole game framework itself, with no planned convergence. What the masterplan still lists is infrastructure, 3D or demos: a plugin npm registry (§14.6); sized binding arrays, CRDT (spike failed), Memory64 and a WebNN demo (§15); tech demos (§18); Loop-Blinn cubics, stencil clip paths, a WebGL 2 fallback, 3D and TAA (§19); 3D, typographic text, SVG, framework integrations and Electron/Tauri templates (§20).
issues.evidence: hyperion-masterplan.md:3-6 (v1.2, 27 Feb 2026, 'Phase 10c prossima'); :35-37 (a rendering primitive, not a complete game engine); :545, :683, :762 ('Non iniziata' on physics and the 2026 tech integrations, both since done); no lighting/Phase 17 section; :1058-1079 (the last dependency is Phase 10 → Phase 11+); no file under docs/ mentions a Phase 18+ (git grep: 0)
issues.roundFix: No. The round's only masterplan edit is step 10's correction of lines 232/247 (round plan :108). Step 9 refreshes CLAUDE.md and the docs. The only work scheduled after the round is the WebKit audio step (round plan :83-87).
issues.workaround: Write a post-round roadmap with a game-readiness track (order in missingForCompleteGame), or build the game layer as TS plugins on top of the engine fixes in roadmap-2..4.

issues.issue: No sprite sheets or texture atlases. A quad always samples its whole texture layer, so frame animation needs one texture per frame.
issues.gameImpact: Character, enemy and VFX animation, the core of an action-adventure or platformer, cannot use standard sprite-sheet or atlas assets (TexturePacker, Aseprite). Swapping a texture per frame burns through 255 layers per tier, and they can never be freed.
issues.evidence: ts/src/shaders/primitives/quad.wgsl:5-7 and prelude.wgsl:142-145 (uv = the full quad); ts/src/prim-params-schema.ts:31 (the quad's 8 primParams slots are unused); no setter on EntityHandle or RawAPI (ts/src/entity-handle.ts:537-571, ts/src/raw-api.ts:47-82); ts/src/texture-manager.ts:7,733-740 (255 per tier)
issues.roundFix: No. Step 8 only makes images upright (ts/src/shaders/primitives/prelude.wgsl:191-198). Its plan puts texture unloading, tier mips and the MSDF atlas-rect convention out of scope (docs/plans/2026-10-14-step8-sprite-light-plan.md:48).
issues.workaround: Engine work: a UV rect (and frame index) in the quad's free primParams slots, a public setter, and quad.wgsl reading it. An unsupported stopgap is recompileShader('quad', …) plus private producer access. Then an animation layer in TS.

issues.issue: The texture pipeline caps and distorts art. Every PNG/JPEG is resized to a square of at most 512 px, sampled linearly at LOD 0 only, limited to 255 textures per tier per session, and never unloaded.
issues.gameImpact: HD backgrounds and large tilesets lose resolution. Non-square art is stretched unless the entity's scale restores the aspect. Pixel art is blurred twice: a high-quality resize up to the tier size, then linear filtering. Zoomed-out sprites alias because mips are never sampled. A game with many levels runs out of layers, because nothing frees them.
issues.evidence: ts/src/texture-manager.ts:5 (tier sizes 64-512), :684-701 (resizeWidth = resizeHeight = tier size), :216-219 (only a linear sampler), :7 and :733-740 (throws when a tier is full), :882 (destroy() is the only release); ts/src/shaders/primitives/prelude.wgsl:151-167 (textureSampleLevel at 0.0); ts/src/hyperion.ts:545-561 (the loadTexture JSDoc states the resize and the cap)
issues.roundFix: No. Step 8's plan lists texture unloading, textures in Mode A and tier mips as out of scope (docs/plans/2026-10-14-step8-sprite-light-plan.md:48), and no later step owns them. Masterplan §15.2, sized binding arrays (hyperion-masterplan.md:718-726), would remove the tiers, but it depends on browsers and exists only as a design artifact (ts/src/shaders/basic-binding-array.wgsl).
issues.workaround: Slice large images into square tiles of at most 512 px by hand, pre-scale pixel art to the tier size with nearest-neighbour, and keep the total under 4×255 textures. Otherwise, engine work on TextureManager: sizes, aspect, a sampler choice, mip generation and a free list of layers.

issues.issue: There is no per-sprite tint, alpha, visibility or flip, and a mirrored sprite (scale(-1, 1)) silently disappears.
issues.gameImpact: Facing left and right (the most common platformer operation), hit flashes, fades, damage blinking, and invisible triggers and walls all need workarounds: duplicated mirrored or tinted textures (against the 255 cap), despawn/respawn, or zero scale. A mirrored sprite is still culled, picked and simulated, so the failure is silent.
issues.evidence: crates/hyperion-core/src/ring_buffer.rs:35-119 (no colour, alpha or visibility command); crates/hyperion-core/src/command_processor.rs:530-544 (every spawn is a drawn quad plus Active, and nothing clears Active); ts/src/render/passes/forward-pass.ts:271,285, occluder-seed-stage.ts:96 and selection-seed-pass.ts:107 (cullMode 'back'); no tint/opacity/flip/visible API in ts/src (git grep: 0)
issues.roundFix: No. The mirrored-quad defect is registered (round plan :72, §4 point (1b)) and explicitly not fixed by step 8 (step-8 plan :48). Tint, alpha and visibility appear nowhere in the round.
issues.workaround: Engine work: cullMode 'none' for the 2D pipelines (with a rule for 3D back faces), a colour/alpha multiplier (in the free quad primParams or a new SoA column), and a visibility command that drops the entity's GPU row.

issues.issue: Input has no gamepad, no multi-touch, and fragile keyboard handling.
issues.gameImpact: A game with gamepad and touch controls must write its own input layer. With the built-in one, keys stick when the window loses focus, onKey fires on auto-repeat (a held jump key re-triggers), and touch drags can scroll the page.
issues.evidence: ts/src/input-manager.ts:15-18 (one pointer), :47-50 and :240-243 (no e.repeat check), :205-210 (only keydown/keyup/pointermove/pointerdown/pointerup/wheel; no blur, pointercancel or gamepad); no touch-action anywhere (git grep: 0); the keyboard listens on the canvas (ts/src/hyperion.ts:220)
issues.roundFix: No round step touches input. Gamepad and multi-touch are not in the masterplan either, and its PluginInputAPI (hyperion-masterplan.md:652) was never built (ts/src/plugin-context.ts:89-95).
issues.workaround: A TS input module built on navigator.getGamepads() and Pointer Events with pointerId, plus window blur handling and an action map. This needs no engine changes.

issues.issue: No UI/HUD layer and no production text. MSDF text is a stub that has never been drawn on a GPU.
issues.gameImpact: HUD, menus, dialogue, inventory and damage numbers must be DOM overlays (mapped from world to screen by hand) or an engine extension. In-canvas text is single-line, has no public setter, and has never been verified.
issues.evidence: ts/src/text/text-manager.ts:17-23; ts/src/text/text-layout.ts:14-51; ts/src/prefab/registry.ts:130-136; ts/src/demo/primitives.ts:293-294; ts/src/renderer.ts:1116-1141 (particles drawn over everything); hyperion-masterplan.md:35 (not a UI framework); ts/src/input-manager.ts:189-211 (keyboard needs canvas focus)
issues.roundFix: No. Typographic text is a masterplan 2027+ item (hyperion-masterplan.md:961). Stencil clip paths, needed for UI masking, are 'Phase 11+' (:944). Neither is scheduled.
issues.workaround: DOM/CSS UI and DOM text over the canvas, with keyboard listeners moved to the window. For in-world text, finish TextManager: upload the atlas, add multi-line layout and a text API.

issues.issue: No scenes, level loading, tilemaps or level format.
issues.gameImpact: Many levels mean a hand-written level loader. It must spawn one entity per tile (one texture layer per tile type) and one cuboid entity per collision box, destroy every handle at each level switch, and live with textures that never unload.
issues.evidence: ts/src/prefab/types.ts:12-37 (one level of children; no body, collider or light fields); no tilemap or scene code (git grep: 0); crates/hyperion-core/src/lib.rs:808-878 (reset and snapshot only with dev-tools)
issues.roundFix: No, and not in the masterplan either.
issues.workaround: A TS scene manager and a Tiled/LDtk importer as plugins, once roadmap-2/3 make tilesets usable.

issues.issue: Physics will not work out of the box even after step 8b. There are only three collider shapes. Gravity is fixed at (0, +980) in y-down pixel units, against a y-up, 20-unit default camera, and TS has no way to change it. Physics has never run in the browser.
issues.gameImpact: Bodies fall up the screen and leave the 20-unit view in a fraction of a second. Avoiding that requires gravityScale(-1) and characterUp(0, 1) on every body and re-scaling the camera. Slopes, one-way platforms and polygon terrain need many boxes or engine work.
issues.evidence: crates/hyperion-core/src/physics.rs:297-306 (gravity 980 'down in pixel coordinates', length_unit 100) and :801-822 (ball, cuboid, capsule); crates/hyperion-core/src/lib.rs:569 (engine_physics_configure, no TS caller); ts/src/hyperion.ts:614-617 (20-unit view); ts/src/physics-api.ts:130 (_init never called); ts/src/engine-worker.ts:41 (the build without physics)
issues.roundFix: Partly. Step 8b (round plan :106) wires collision events, raycast, queryAABB/queryCircle and isGrounded in every mode. It decides how apps get the physics build and whether the collider-generation fix goes in. It says nothing about shapes, gravity or units: the round plan never mentions gravity or configure.
issues.workaround: Expose engine_physics_configure through PhysicsAPI (a small change). Add polygon/polyline shapes, which need the payload split already used for joints. Meanwhile use gravityScale per body.

issues.issue: The default execution mode on Chromium and Electron (Mode A) cannot run a game.
issues.gameImpact: With preferredMode 'auto', a Chrome or Electron build shows a fixed view. Camera moves never reach the render worker, loadTexture throws, and particles, bloom and outlines are unavailable.
issues.evidence: ts/src/capabilities.ts:48-49 and ts/src/types.ts:128; ts/src/render-worker.ts:18,41,54-66; ts/src/hyperion.ts:562-565,791,813,847; hyperion-masterplan.md:45 (desktop embedding means 'sempre Mode A')
issues.roundFix: Partly. Step 10 fixes the empty-world freeze and forwards device loss from the worker (round plan :108). Textures in Mode A are a declared limitation of step 8 (round plan :70). Camera sync and particles are in no step.
issues.workaround: Set preferredMode: 'B'. It keeps the ECS worker, and the harness defaults to B for this reason.

issues.issue: No recovery from GPU device loss.
issues.gameImpact: A driver reset, a GPU switch or a mobile background eviction leaves a black canvas. The player loses the session unless the game reloads the page and restores its own save.
issues.evidence: ts/src/renderer.ts:270-273; ts/src/renderer.ts:285 (retainBitmaps never enabled); hyperion-masterplan.md:232,247 (claimed as done) and :986 (risk table: 'fallback page reload')
issues.roundFix: Partly. Step 10 forwards the event to config.onDeviceLost in Mode A and corrects the masterplan lines (round plan :108). Recovery itself is in no step.
issues.workaround: On onDeviceLost, save state and reload the page. Later, rebuild the renderer and re-upload textures from retained bitmaps.

issues.issue: WebGPU only, with no WebGL 2 fallback, and never run on mobile, Firefox, Electron or Tauri.
issues.gameImpact: A web release excludes every browser and device without WebGPU; the masterplan's own risk table names Safari mobile. The platforms games ship on most, phones and Steam through Electron, are unverified.
issues.evidence: No WebGL code (git grep: 0); ts/src/hyperion.ts:210-217 (renderer null without WebGPU); hyperion-masterplan.md:945 (WebGL 2 fallback 'Phase 11+') and :983; Firefox checked only offline with naga (docs/plans/2026-09-27-transparent-sort-uber-design.md:658); no Electron/Tauri file or run (git: 0)
issues.roundFix: No. Step 9 runs Chrome and Safari in Modes B/C/A on the Mac, with Fedora B/C later (round plan :109). Nothing covers mobile, Firefox or desktop shells.
issues.workaround: Target desktop Chrome/Edge, Safari 26+ and Electron (forcing Mode B), and test on devices early.

issues.issue: Not packaged for use from another project.
issues.gameImpact: Testing it in a practical project means copying the engine's source tree, its Vite config and its WASM outputs into the game repo, and tracking upstream by hand.
issues.evidence: ts/package.json:1-5 (private, 0.1.0, no main/exports/types); ts/vite.config.ts:19-21; ts/src/engine-worker.ts:41 and ts/src/worker-bridge.ts:384 (relative ../wasm import)
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: A library build (Vite lib mode, or tsc plus the copied WASM), an exports map, a configurable WASM URL and a physics-build option. The last overlaps step 8b's decision 2.

issues.issue: No save/persistence, and almost no state readback in production.
issues.gameImpact: Save games must be built entirely in TS from the game's own state, because a production build cannot serialise the engine's world. Reading one entity's position means scanning entityIds every frame.
issues.evidence: crates/hyperion-core/src/lib.rs:808-878 (snapshot, restore and hash only with dev-tools); ts/src/system-views.ts:10-16 (slot-indexed views, no velocity or physics); no position getter on EntityHandle (ts/src/entity-handle.ts:313-970); the linear-scan pattern at ts/src/debug/ecs-inspector.ts:141-142
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: Keep the authoritative game state in TS and respawn from it. Build an id-to-slot map each frame from views.entityIds.

issues.issue: Audio has no path for music: every file is fully decoded, and there are no buses, fades or per-sound pause.
issues.gameImpact: Long music tracks cost tens of MB of decoded PCM and start only after a full download and decode. Separate music/SFX volume settings and crossfades must be written outside AudioManager.
issues.evidence: ts/src/audio-manager.ts:33; ts/src/sound-registry.ts:23-24; ts/src/audio-types.ts:8-15; ts/src/playback-engine.ts:14-39
issues.roundFix: Partly. The WebKit audio step after the round makes suspend() resolve and adds audio.state and a first-gesture unlock hook (round plan :83-87). Streaming, buses and fades: no.
issues.workaround: A music player on HTMLAudioElement/MediaElementAudioSourceNode, plus gain groups, next to AudioManager.

issues.issue: Game-loop control is minimal and fragile: a fixed 60 Hz step with no interpolation, no time scale, a pause that also freezes rendering, and a single exception that stops the engine for good. Game logic cannot run inside the WASM.
issues.gameImpact: Scrolling judders on 144 Hz displays. Slow motion and hit-stop need workarounds. An in-canvas pause screen cannot render while paused. One uncaught error during rendering ends the session silently. Custom ECS systems need a fork of the Rust crate.
issues.evidence: crates/hyperion-core/src/engine.rs:19,207-216; ts/src/game-loop.ts:166-176; ts/src/hyperion.ts:598-601,862-908; hyperion-masterplan.md:627-633 (the Rust core is closed to plugins)
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: Keep the engine running and pause gameplay in TS, with a DOM pause menu. Wrap risky hook code in try/catch. Interpolation and tick isolation need engine work.

issues.issue: Particles are untextured circles with continuous emission only, drawn over everything, and absent in Mode A.
issues.gameImpact: Sparks, smoke, dust and hit effects need textured, burst-emitted particles with a choice of blend mode, drawn in the scene's depth and light order. Here particles overdraw the HUD and cannot be lit.
issues.evidence: ts/src/particle-types.ts:12-22; ts/src/particle-system.ts:113-121,166-244; ts/src/renderer.ts:1116-1141 (which also rebuilds a Map of every entity's position each frame while any emitter exists); ts/src/hyperion.ts:845-848
issues.roundFix: No.
issues.workaround: Use transparent quad entities as particles (moved by the ECS velocity system), limited by roadmap-3/4: no alpha fade and the texture cap.

issues.issue: The camera API is bare: no follow, bounds, shake, rotation or second camera, and resize() resets the view.
issues.gameImpact: Follow and shake are easy TS code. A minimap or split screen needs engine work, because each frame has one camera. A custom world scale is lost on every resize.
issues.evidence: ts/src/camera-api.ts:15-46; ts/src/hyperion.ts:614-617; round plan :192 (zoom() drops near/far; listed for step 9)
issues.roundFix: No. The zoom near/far loss is only listed for step 9 (round plan :192), with no decided fix.
issues.workaround: Camera helpers in a preTick hook; call setOrthographic again after every resize.

issues.issue: The masterplan lists features as delivered that do not exist, and some shipped features do nothing.
issues.gameImpact: A team planning from the masterplan would count on AudioWorklet audio, GPU picking, line caps and joins, LUT gradients, MSDF atlas management, measured mobile performance and device-loss recovery. None of these exists. Texture streaming, commandBufferSize and enablePostProcessing do nothing.
issues.evidence: hyperion-masterplan.md:325 and :328-330 (Color-ID picking, AudioWorklet, a separate audio crate; no 'audioworklet' or 'color id' in ts/src, and crates/ holds only hyperion-core and two spikes); :261-264 (MSDF shelf packing and LRU; text-manager.ts:17-23 is a stub); :275 and :280 (caps/joins and a 1D LUT: 0 matches in line.wgsl and gradient.wgsl); :314 (20k on mobile validated: no mobile evidence); :232, :247; texture-streaming.ts imported by no non-test module; ts/src/types.ts:125 vs ts/src/worker-bridge.ts:12,97,211,386 (commandBufferSize is ignored); ts/src/hyperion.ts:683-687 (stub)
issues.roundFix: Partly. Step 10 fixes masterplan lines 232/247. Step 9's claude-md-auditor covers CLAUDE.md (round plan :199 already records the texture-streaming drift), but not these masterplan claims.
issues.workaround: Check the masterplan's Part II against the code before planning on it.

issues.issue: If Mode A fails after the canvas has been transferred, the fallback mode runs with a blank canvas and no error.
issues.gameImpact: On a machine where WebGPU fails in the worker, players see nothing and the console says nothing about the renderer.
issues.evidence: ts/src/worker-bridge.ts:223 (transferControlToOffscreen at bridge creation); ts/src/hyperion.ts:195-200 (fallback) and :211-216 (a createRenderer failure swallowed by catch { renderer = null; })
issues.roundFix: No. It is not in the round plan; step 10 touches other Mode A paths.
issues.workaround: preferredMode: 'B'.

issues.issue: Lighting has gaps a lit action game will notice: no normal maps, only quads and gradients receive light, particles are unlit, and a sun's caster can pop its full shadow in at the screen edge on the sun's side.
issues.gameImpact: Lit sprites look flat next to Godot's or Phaser's normal-mapped lighting. Text, lines and particles never react to light. A directional shadow can appear all at once when its caster scrolls in.
issues.evidence: ts/src/render/primitive-shaders.ts:37-42; docs/plans/2026-08-04-phase17-lighting-2d-design.md:1074 and :1119 (normal maps excluded, still an open question) and :1117 (the edge pop measured at 0.9995 over the whole view width at range 100)
issues.roundFix: Partly. Step 8 adds sprite (cookie) lights. Step 8c decides the SDF padding and stops off-screen point/spot marches at the SDF exit (round plan :107). Normal maps and other receiver types: no.
issues.workaround: Design the art for flat lighting, and keep the casters of shadowed suns inside the view.

surveys.afterRound:
This is the state after steps 8, 8b, 8c, 10 and 9 and the WebKit audio step, as scoped in the round plan §2-§3.

- **Step 8:** sprite lights with a texture cookie (already on this branch: 95800b3); upright images for every textured primitive (ts/src/shaders/primitives/prelude.wgsl:191-198); a dev warning for a sprite light without a texture; shadowed lights that cannot draw open no SDF set.
- **Step 8b:** PhysicsAPI connected to the WASM in every mode: collision, sensor and contact-force events, raycast, queryAABB/queryCircle and isGrounded. Apps get a way to load the physics build and the harness gets a check on it. The query shape in Modes A/B is decided at the step's start.
- **Step 8c:** the SDF-padding decision, implemented only if the measurement justifies it, plus point and spot marches that stop at the SDF exit.
- **Step 10:** Mode A shows an empty world and forwards device loss to config.onDeviceLost. The masterplan's device-lost lines are corrected.
- **Step 9:** docs and CLAUDE.md refreshed, an adversarial review of steps 6-10, preflight --full, and GPU checks in Chrome and Safari (Modes B, C and A) on the Mac.
- **WebKit audio step:** suspend() resolves before the first gesture, a first-gesture unlock hook, and audio.state.

What changes for a game team: the lighting feature set is complete and verified on two GPUs, physics becomes reachable from TS for the first time, and three silent failures close (the unwired physics API, Mode A's empty-world freeze and device-loss forwarding, and WebKit audio).

None of roadmap-2..7 or roadmap-11..16 changes. There are still no sprite frames, tint, alpha, visibility or flip, and the same 512-px square, linear-only, never-unloaded textures. Input is still keyboard and mouse only. There is still no UI, scene, tilemap, save or music support. Mode A still cannot move the camera or load a texture, device loss is not recovered, rendering is WebGPU-only, and the engine is not packaged. Physics still has three shapes and a y-down gravity that TS cannot set.

Readiness after the round: a strong, verified 2D rendering and simulation core for desktop Chrome, Edge and Safari in Mode B or C. It fits tech demos, lighting and physics prototypes, and a small game with few textures that are not pixel art, using a DOM UI. It is not ready for a complete complex 2D game: that first needs engine-level sprite, texture, input and physics-configuration work, then a game-framework layer that no roadmap plans.
missingForCompleteGame: 1. Packaging (not in the masterplan; §14.6 covers plugin packages only): an npm library build with exports, a configurable WASM URL and a selectable physics build. This is the prerequisite for using the engine in a real project.

2. Sprite essentials in the engine (planned nowhere): atlas/sprite-sheet UV rects; per-sprite tint and alpha; a visibility toggle; mirroring that does not make the sprite vanish (cullMode); nearest filtering; non-square textures larger than 512 px; texture unload and layer reuse; mip sampling.

3. Input completion (not planned; the masterplan's PluginInputAPI was never built): gamepad; multi-touch with pointerId; pointercancel and window-blur handling; just-pressed/just-released state; action mapping and rebinding; touch-action on the canvas.
4. Physics for platformers (not planned beyond 8b's wiring): gravity and unit configuration from TS, consistent with the y-up camera; polygon, polyline and heightfield colliders; one-way platforms.
5. Game-loop robustness (not planned): isolating exceptions in the tick, render interpolation or a configurable tick rate, a time scale, and pausing gameplay and physics while still rendering.
6. Sprite animation and tweening (not in the masterplan): frame sequences, Aseprite/TexturePacker import, tweens, timers.
7. Tilemaps and level loading (not in the masterplan): Tiled/LDtk import, tile rendering from atlases, collision generation, and a scene/level manager with load, unload and transitions.

8. A UI/HUD strategy (a UI framework is excluded by masterplan §1.3): either DOM-overlay helpers with world-to-screen anchoring and focus handling, or an in-canvas screen-space layer. Plus production text: a finished MSDF TextManager, multi-line layout, a public text API and glyph coverage for localisation. Typographic text is only a 2027+ masterplan item.
9. Save/load (not in the masterplan): either production-safe world serialisation or documented TS-side ownership of state, plus an id-to-slot lookup and component readback.
10. Audio for games (not planned beyond the WebKit step): music streaming, buses/groups, fades, per-sound pause, audio sprites.
11. Camera features (not planned): follow, deadzone, bounds, shake, rotation, and multiple cameras or viewports (minimap, split screen).
12. Particles for VFX (not planned): textured particles, bursts, blend modes, runtime emitter updates, drawing in scene order, and particles in Mode A.
13. Device-loss recovery with texture re-upload. The masterplan claims it is done (hyperion-masterplan.md:232,247); only forwarding is scheduled (step 10).
14. Mode A parity (camera sync, textures, particles, post-processing in the render worker), or a default mode for games that avoids Mode A (not planned).

15. Platform reach: the WebGL 2 fallback (masterplan §19, 'Phase 11+', not started); mobile device testing and performance (the masterplan §22 targets were never measured); Electron/Tauri templates (masterplan §20, 2027+).
16. Lighting polish (Phase 17 design §15/§17, not scheduled): normal maps, and light on more primitive types.
17. Optional for this genre: networking (the Loro spike failed and nothing is planned), editor integration (Hyperion is not an editor by design), and localisation and accessibility hooks.
surveys.summary:
The roadmap stops at the open-items round. hyperion-masterplan.md (v1.2, status as of 27 Feb 2026) has no Phase 17 or later. Its future sections cover infrastructure (plugin registry, binding arrays, Memory64, WebNN), demos, 3D and a WebGL 2 fallback, and it defines Hyperion as a rendering primitive, not a game engine. No document under docs/ mentions a Phase 18 or later.

After the round, the engine is a strong, verified 2D rendering and simulation core for desktop Chrome, Edge and Safari in Mode B or C. The round adds:
- step 8: sprite lights and upright textures;
- step 8b: the physics API connected to the WASM;
- step 8c: the SDF-padding decision;
- step 10: Mode A empty world and device-loss forwarding;
- step 9: close-out;
- then the WebKit audio fix.

Hyperion is ahead of Phaser, PixiJS, Excalibur, Defold and Godot's web export in five areas:
- GPU-driven scale: compute culling, 100k entities, GPU transparent sort.
- 2D lighting with SDF soft shadows and light layers; only Godot is comparable, and it adds normal maps.
- Multi-threaded ECS with Rapier in a single WASM.
- Deterministic replay and time-travel, in dev builds.
- Per-pass GPU profiling and GPU-validated shader hot reload.

Against what those engines give a team out of the box, Hyperion is missing sprite animation and atlases, tilemaps, scenes, UI, gamepad and touch, save data, music, an editor, a WebGL fallback and npm packaging.

Four engine-level gaps make sprite-heavy games impractical:
- no atlas UVs;
- a texture pipeline that resizes everything to squares of at most 512 px, samples linearly only and never unloads;
- no per-sprite tint, alpha or visibility;
- mirrored sprites that vanish.

The round fixes none of these, and the masterplan does not plan them. Three more problems remain:
- Mode A, which 'auto' picks on Chrome and Electron, still cannot move the camera or load textures.
- Device loss is not recovered.
- The engine has never run on mobile, Firefox or a desktop shell.

Verdict: not ready for a complete complex 2D game. It is usable for a prototype only by forcing Mode B, using a DOM UI and few textures that are not pixel art.

A realistic path:
1. Package it.
2. Fix the sprite, texture, input, physics-configuration and loop gaps in the engine.
3. Build animation, tilemap, scene, UI, save, camera and audio layers as TS plugins.
4. Add device-loss recovery, Mode A parity, and decide on WebGL 2, mobile and Electron.

decisive.issue: The texture model cannot hold a complete game's art: each image is one whole layer of a square tier array (64/128/256/512 px; resized to that square; anything larger shrunk to 512), quads have no UV sub-rectangle (no atlas, no sprite sheet), each array holds 255 images, and nothing is ever unloaded.
decisive.gameImpact: Every animation frame, tile and UI piece costs a layer: about 1020 PNG/JPEG images per session over the four arrays (on BC7/ASTC desktops all PNGs share the four rgba8 overflow arrays), shared by every level, with no way to free a finished level's art. Sheets from Aseprite/TexturePacker/Tiled are unusable as is, backgrounds wider than 512 px must be cut into tiles or are downscaled, non-square art is resampled twice. A load at the cap reallocates and copies the whole array (about 341 MiB on tier 3) before it throws 'is full'.
decisive.evidence: quad.wgsl:5-7; prim-params-schema.ts:32; texture-manager.ts:5-7, :684-702, :706-760 (throw after ensureOverflowCapacity/ensureTierCapacity), :349-433 and :442-536 (realloc + copy + destroy), :191 (cache never evicted), :715, :741; no unload method in TextureManager; hyperion.ts:675-680 (compact() calls a non-existent shrinkUnusedTiers); demo/lighting-sprite.ts:14-18, :552-553 (the harness must reload the page at the cap); docs/plans/hyperion-engine-design-v3.md:500-509 (arrays chosen over atlases).
decisive.roundFix: Not fixed. The step-8 plan lists texture unloading and tier mips out of step (docs/plans/2026-10-14-step8-sprite-light-plan.md:48); 8b, 8c, 10 and 9 do not touch the texture manager. The realloc-before-throw at the cap is only recorded for step 9 with a candidate fix (step-8 plan :4482, note (3)); the masterplan has no atlas or unload item.
decisive.workaround: Slice sheets at runtime (canvas → blob: URL → loadTexture, which accepts blob:/data: URLs) at one layer per frame, budget layers per tier and per level, or destroy() and re-create the engine between level sets. Engine fix: a UV rect for quads in primParams (slots unused today), a layer free-list/unload API, larger or non-square tiers.

decisive.issue: Mirrored sprites disappear: a negative x or y scale (scale(-1, 1), the usual way to face a character left) reverses the unit quad's winding, and every entity pipeline culls back faces.
decisive.gameImpact: A flipped character, enemy or prop is not drawn, casts no shadow and gets no outline, while the cull still counts it and picking still hits it. Every left/right-facing sprite of a platformer or action-adventure would need a pre-flipped copy of each frame, doubling its layer use under rendering-1's cap.
decisive.evidence: forward-pass.ts:271, :285 (cullMode 'back', uber and opaque pipelines); render/passes/occluder-seed-stage.ts:96; render/passes/selection-seed-pass.ts:107; CCW unit quad forward-pass.ts:156-168; only the light pipeline uses cullMode 'none' (render/passes/light-accum-stage.ts:164-166); verified on the device per the round plan's step-8 sub-decision 2 (docs/plans/2026-09-27-open-items-round-plan.md:73, 'una scala negativa lo fa scartare'); step-8 plan :4482 note (1b).
decisive.roundFix: Not fixed. Step 8 explicitly leaves it (step-8 plan :48); it is recorded for step 9 as point (1b) with a candidate fix (cullMode 'none' in the four pipeline families), 'da decidere col proprietario'. Step 9 is a close-out (docs, reviews, GPU legs) and does not commit to it.
decisive.workaround: Set cullMode to 'none' in those four pipelines (the recorded analysis says no pixel changes without a mirroring transform) — a few lines of engine work — or ship pre-flipped textures.

decisive.issue: No per-sprite colour, tint, opacity or visibility: a quad draws exactly its texel (white when untextured), lines and beziers are white or textured, gradients are always opaque, and the protocol has no colour, alpha or visibility command.
decisive.gameImpact: Hit flashes, fade in/out, team or palette colours, darkening, ghost trails, invulnerability blinking and hiding pooled sprites need baked texture variants (more layers) or extra entities.
decisive.evidence: quad.wgsl:11-17; line.wgsl:119; bezier.wgsl:139; gradient.wgsl:49; ring-buffer.ts:15-93 (CommandType list); entity-handle.ts:354-563 (no tint/opacity/visible method).
decisive.roundFix: None: not in the round nor in the masterplan.
decisive.workaround: Texture variants; box shadows (rgba primParams, blur 0) as translucent coloured rectangles for screen fades; a sprite on its own light layer tinted by a masked global light (needs the lit graph, at most 16 layers); scale(0, 0) or off-screen to hide.

decisive.issue: Text has no working path: the MSDF glyph shader exists, but TextManager is a placeholder and unexported, layoutText handles one line with no wrapping, newlines, kerning or alignment, no EntityHandle method sets glyph parameters, and MSDF has never been checked on a GPU.
decisive.gameImpact: HUD counters, menus, dialogue, damage numbers and localisation have no in-engine route; each glyph would be a hand-configured entity, the atlas is resized to a ≤512-px square at load, and the AA parameter appears to behave as a UV-unit range rather than the screen pixels it is named for (code reading, unverified).
decisive.evidence: text/text-manager.ts:17-20 (bitmap closed, textureLayer = 0 placeholder); index.ts:17-20; text/text-layout.ts:13-50; prefab/registry.ts:126-137 (only public route to SDFGlyph primParams, via the private producer); msdf-text.wgsl:12-26, :46-52; demo/primitives.ts:293-294 ('MSDF text' skipped: no font atlas); no font asset in the repo; hyperion-masterplan.md:261-264, :309 claim shelf packing, LRU and zoom validation.
decisive.roundFix: None; the MSDF atlas-rect convention is out of step 8 (step-8 plan :48).
decisive.workaround: DOM/CSS overlay for HUD, menus and dialogue (project world anchors with cam.viewProjection each frame); or a glyph layer on prefabs with an offline msdf-atlas-gen atlas of at most 512 px, validated on a GPU first.

decisive.issue: No mipmaps, one linear sampler, and FXAA that cannot be switched off: tiers allocate full mip chains but only mip 0 is written, and every primitive samples LOD 0.
decisive.gameImpact: Sprites drawn smaller than their tier (zoom-out, 512-px art on small sprites) shimmer while moving; pixel art is bilinearly blurred, FXAA-smeared and lit from a half-resolution light buffer; there is no nearest filtering, integer scaling or pixel snapping; unused mips cost about a third more VRAM.
decisive.evidence: texture-manager.ts:216-220, :375-389, :469-483 (mips allocated), :716-720, :742-749, :796-801, :840-845 (mip 0 only); prelude.wgsl:151-171 (textureSampleLevel at LOD 0); fxaa-tonemap.wgsl:107-150; render/passes/light-groups-pass.ts:30, :99.
decisive.roundFix: None; 'mip dei tier' is out of step 8 (step-8 plan :48).
decisive.workaround: Author images at their displayed size and keep zoom near 1; snap camera and sprites to texels in TS; for pixel art, upscale offline with nearest to the tier size; or patch the sampler and the composite.

decisive.issue: No sprite animation, tween or timeline system.
decisive.gameImpact: Frame animation, animation state machines, frame events and eased motion or UI transitions are all game-side code, and frames cannot come from an atlas (rendering-1).
decisive.evidence: No animation/tween/keyframe/timeline code in ts/src or crates/hyperion-core/src (grep hits only requestAnimationFrame); entity-handle.ts:492-496 (`.texture()` is the only lever, SetTextureLayer 9 bytes, ring-buffer.ts:105); hyperion-masterplan.md:33-37 (a rendering primitive, not a complete engine).
decisive.roundFix: None; not in the masterplan either.
decisive.workaround: A TS animator in a preTick hook calling `.texture()` per frame; a JS tween library driving position()/scale()/rotation().

decisive.issue: No tilemap renderer or map import.
decisive.gameImpact: A level is one entity per tile inside the 100 000-entity budget shared with sprites, glyphs and lights; outside Mode C every row is re-uploaded every frame even for a static map (124 B per entity); the fixed 64 KB ring buffer spreads a big level spawn over many frames; RawAPI cannot set depth or transparency; each tile image takes a layer (rendering-1).
decisive.evidence: No tilemap code; types.ts:78; raw-api.ts:52-82; worker-render-state.ts:211-214 and renderer.ts:956-996 (full upload outside Mode C); worker-bridge.ts:12 with types.ts:125 (commandBufferSize never read).
decisive.roundFix: None.
decisive.workaround: EntityHandle per tile with chunked spawn/despawn by camera distance, Mode C for dirty-only scatter uploads, or a plugin RenderPass that draws the map.

decisive.issue: Motion advances only on the fixed 60 Hz tick, without render interpolation, the fixedTimestep config is ignored, and a camera set from hooks lags the drawn state by one update.
decisive.gameImpact: On 120/144/165 Hz displays (ProMotion MacBooks, gaming monitors) entities move in irregular 0/1-tick steps while a TS camera scrolls every frame, so sprites judder against the background; at 60 Hz the accumulator still runs 0 or 2 ticks on some frames; a camera following a physics- or velocity-driven player trails it by one update and jitters when tick counts vary.
decisive.evidence: crates/hyperion-core/src/engine.rs:19 (FIXED_DT const), :197-217, :407-411 (interpolation_alpha, no caller in ts/src or crates); types.ts:127; game-loop.ts:166-172 (preTick sees the previous views, the render runs inside tickFn) with hyperion.ts:876-909.
decisive.roundFix: None; not in the round nor in the masterplan.
decisive.workaround: Drive the camera from positions the game itself commands, or step it on tickCount changes. Real fix is engine work: keep previous transforms and blend by interpolation_alpha before upload.

decisive.issue: Mode A, which preferredMode 'auto' picks on Chrome and Chromium desktop shells, cannot run a content game: no textures, the main-thread camera never reaches the render worker, and particles, bloom, outlines and plugin render passes are unavailable.
decisive.gameImpact: With default config a Chrome/Electron build shows untextured entities through a fixed camera at the origin (20 units tall, zoom 1); sprite lights light nothing; the masterplan names desktop embedding as always Mode A.
decisive.evidence: capabilities.ts:47-55; types.ts:128; hyperion-masterplan.md:45; hyperion.ts:210-217, :564, :791, :813, :847; plugin-context.ts:126-133; render-worker.ts:18, :41, :66; worker-bridge.ts:370-375.
decisive.roundFix: Partly: step 10 renders Mode A's empty world and forwards device loss (round plan §3 row 10). Textures in Mode A are a declared limitation of step 8 (round plan :70, :217); camera sync is scheduled nowhere.
decisive.workaround: Force preferredMode: 'B' (needs COOP/COEP) or 'C'.

decisive.issue: GPU particles are minimal and composited outside the scene: untextured circles from a point emitter at a continuous rate, alpha blend only, drawn on the swapchain after the whole graph (after tonemap, FXAA and bloom), without depth or lighting, and unavailable in Mode A.
decisive.gameImpact: No smoke, sparks, dust or magic sprites, no additive glow, no bursts or one-shots, no emitter shapes; particles always cover every sprite (foreground, in-engine HUD) and ignore lights; destroying an emitter kills its live particles; with any emitter alive the renderer rebuilds a Map of every entity's position each frame. The harness never checks their pixels.
decisive.evidence: particle-render.wgsl:57-66; particle-simulate.wgsl:107; particle-types.ts:12-23; particle-system.ts:296-310; renderer.ts:1116-1142 (Map per frame :1118-1130); hyperion.ts:845-850; demo/particles.ts:48, :104, :117-121 (checks passed with literal true).
decisive.roundFix: None.
decisive.workaround: Sprite particles as transparent entities (sorted and lit, but each an ECS entity and a layer), or a custom plugin pass.

decisive.issue: A lost GPU device is never recovered: the renderer logs and calls config.onDeviceLost; texture bitmaps are not retained and the renderer cannot be rebuilt under a live engine.
decisive.gameImpact: A driver reset, GPU-process crash or sleep/resume leaves a dead canvas; the game must recreate the whole engine, reload every texture and rebuild its world from its own save.
decisive.evidence: renderer.ts:270-273, :285; texture-manager.ts:206-215 (retainBitmaps off by default, no re-upload path); hyperion.ts:73 (renderer readonly); hyperion-masterplan.md:232, :247 (claim transparent recovery).
decisive.roundFix: Step 10 forwards Mode A device loss to config.onDeviceLost and corrects masterplan lines 232 and 247; no recovery is planned.
decisive.workaround: onDeviceLost → destroy() + Hyperion.create(), reload textures, respawn from a game-side save; autosave often.

decisive.issue: With default settings, every Chromium browser (Chrome and Edge on desktop and Android, Opera, Samsung Internet, Electron, WebView2) runs in Mode A as soon as the page is cross-origin isolated, which is exactly the setup the deployment guide prescribes. Mode A cannot run a typical game. loadTexture throws. The render worker's camera never follows engine.cam. Particles, bloom, outlines, selection, plugin rendering (debug overlays, physics wireframes), positionImmediate, GPU profiling and the probe are all unavailable. Until step 10, destroying every entity leaves the last frame on screen and device loss is only logged inside the worker.
decisive.gameImpact: A sprite-based, scrolling game shipped with default settings shows no sprite art, no MSDF text, no sprite-light cookies and a view that never moves. Only untextured shapes and lighting draw. The docs call Mode A optimal, and the masterplan's desktop path is 'always Mode A', yet it cannot be used for a game.
decisive.evidence: capabilities.ts:33-36, :47-55; hyperion.ts:157-159, :176-185. Measured on Chrome macOS: auto picks A (docs/plans/assets/2026-09-29-mac-m2/README.md:113). Gaps: hyperion.ts:562-566, :573-578, :789-815, :773-775, :845-850; plugin-context.ts:113-120. Camera: render-worker.ts:18, :40-41, :65-66, and no camera message in worker-bridge.ts:339-376. Immediate mode: hyperion.ts:893-896 patches the main-thread copy after worker-bridge.ts:303-310 has already forwarded the original. Also worker-render-state.ts:185-216; worker-bridge.ts:272 with render-worker.ts:72 (empty world); render-worker.ts:37 (no onDeviceLost). Harness in A: 17 pass, 42 skip, 4 pending out of 63 (round plan:187). The harness forces B for exactly this reason (ts/src/demo/preferred-mode.ts:5-16).

Step 8 keeps textures out of Mode A as a declared limitation (round plan:70, :105; step-8 plan:22, :48). No step covers camera sync, texture loading in the render worker, particles, post-FX, selection, overlays, immediate mode, or changing auto-selection.
decisive.workaround: Pass preferredMode 'B' (behind COOP/COEP) or 'C' to Hyperion.create, as the harness does.

decisive.issue: There is no working production build. `npm run build` (tsc + vite build) fails with the repo's config: Vite bundles workers as IIFE by default, both workers reach dynamic import() calls, and Rollup refuses to split IIFE output into chunks. No production bundle (`__DEV__` false, minified worker chunks, WASM and transcoder assets) has ever been built and run. The engine is also not a package: ts/package.json is private and has no exports or library build, so a game imports the TS source and has to reproduce the Vite setup (`?raw` WGSL, `new URL(…, import.meta.url)` workers). The WASM flavour is a hardcoded import path, so the physics build in ts/wasm-physics is never loaded.
decisive.gameImpact: The first deploy fails at build time. After the config is fixed, the production path runs for the first time in front of players. A physics game cannot select its WASM without editing engine source.

Dynamic imports: engine-worker.ts:41; basis-transcoder.ts:85-87, reached from render-worker.ts:14 through renderer.ts. The failure is recorded in docs/plans/2026-09-27-transparent-sort-uber-plan.md:9340. scripts/preflight.sh:66-73 never runs vite build. ts/package.json:2-5. Hardcoded WASM: worker-bridge.ts:384, engine-worker.ts:41. Inferred from source; not re-run (read-only).
decisive.roundFix: No. Step 9's criterion is `preflight.sh --full` (round plan:109), which builds the WASM but not the bundle. Step 8b only decides how an app obtains the physics WASM (round plan:106).
decisive.workaround: Set `worker: { format: 'es' }` in the game's Vite config (expected to fix it; unverified), then smoke-test the built bundle in each mode.

decisive.issue: There is no rendering fallback. Without WebGPU, or when createRenderer fails, the engine runs the simulation on a blank canvas, logs nothing, and gives the app no API or event saying rendering is off.
decisive.gameImpact: Players on browsers or devices without WebGPU (about 15% per design 17) see a black canvas unless the game detects this itself. The missing cases listed there: Firefox on Linux, Android and macOS Intel; Chrome Android below 12 or on non-Adreno/Mali/PowerVR GPUs; Windows ARM64; Safari before macOS/iOS 26. Without WebGL these players are lost.
decisive.evidence: hyperion.ts:210-217 (`if (rendererOnMain && caps.webgpu)` … `catch { renderer = null; }`); capabilities.ts:29; renderer.ts:223-224. Masterplan :120 ('Futuro: fallback WebGL 2 o Canvas 2D'), :945 (Phase 11+, not started), :983. PROJECT_ARCHITECTURE.md:1729; deployment-guide.md:508-525; docs/plans/2026-08-04-phase17-lighting-2d-design.md:181.
decisive.roundFix: No.
decisive.workaround: Call navigator.gpu?.requestAdapter() before Hyperion.create and show an unsupported-browser screen. A real fallback means a second renderer, which is large engine work.

decisive.issue: Fault handling contradicts the masterplan's 'the application never dies, it degrades'. In Mode B, Hyperion.create hangs forever if the engine worker posts an error: the ready promise has no reject. No Worker in A or B has an onerror handler, so a worker or WASM load failure also hangs. A Mode A failure after transferControlToOffscreen leaves a canvas that the B and C fallback cannot use; the renderer error is swallowed and the engine reports Mode B over a blank canvas. A throw in render() or a WASM trap stops the main loop for good because tickFn is not isolated; the Mode A render loop is the same. There is no uncapturederror handler and no panic hook. The supervisor only warns, and onModeChange is never called.
decisive.gameImpact: A deploy mistake leaves players on an endless loading screen instead of a Mode C fallback: a wrong .wasm MIME type, a CSP without wasm-unsafe-eval or worker-src, a 404 on a worker chunk. A single runtime exception freezes the game and gives the app no callback to report it or save.
decisive.evidence: worker-bridge.ts:117-120 (resolve only), :131-132 (an 'error' message is only logged). No onerror or 'error' listener in ts/src (grep). worker-bridge.ts:223; hyperion.ts:195-200, :211-216; docs/handoff/2026-09-29-mac-m2-handoff.md:502, :705. game-loop.ts:166-176: tickFn at :169 is outside any try, and rAF is re-armed at :176 only if it returns. render-worker.ts:70-80; engine-worker.ts:68-89. worker-bridge.ts:101-107, :215-221 and supervisor.ts:14-17, :33-46 (warn only). types.ts:14. Masterplan :57, :72, :124, :211 ('[x] Supervisor … degrada A→B→C').
decisive.roundFix: No.
decisive.workaround: Wrap Hyperion.create in an app-side timeout and retry with preferredMode 'C' on a new canvas element. Add window 'error' and 'unhandledrejection' handlers. Never force 'A'.

decisive.issue: Device loss is reported but never recovered. In Modes B and C the renderer logs it and calls onDeviceLost(message); in Mode A it is only logged in the worker. Nothing rebuilds the device, the pipelines or the textures. onDeviceLost also fires on every engine.destroy(), because renderer.destroy() destroys the device and the handler does not check info.reason ('destroyed').
decisive.gameImpact: A GPU reset, driver update, GPU-process crash or mobile background eviction freezes the picture while the simulation keeps running. The app must recover on its own by destroying and recreating Hyperion. That loses the ECS world (production builds have no snapshot), reloads every texture, and in Mode A needs a new <canvas> element. An app that recreates the engine from onDeviceLost will also loop after its own destroy().
decisive.evidence: renderer.ts:270-273 (no reason check), :1200 (device.destroy(), reached from hyperion.ts:648). render-worker.ts:37; worker-bridge.ts:223. crates/hyperion-core/src/lib.rs:808-835 (snapshot and reset only with feature dev-tools). The only test checks that the callback is stored: hyperion.test.ts:422-426. masterplan:232, :247 mark 'device.lost recovery trasparente' as done.
decisive.roundFix: Partly. Step 10 forwards Mode A's loss to config.onDeviceLost and corrects masterplan lines 232 and 247 (round plan:81-82, :108). Recovery and filtering out 'destroyed': no step.
decisive.workaround: Ignore an onDeviceLost call that follows your own destroy(). Otherwise persist game state, then reload the page or recreate the engine on a new canvas and restore from the save.

decisive.issue: Mobile is unverified and the input model is desktop-only. InputManager tracks a single pointer with no pointerId, handles no pointercancel, sets no touch-action, and has no gamepad support. Android Chrome lands in Mode A through the UA guess. The ASTC texture path that most mobile GPUs need has never run, and no mobile device appears in any measurement.
decisive.gameImpact: A touch control scheme (virtual stick plus buttons) cannot read two fingers. When a browser gesture cancels a touch, isPointerDown(0) stays true. Without touch-action:none the page pans and zooms. Mobile performance (the masterplan targets 20k entities at 60 fps) is unknown.
decisive.evidence: input-manager.ts:15-20, :30-37, :84-98, :197-210, :250-267. No getGamepads, pointercancel or touch-action in ts/src (grep). capabilities.ts:34. docs/handoff/2026-09-29-mac-m2-handoff.md:1060 (M11 ASTC skipped). Round plan:75: layer 0 on ASTC decodes to the error colour, 'from the spec, not measured'. Masterplan :41, :1035-1036, :1041-1050.
decisive.roundFix: No. The WebKit audio step after the round adds a first-gesture unlock hook, which helps iOS audio only.
decisive.workaround: Write an app-side pointer layer on the canvas: a pointerId map, pointercancel, setPointerCapture, CSS touch-action:none. Poll navigator.getGamepads() in a preTick hook. Force Mode B or C on Android.

decisive.issue: Desktop embedding exists only as deployment-guide prose, and that prose contradicts the engine. No Electron, Tauri or WebView2 template, build or test exists. The guide says SharedArrayBuffer is available without headers, but the engine requires crossOriginIsolated === true, which the guide's `win.loadFile` recipe (a file:// page) does not establish. Where isolation does hold, Electron and WebView2 get Mode A (their UAs contain 'Chrome/' or 'Edg/'), the mode without textures and the masterplan's 'always Mode A'. Tauri on macOS and Linux (WebKit UA) never gets Mode A. The Tauri JSON uses v1 keys while describing v2, and the guide itself doubts WebGPU in macOS WKWebView. A blank window follows, since there is no fallback.
decisive.gameImpact: The 'desktop app' target is unproven. Following the guide gives Mode C (no isolation) or the texture-less Mode A (isolation), plus first-time integration work: asset base path, WebGPU switches per OS, a custom protocol serving COOP/COEP.
decisive.evidence: deployment-guide.md:276-308, :312-344 (v1 keys at :318-337 against 'Tauri v2' at :342; WKWebView at :343). capabilities.ts:19-25, :33-36; ring-buffer.ts:366. git ls-files has no electron, tauri or webview file. Masterplan :45, :969, :1037. vite.config.ts sets no `base`, and Vite's default emits root-absolute /assets/ URLs that do not resolve under file:// (general Vite behaviour).
decisive.roundFix: No.
decisive.workaround: Electron: serve the build through a privileged custom protocol that adds COOP/COEP, or accept Mode C. Force 'B' or 'C', set Vite `base: './'`, and verify WebGPU on each OS before committing.

decisive.issue: Firefox has never been run. The Phase 17 research says it exposes no optional WebGPU features. Without 'indirect-first-instance', every indirect draw with a non-zero firstInstance is a silent no-op. Among opaque entities only tier-0 quads would then draw, and only they would cast shadows or get outlines. That leaves out opaque lines, MSDF text, beziers, gradients, box shadows, and quads textured from tiers 1-3 or overflow.
decisive.gameImpact: On Firefox (Mode B when isolated) most of a game's opaque art could vanish, with a single console warning. Firefox has no WebGPU at all on Linux, Android and macOS Intel. Unverified: inferred from code plus the design's research.
decisive.evidence: capabilities.ts:31-32, :227 (the feature is requested only if offered), :246-251 (the warning's text). ts/src/shaders/cull.wgsl:99-104 (bucket 1 for tier > 0 or overflow). docs/plans/2026-08-04-phase17-lighting-2d-design.md:178-183, :1066. docs/plans/2026-09-26-cull-temporal-firstinstance-brief.md:11, :32. Firefox coverage so far is the naga CLI only (docs/plans/2026-09-27-transparent-sort-uber-design.md:658, :706).
decisive.roundFix: No. Step 9's GPU legs are Chrome and Safari on the Mac; Fedora Chrome is non-blocking (round plan:109).
decisive.workaround: Mark sprites .transparent() so they go through the sorted uber draw (firstInstance 0), at the cost of the sort and of depth writes; or do not support Firefox.

decisive.issue: Verification covers two machines: one Mac (Chrome 154/155 and Safari 27, Modes B, C, A) and one Linux box running Chrome with WebGPU flags. Windows on D3D12, where most players are, has never run the engine. Neither have Edge, Android, iOS, Firefox or any desktop shell. On Linux, the engine's own diagnostic says stock Chrome needs flags for a hardware adapter.
decisive.gameImpact: Backend- and driver-specific defects would be found by players. Past examples: the subgroup cull that was wrong on AMD, the BC7 tier growth that failed on Metal (M10). Linux players may get no adapter or a software one.
decisive.evidence: docs/plans/assets/2026-09-29-mac-m2/README.md:29-46, :344-411. No Windows or D3D12 run in docs/ (grep). capabilities.ts:193-198. Round plan:109 (step 9: Mac Chrome B/C/A, Safari B/C/A, Fedora B/C at the next session, non-blocking).

decisive.workaround: Run the harness (?mode=B and ?mode=C) on every target platform before committing to it.

decisive.issue: Modes A and B have no tick backpressure and no partial upload. The main thread posts one tick per requestAnimationFrame whether or not the worker has finished the last one. On every tick message, even one that runs no fixed tick, the worker copies all SoA columns into fresh ArrayBuffers, and Mode A copies them again on the main thread. The scatter (dirty-only) upload exists only in Mode C. The main thread also renders the state of an earlier tick, which adds at least one frame of latency.
decisive.gameImpact: When one worker tick costs more than a display frame (8.3 ms at 120 Hz, 4.2 ms at 240 Hz; heavy physics or slow CPUs), tick messages pile up without bound. The displayed state and audio then drift further and further behind real time, while garbage grows with the entity count. Inferred from code; not measured at game scale.
decisive.evidence: game-loop.ts:166-169; worker-bridge.ts:174-177 (B), :342-345 (A). tick-sequencer.ts:9-13 ('a lagging worker handles an older tick'). engine-worker.ts:68-89 (capture after every message); worker-render-state.ts:135-155 (new arrays every tick), :211-214 (no staging). worker-bridge.ts:277-301 (Mode A's second copy). Mode C reads staging at worker-bridge.ts:480-500. Round plan:124 (the scatter upload runs only in Mode C).
decisive.roundFix: No.
decisive.workaround: Use Mode C, or keep the worker's per-tick cost well below the display interval. An app cannot throttle the bridge without engine changes.

decisive.issue: Rendering shows the last fixed 60 Hz tick with no interpolation, and the fixed step cannot be changed. On 120, 144, 165 and 240 Hz displays motion advances in 1/60 s steps, with uneven cadence whenever the refresh rate is not a multiple of 60.
decisive.gameImpact: Visible judder while scrolling and in fast action on gaming monitors and 120 Hz Macs and phones; Chrome on the test M2 runs rAF at 120 Hz. Inferred from code; not measured. This may overlap with a game-loop dimension.
decisive.evidence: crates/hyperion-core/src/engine.rs:19 (FIXED_DT, the constant 1/60), :207-216, :407-410 (interpolation_alpha() never exported or called; grep). types.ts:12 (fixedTimestep has no consumer). README:346.
decisive.roundFix: No.
decisive.workaround: Interpolate app-driven visuals such as the camera on the app side. Sprites driven by the ECS cannot be interpolated without engine work.

decisive.dimension: Gameplay systems and the game-facing API
decisive.issue: No sprite-sheet path. A quad always samples its whole texture layer, with no UV or frame rect and no per-sprite tint or opacity. Texture capacity is per session, square and at most 512 px, and nothing can be unloaded.
decisive.gameImpact: Sprite animation needs one loaded texture per frame. On a BC7/ASTC desktop every PNG/JPEG goes to the rgba8 overflow arrays: 4 × 255 = 1020 images for the whole session (KTX2 can add the primary arrays). Every image is squashed into a 64/128/256/512 square, and nothing can be freed between levels. A multi-level game with animated characters, tilesets and backgrounds exceeds this. Hit flashes, fade-outs and damage tints have no control.
decisive.evidence: quad.wgsl:5-7, :11-13; prim-params-schema.ts:32 ('Quad has no schema'); prelude.wgsl:191-198 (whole-layer sample); shaders read only renderMeta word 1 (cull.wgsl:93, light-accum.wgsl:131, line.wgsl:81), so MeshHandle is inert; texture-manager.ts:5, 7; hyperion.ts:545-561; no unload method in texture-manager.ts
decisive.roundFix: No. Step 8 only makes tier images upright (prelude.wgsl:196). Its plan lists texture unloading and tier mips as out of scope (docs/plans/2026-10-14-step8-sprite-light-plan.md:48), and no later step covers UV rects, tint or unloading.
decisive.workaround: Write a custom sprite-batch pass with the plugin API (ctx.rendering.addPass and ctx.gpu, plugin-context.ts:113-120), with its own atlas, camera, depth and lighting handling. That is a large job. The alternative is one PNG per frame within the cap, re-creating the engine between chapters.

decisive.dimension: Gameplay systems and the game-facing API
decisive.issue: Mirrored sprites disappear. scale(-1, 1), the standard 2D way to make a character face left, reverses the triangle winding, and every entity pipeline culls back faces.
decisive.gameImpact: A character, enemy or projectile flipped to face left is not drawn, casts no shadow and gets no outline. Culling still counts it and picking still hits it.
decisive.evidence: forward-pass.ts:271, 285; occluder-seed-stage.ts:96; selection-seed-pass.ts:107 (cullMode 'back'; no frontFace override anywhere); a det<0 model matrix in unitQuadVertex (prelude.wgsl:142-145) reverses the screen winding; recorded at round plan:72 and step-8 plan:48
decisive.roundFix: No. Step 8 explicitly leaves it (round plan:72). The step-8 plan records the candidate fix (cullMode 'none' in the four pipeline families) as 'da decidere col proprietario', and no step owns it.
decisive.workaround: Load a pre-mirrored copy of every directional texture. This doubles texture use and makes gameplay-1 worse. A y-flipped camera is no escape: it mirrors every quad and culls the whole scene.

decisive.dimension: Gameplay systems and the game-facing API
decisive.issue: Physics is unreachable from a game: PhysicsAPI is never connected to the WASM, and no bridge can load the physics build.
decisive.gameImpact: onCollisionStart/End, onSensorEnter/Exit and onContactForce never fire. raycast returns null, queryAABB/queryCircle return [] and isGrounded is always false, with no warning. Hyperion.create always loads ts/wasm, built without physics-2d, so bodies and colliders are not even simulated.
decisive.evidence: physics-api.ts:130-132 (_init) has no caller; only hyperion.ts:124 (_initProducer) touches the API; physics-api.ts:242, 282, 296, 304, 175, 193; engine-worker.ts:41 and worker-bridge.ts:384 (hard-coded ../wasm/hyperion_core.js); ts/package.json:9 vs :12; physics-api.test.ts covers only the no-WASM path; no physics in ts/src/demo
decisive.roundFix: Yes, step 8b (round plan:106). It brings wiring in every mode, a bridge protocol for events and queries in Modes A/B, a way for apps to get the physics build, and possibly the collider-generation fix. Its exit criteria are tests per mode and a harness check on the physics build. Still open: whether Mode A/B queries are async, synchronous on a one-tick-old snapshot, or Mode C only.
decisive.workaround: None through the public API today. A forked Mode C bridge could load ts/wasm-physics and call physicsApi._init itself.

decisive.dimension: Gameplay systems and the game-facing API
decisive.issue: Physics units and axis convention do not match the renderer, and they cannot be configured from TS.
decisive.gameImpact: With the defaults, a dynamic body accelerates at 980 units/s² toward +y, which is up on screen, in a view 20 units tall. Rapier's tolerances assume 100 units per metre. A character controller's 'up' (-gravity) points down the screen, so ground detection is inverted unless overridden.
decisive.evidence: physics.rs:298-307 (gravity (0, 980) 'down in pixel coordinates', length_unit 100); physics.rs:286-293 (up = -normalize(gravity)); camera.ts:240 (bottom -hh, top +hh: y-up); entity-handle.ts:107 ('the world is y-up'); hyperion.ts:617 (20-unit view); lib.rs:567-577 (engine_physics_configure) has no TS caller; the Rust tests set gravity directly (tests/verify_physics.rs:339)
decisive.roundFix: No. Step 8b's stated scope (round plan:106) is wiring, the A/B protocol, build delivery and the collider-generation fix. Gravity and units are not listed: a physics config option might come with 8b decision (2), but that is not guaranteed.
decisive.workaround: Set gravityScale(-1) on every dynamic body and characterUp(0, 1) on every controller. Pick a world scale where 100 units is about 1 m (setOrthographic in pixel-like units, re-applied after every resize()).

decisive.dimension: Gameplay systems and the game-facing API
decisive.issue: Platformer and action body controls are missing: no velocity set or get, no rotation lock, no one-way platforms, only three collider shapes, and unfiltered raycasts. CCD, torque, angular damping and body/collider removal are not public.
decisive.gameImpact: Jumps and knockback need velocity changes, but only impulses are available and the body's mass is unknown in TS. A dynamic player capsule tips over. One-way platforms are impossible. Tilemaps need a box per tile (no polygon, segment, polyline or heightfield). A ray cast from the player hits the player's own collider and every sensor. Fast bullets tunnel because CCD has no public setter. Rotating kinematic platforms rotate only by teleport.
decisive.evidence: command_processor.rs:763 (SetVelocity writes only the ECS Velocity); systems.rs:75-80 (velocity systems skip PhysicsControlled); no SetVelocity arm in physics_commands.rs; physics.rs:9-15 (no lock flags); no PhysicsHooks or one-way code in crates (git grep: 0); physics.rs:801-822 (ball/cuboid/capsule only); physics.rs:381-387 (QueryFilter::default(), solid ray); backpressure.ts:485-528 (destroyRigidBody, destroyCollider, setAngularDamping, setCCDEnabled, applyTorque) have no EntityHandle or RawAPI method; physics.rs:664-676 (kinematic sync is translation only)
decisive.roundFix: No. 8b wires the existing API, and none of these items is in any step.
decisive.workaround: Tune impulses by trial instead of setting velocity. Call (handle as any)._producer.setCCDEnabled(...), as prefab/registry.ts:132 already does for primParams. Use a box per tile, start rays outside the player's collider, and use a kinematic body with the character controller for the player.

decisive.dimension: Gameplay systems and the game-facing API
decisive.issue: The default mode on Chromium and Electron, Mode A, cannot run a typical game: the camera never moves, textures do not load and particles are unavailable.
decisive.gameImpact: preferredMode 'auto' picks Mode A on every cross-origin-isolated Chromium page, including Chrome, Edge, Electron and WebView2. There the render worker draws with its own camera fixed at the origin, so a scrolling level is impossible. loadTexture throws, createParticleEmitter returns null and selection is null. Picking uses the main-thread camera and a stale canvas size.
decisive.evidence: types.ts:128; capabilities.ts:33-36, 48-49 (isChromium = /Chrome\//); render-worker.ts:18, 41, 66, 73 (no camera message); hyperion.ts:564, 773-775, 847; demo/preferred-mode.ts:5-16 (the harness forces Mode B for this reason); docs/deployment-guide.md:531 (presents Mode A as the automatic choice)
decisive.roundFix: Partly. Step 10 fixes only the empty world and forwards device loss to config.onDeviceLost in Mode A (round plan:108). Textures in Mode A are a declared limitation (round plan:70), and no step syncs the camera.
decisive.workaround: Set preferredMode: 'B' (or 'C'), giving up the separate render worker.

decisive.dimension: Gameplay systems and the game-facing API
decisive.issue: There is no render interpolation and no fixed-rate gameplay hook. The image changes only on 60 Hz simulation ticks, while TS game logic runs once per display frame with variable, unclamped dt.
decisive.gameImpact: Motion is uneven on 144/165 Hz monitors and 75/90/100 Hz displays, which alternate between two and three refreshes per tick. Gameplay code in hooks runs at a different rate from physics, must clamp dt itself after a tab switch, and cannot be deterministic. There is no slow motion or hit-stop (time scale).
decisive.evidence: engine.rs:19 (const FIXED_DT); engine.rs:207-218 (whole ticks only); engine.rs:409-411 (interpolation_alpha, absent from the lib.rs exports); game-loop.ts:139-177 (one hook pass per RAF, raw dt at :146); types.ts:12, 127 (fixedTimestep never read)
decisive.roundFix: No.
decisive.workaround: None for bodies the engine moves. For TS-driven entities, run your own accumulator in a preTick hook and push positions every frame, losing the physics integration.

decisive.dimension: Gameplay systems and the game-facing API
decisive.issue: Input covers only the keyboard, one pointer and the wheel, and has correctness bugs. There is no gamepad, touch/multi-touch or action map. Keys stick when focus is lost, and auto-repeat re-fires key callbacks.
decisive.gameImpact: The use case's gamepad and touch targets need a custom input layer. A key held during alt-tab stays down, so the character keeps running. A jump bound with onKey repeats while the key is held. A button released outside the canvas stays pressed. Once a DOM HUD element takes focus, the game stops receiving keys. Picking at the pointer is wrong on HiDPI screens unless the game multiplies by devicePixelRatio.
decisive.evidence: input-manager.ts:205-210 (canvas listeners for keydown/keyup/pointermove/pointerdown/pointerup/wheel only); input-manager.ts:240-243 then :47-50 (no repeat check); input-manager.ts:15-20 (single pointer state, buttons keyed by button number); input-manager.ts:250-253 (CSS px offsetX/Y); git grep in ts/src for getGamepads, touch-action, pointercancel, pointerId, 'blur', visibilitychange and setPointerCapture: all 0; hyperion.ts:395-398 with camera.ts:283-284 (normalised by the backing store); the harness Input tab only calls hitTest(0, 0) (demo/input.ts:87)
decisive.roundFix: No.
decisive.workaround: Write an input layer on the Gamepad API and Pointer Events: window-level listeners, a blur reset, edge detection and an action map. Pass DPR-scaled coordinates to picking.hitTest.

decisive.dimension: Gameplay systems and the game-facing API
decisive.issue: There is no level lifecycle: no way to clear the world, no cascade destroy, a compact() that does nothing, no tilemap or level format, and no per-level asset release.
decisive.gameImpact: Unloading a level means tracking and destroying every handle yourself. Destroying a parent leaves its children alive at their local offset from the world origin. Textures and audio buffers from past levels keep their slots. In a tile level, every tile counts against the 100 000 live-entity cap.
decisive.evidence: no clear or despawnAll in hyperion.ts; lib.rs:808-817 (engine_reset, dev-tools only, no TS caller); command_processor.rs:405-419 (children orphaned); hyperion.ts:675-680 (compact calls a non-existent shrinkUnusedTiers through 'as any'; the lib.rs:423-441 exports are never called); hyperion.test.ts:412-419 (only checks that compact() does not throw); types.ts:78 (MAX_GPU_ENTITIES 100 000); git grep for tilemap/tileset: 0
decisive.roundFix: No.
decisive.workaround: Keep a per-level registry of handles and destroy children before parents (PrefabInstance.destroyAll does this for prefabs). Stream tile chunks in and out around the camera. Destroy and re-create the engine between chapters, which means a new GPU device and reloading every texture.

decisive.dimension: Gameplay systems and the game-facing API
decisive.issue: There is no production save/load. Snapshots are dev-tools only and unwired, and the engine exposes no state readback a game could build one from.
decisive.gameImpact: A save system must keep the authoritative game state in TS and rebuild the world on load. Physics body positions can be read only by scanning SystemViews; velocities and angular state cannot be read at all, so a save made mid-air or on a moving platform cannot restore exact physics. The same rebuild is the only recovery from a GPU device loss.
decisive.evidence: lib.rs:808-844 (#[cfg(feature = 'dev-tools')]); crates/hyperion-core/Cargo.toml:10; ts/package.json:9; no TS caller of engine_snapshot_* (git grep: 0); hyperion.ts:281-282 (debug is null in production); system-views.ts:9-17; renderer.ts:270-272 (device lost: a log line and the callback, no recovery; the 'recupero trasparente' of hyperion-masterplan.md:232, 247 is false)
decisive.roundFix: No. Step 10 only forwards device loss in Mode A and corrects the masterplan lines (round plan:108).
decisive.workaround: Save game-level data (player, inventory, level id, checkpoint) and respawn the level on load. Avoid saving in the middle of physics.

decisive.dimension: Gameplay systems and the game-facing API
decisive.issue: Audio is SFX-grade. There is no music streaming, no bus, no fade, no per-sound pause or end callback; pause() silences everything, and nothing unlocks audio on the first gesture today.
decisive.gameImpact: Each music track is decoded whole into memory, minutes of stereo float PCM per track. There are no separate music/SFX/UI volumes and no crossfade between level themes. engine.pause() stops pause-menu music and UI clicks. In Chrome, a context created before a user gesture stays suspended until the game calls audio.resume() from one. On Safari, pausing before the first gesture hangs suspend().
decisive.evidence: audio-manager.ts:33-37, :86-94; playback-engine.ts:26-27 (one master gain), :30-61; hyperion.ts:598-607; hyperion.ts:864, 912-915 (listener set to the camera every tick); git grep for MediaElementAudioSource/AudioWorklet/fade: 0; round plan:83-87, :213
decisive.roundFix: Partly. The post-round audio step makes suspend() resolve on a never-started context, adds audio.state and a first-gesture unlock hook verified in Safari, and files a WebKit bug. Streaming, buses and fades are in no step.
decisive.workaround: Play music through an HTMLAudioElement or Web Audio graph (or a library such as Howler) beside the engine. Call engine.audio.resume() right after engine.pause() when UI sounds must keep playing.

decisive.dimension: Gameplay systems and the game-facing API
decisive.issue: In-canvas text is unfinished, and there is no UI/HUD or localization layer.
decisive.gameImpact: Score, health, dialogue, damage numbers and menus need one of two paths. One is an entity per glyph, through a pipeline never verified on GPU: TextManager never uploads the atlas, and layout is a single line with no wrap or kerning, in UTF-16 units. The other is a DOM overlay positioned by hand from world coordinates (there is no world-to-screen helper), which then takes keyboard focus from the canvas (gameplay-8). Localization (plural rules, CJK, RTL) is entirely the game's.
decisive.evidence: text-manager.ts:19; text-layout.ts:26, 47; index.ts:18-19; demo/primitives.ts:293-294; prim-params-schema.ts:48-51 (atlas rect plus rgb, no alpha); camera-api.ts:29-55 (no projection helper); hyperion-masterplan.md:35
decisive.roundFix: No.
decisive.workaround: Build the HUD and menus in DOM/HTML (or a UI framework) over the canvas, with an app-side i18n library. Compute screen positions from engine.cam.viewProjection.

decisive.dimension: Gameplay systems and the game-facing API
decisive.issue: Game logic cannot live in the engine's ECS: there are no custom components or systems. TS systems see only render rows indexed by GPU slot, and there is no per-entity readback.
decisive.gameImpact: Health, inventory, AI state and timers live in a separate TS object model keyed by entity id that the game must keep in sync. Finding where an entity is means scanning entityIds every frame (O(n)), one frame late in Modes A/B. There is no query by component, and none of this data is in snapshots.
decisive.evidence: hyperion-masterplan.md:629-633; engine.rs:340-378; ring_buffer.rs:124, 304-315 (no plugin opcode range despite hyperion-masterplan.md:239); system-views.ts:9-17; entity-handle.ts (no getter); plugin-context.ts:60-80 (side tables not cleared on release; the facade emits 'entity:released' at hyperion.ts:873); event-bus.ts:3-33 (untyped); git grep for getPosition/getVelocity/idToSlot: 0
decisive.roundFix: No.
decisive.workaround: Keep a TS entity store (Map<id, GameObject>) updated in hooks, and build an id-to-slot index from views.entityIds once per frame.

decisive.issue: The documented production build fails, and no validation runs it
decisive.gameImpact: The web build cannot be produced with the documented command (CLAUDE.md:69, docs/deployment-guide.md:56-66). Even once it builds, the production bundle (`__DEV__` false, bundled workers, an emitted .wasm) has never been run on a GPU in any mode.
