The worker graphs use dynamic import: engine-worker.ts:41 imports the WASM glue, and render-worker.ts → renderer → texture-manager → basis-transcoder.ts:85-87 imports the transcoder. The 5b plan records that `npm --prefix ts run build` 'fallisce già su aa9ee92 (worker.format iife con code-splitting nei worker)' (docs/plans/2026-09-27-transparent-sort-uber-plan.md:9340). vite.config.ts is unchanged since 75fecc7. scripts/preflight.sh never runs `npm run build`, and no GPU session record mentions a production bundle. Not re-run here (read-only task).
decisive.roundFix: Not in the round. The failure is recorded only in the 5b plan, not in round plan §2-§4, CLAUDE.md or step 9's list.
decisive.workaround: Probably `worker: { format: 'es' }` in the Vite config, since the engine already creates module workers. This is unverified. Then run a GPU pass over the production bundle in Modes B and C.

decisive.issue: No licence grant and no third-party notices
decisive.gameImpact: A team that does not hold the copyright has no right to use or ship the engine. Every shipped build also owes the licence texts of what is compiled in. For the owner's own team this is a compliance chore; for anyone else it stops adoption. The fix is one file plus a manifest line.
decisive.evidence: git ls-files has no LICENSE, COPYING or NOTICE. Cargo.toml:6-8 declares `license = "MIT"` under [workspace.package], but crates/hyperion-core/Cargo.toml:1-4 inherits only version and edition, so neither the crate nor the generated ts/wasm/package.json carries a licence. ts/package.json has no license field. ts/vendor/basis_transcoder.js and .wasm (Basis Universal, Apache-2.0, added in fb6eb08) contain no licence text (`grep -c license` returns 0) and record no version. The locked dependency closure is permissive (MIT, Apache-2.0, Zlib, Unlicense), but rapier2d 0.34, parry2d 0.29, nalgebra 0.35, simba and approx are Apache-2.0 only.
decisive.roundFix: Not in the round. Round plan §2-§3 have no licensing item, and step 9 only refreshes docs and CLAUDE.md.
decisive.workaround: The owner adds a LICENSE, `license.workspace = true` in the crate, a generated notices file (e.g. cargo-about) and the Basis Apache-2.0 text.

decisive.issue: No installable or versioned distribution: a game has to vendor the source and build the WASM itself
decisive.gameImpact: Setting up a game means a git submodule of the engine and a path import of ts/src/index.ts into a Vite project. That project must re-create the engine's own config: COOP/COEP headers, the `__DEV__` define, raw WGSL imports and module workers. Every dev machine and CI runner needs Rust 1.97.1, wasm-pack and binaryen. Each engine update is a source merge plus a WASM rebuild, and there is no version to pin. Non-Vite bundlers and a CDN-hosted .wasm are not supported.
decisive.evidence:
- ts/package.json:2-5: private 0.1.0, with no main, exports, types or files; it is the only package.json in git.
- No `build.lib` in vite.config.ts, and no declaration emit in tsconfig.json.
- ts/wasm is gitignored (.gitignore:3).
- The WASM path is hard-coded (engine-worker.ts:41, worker-bridge.ts:384), and `default()` is always called without arguments (engine-worker.ts:42, worker-bridge.ts:390), so the URL comes from the glue (hyperion_core.js:562-568).
- renderer.ts has 22 `?raw` imports.
- No git tags.
decisive.roundFix: None. No step touches packaging. The masterplan puts an npm scope for plugins after Phase 10 (§14.6) and lists framework and Electron/Tauri templates as long-term vision (§20, :969).
decisive.workaround: A submodule plus a Vite alias, with a scripted `build:wasm:release` in the game's build, or commit the built WASM. Pin an engine commit.

decisive.issue: No documentation for engine users, and the one user guide is stale
decisive.gameImpact: A new team has to learn the engine from JSDoc, an agent instruction file and a verification harness. Mode policy, asset limits, physics builds and deployment pitfalls must be rediscovered by reading code, and the deployment guide misleads on Node, Tauri and diagnostics.
decisive.roundFix: Partial and internal only. Step 9 refreshes CLAUDE.md and the stale docs listed in round plan §5, and step 10 corrects masterplan :232/:247. No step writes user documentation or examples.
decisive.workaround: Read the JSDoc in hyperion.ts and entity-handle.ts and the harness sections, and write an internal getting-started guide.

decisive.issue: Dev tools are half-wired, and most do nothing in Mode A
decisive.gameImpact: A complex game needs an inspector and a free camera. The inspector throws on first use and could show only position and radius. In Mode A the debug camera, the bounds and physics overlays, GPU profiling and the probe are all absent. The harness cannot catch this, because its Debug Tools checks pass as soon as a plugin installs.
decisive.evidence:
- ecs-inspector.ts:115 calls the getter `selectedIds` (selection.ts:69) as a method: TypeError on the first update. The loop removes the failing hook after 60 throws (game-loop.ts:16).
- `engine.selection` is null without a renderer (hyperion.ts:773-775).
- The WASM channel is a stub (ecs-inspector.ts:136).
- The debug camera moves only the main-thread camera (debug-camera.ts:54), while the Mode A render worker's camera is never synced (render-worker.ts:18, 41, 66).
- Both overlays return early without a renderer (bounds-visualizer.ts:93, physics-debug.ts:53).
- In Mode A GPU profiling returns false and the probe rejects (hyperion.ts:732-735, 317-319).
- debugCameraPlugin and ecsInspectorPlugin are not exported (index.ts).
- demo/debug-tools.ts:46-121 passes on 'plugin installed'.
decisive.roundFix: None. Round plan §4 (:122) calls the inspector bug out of scope, and no step owns it. Mode A camera sync and the main-thread-only overlays are not part of step 10, which covers the empty world and device lost only.
decisive.workaround: Develop in Mode B or C, patch the one-line inspector bug locally, read state from SystemViews, and use browser devtools for the rest.

decisive.issue: An app cannot select the physics or dev-tools WASM build
decisive.gameImpact: Today a physics game gets no collision events, raycasts or grounded state from the facade. The dev-tools features (state hash, snapshots, component inspection) need a hand-run wasm-pack into ts/wasm.
decisive.evidence: Nothing imports ts/wasm-physics. The only dev-tools script writes into wasm-physics (ts/package.json:13). PhysicsAPI._init (physics-api.ts:130) has no caller: hyperion.ts:124 wires only the producer. stateHash resolves null without dev-tools (hyperion.ts:378-380, and the harness skips it at demo/debug-tools.ts:123-128).
decisive.roundFix: Step 8b (round plan §3 row 8b) wires PhysicsAPI in every mode and decides how an app and the harness get the physics build: a config option, a build alias, or the harness on the physics build. A dev-tools variant and a runtime option for the WASM URL are not in its scope.
decisive.workaround: Until 8b: build physics into ts/wasm by hand and call `_init` locally (Mode C only).

decisive.issue: No supported way to test game code headlessly against the real engine, and no CI
decisive.gameImpact: Gameplay regression tests (movement, physics, spawn/destroy churn, save/load) need home-made scaffolding around private seams. Rendering cannot be tested at all without a GPU browser. Nothing runs the engine's own suites on each change.
decisive.evidence:
- Hyperion.create needs an HTMLCanvasElement (types.ts:111-114), navigator (capabilities.ts:17-45) and DOM input (hyperion.ts:220).
- The loop advances only through requestAnimationFrame (game-loop.ts:99, 176); there is no public step(dt).
- createDirectBridge's default loader fetches the .wasm by URL (worker-bridge.ts:384-391).
- createRingBuffer reads the `crossOriginIsolated` global (ring-buffer.ts:366), which Node does not define.
- The types that fromParts needs (EngineBridge, Renderer) are not exported.
- engine_init overwrites the static ENGINE with a raw write (lib.rs:30-35): one engine per JS realm, and creating another leaks the previous one.
- No TS test loads the real WASM.
- No .github/ or other CI.
decisive.roundFix: None.
decisive.workaround: Use fromParts with a custom loadWasm that passes `{ module_or_path: bytes }`, as scripts/determinism-cross-version.mjs:51-58 does. Stub `crossOriginIsolated` and requestAnimationFrame, as hyperion.test.ts:742-757 does. Run one engine per test worker. For visual tests, use engine.debug.probe on a GPU runner, and set up your own CI.

decisive.issue: Failures are silent, hang, or stop the engine instead of being reported
decisive.gameImpact: A misdeployed or stale .wasm, a NaN in game code, or one exception in a collision callback gives one of four results: a startup that never finishes, a blank canvas, entities that silently stop updating, or a game frozen for good. At most one console line appears, and there is no hook to recover.
decisive.evidence:
- Mode B's ready() never rejects, because the worker's error is only logged (worker-bridge.ts:117-133, 184-186). Hyperion.create therefore awaits forever at hyperion.ts:193, with no fallback, and no Worker sets onerror.
- A failure to create the renderer is swallowed (hyperion.ts:212-216).
- If Mode A fails after `transferControlToOffscreen` (worker-bridge.ts:223), the fallback lands on a canvas that can no longer draw.
- The WASM counts rejected commands and dropped bytes (lib.rs:78-97), and an unknown opcode drops the rest of the batch (ring_buffer.rs:315-319). TS only declares those counters and never reads them (worker-bridge.ts:397-403), and there is no TS↔WASM protocol version check.
- NaN/Inf payloads are dropped without being counted (command_processor.rs:16-39).
- A throw inside tickFn (render, or the user collision callbacks dispatched inside it, physics-api.ts:256-277 via hyperion.ts:867) skips the requestAnimationFrame re-arm (game-loop.ts:166-176), after which start() is a no-op (game-loop.ts:88).
- With COOP/COEP missing, the engine runs in Mode C without a word.
- WorkerSupervisor only warns (worker-bridge.ts:101-106, marked 'TODO(Phase 5)').
- There is no uncapturederror handler.
decisive.roundFix: Only step 10: a Mode A device loss will reach config.onDeviceLost (round plan §3 row 10). Step 8b wires the physics callbacks, but isolating them is not in its exit criteria.
decisive.workaround: Wrap your own callbacks in try/catch, put a timeout around Hyperion.create, treat `engine.selection === null` as 'no renderer', and patch in a dev poll of the WASM counters.

decisive.issue: Public options and methods that silently do nothing
decisive.gameImpact: A team that sets a 120 Hz simulation, a larger command buffer, an overflow callback or texture streaming gets no effect and no warning. So does a team that relies on compact() or memoryStats in long sessions. The fixed tick rate is a Rust constant.
decisive.roundFix: None. Step 9 lists only the opaque() comment (round plan §4 :191), and the tonemap stub stays a declared skip (§3 row 3).
decisive.workaround: Do not rely on these options and methods. For a different tick rate, fork engine.rs.

decisive.issue: The asset pipeline only generates texture paths, and the compressed-texture path has never run with a real asset
decisive.gameImpact: Sprite sheets, tile sets, audio, fonts and levels get no build-time support. Art larger than 512 px, or non-square, is silently squashed into a 64-512 px square. KTX2/Basis, which mobile memory budgets and large atlases need, is unproven and probably fails when the transcoder loads.
decisive.evidence:
- The scanner reads one directory, non-recursively, and only image files (scanner.ts:54).
- PNG/JPEG sizes come out 0×0: image-size is loaded with `require` (scanner.ts:39) inside an ESM package and is not installed.
- The generated module contains paths only, and the repo itself does not use the plugin.
- Images are resized to their tier square (texture-manager.ts:5, 684-693), and a quad cannot sample a sub-rect.
- No KTX2 asset exists (Mac README:330).
- The Basis glue is UMD/CommonJS but is imported as an ESM default (basis-transcoder.ts:85-87). From the code this should fail; it was not run.
- Step 8 found that a BC7/ASTC file on an rgba8 tier fails silently and that KTXorientation is never read (step-8 plan :4482).
decisive.roundFix: None. Step 8 only makes tier images upright, and it explicitly leaves KTXorientation, the texture-manager fixes and textures in Mode A out of scope (step-8 plan :48).
decisive.workaround: Keep art in PNG squares of 512 px or less (one texture per animation frame), and write your own manifest and loaders for audio, fonts and levels.

decisive.issue: Behaviour changes from round to round with no versioning, changelog or deprecation path
decisive.gameImpact: A game that updates the engine mid-production gets visual and semantic changes with no release notes. Recorded tapes, snapshots and authored scenes render differently. Code that compensated for an old behaviour breaks: for example, art pre-flipped to correct the old upside-down sampling now comes out inverted.
decisive.roundFix: None, and step 8 itself adds one more visual breaking change. Masterplan principle 5 (:59) calls the API near-irreversible after the first external user, but defines no mechanism for that.
decisive.workaround: Pin a commit, read CLAUDE.md gotchas and round plan §4 before each update, and re-record tapes and snapshots.

decisive.issue: No editor or level-design tooling, and prefabs cannot describe a full game object
decisive.gameImpact: A game with many levels needs authored data. The team must write its own level format and an importer (for Tiled or LDtk), and keep lights, bodies, colliders and depth in code.
decisive.evidence: ts/src contains no scene serialization or importer. PrefabNode (prefab/types.ts:12-23) has no fields for lights, rigid bodies, colliders, depth or transparency, its children cannot nest, and its texture is a session-scoped number (types.ts:4). Masterplan §1.3 (:35) excludes a visual editor, the 'Hyperion Canvas' level editor (§18.1, :909) is not started, and §20 (:969) mentions a light editor only as long-term vision.
decisive.roundFix: None.
decisive.workaround: Tiled or LDtk, plus a custom loader that maps layers and objects to spawn(), light(), rigidBody() and collider() calls.

decisive.issue: The default `preferredMode: 'auto'` picks Mode A on Chromium and desktop shells, where textures, camera control and the dev tools do not work
decisive.gameImpact: The web build on Chrome/Edge lands in Mode A, and so does a desktop build on Electron or WebView2 once it is cross-origin isolated. There, loadTexture throws, the camera never scrolls, particles return null, and outlines and bloom throw: a sprite game cannot run. The error messages say 'no renderer available' without naming the mode or the fix. Browsers without WebGPU get no rendering at all, because there is no fallback.
decisive.evidence:
- capabilities.ts:31-36 and :47-50 choose Mode A from a Chrome/Edge user-agent test.
- hyperion.ts:564/578 (textures throw), :847 (particles return null), :791/:813 (outlines and bloom throw), :211 (no WebGPU means no renderer).
- render-worker.ts:18/41/66 keeps an unsynced camera.
- The harness defaults to Mode B to avoid exactly this (demo/preferred-mode.ts:5-15).
- The WebGL 2 fallback sits in the masterplan §19 backlog.
decisive.roundFix: Partial. Step 10 makes an empty Mode A world render and forwards device loss. Step 8 declares 'no textures in Mode A' a limitation (round plan §2 :70, §4 :217). No step owns camera sync or texture loading in Mode A.
decisive.workaround: Always pass `preferredMode: 'B'` and serve COOP/COEP. In Electron and Tauri, set the headers in the protocol handler.

decisive.issue: The texture model caps a complete game. Each tier array holds at most 255 images (4 square tiers, 64-512 px), every PNG or JPEG is resampled to its tier's square, nothing is kept above 512 px, quads have no UV sub-rectangle (so no atlas, sprite sheet or tileset), and a loaded texture can never be freed during the session.
decisive.gameImpact: A multi-level game with sprite animation and tilesets runs out of layers, because every animation frame and every tile takes a layer of its own. On BC7/ASTC desktops all PNGs share the 4 × 255 rgba8 overflow layers. Backgrounds and atlases above 512 px are downscaled, non-square art is stretched, and pixel art is resampled with resizeQuality 'high' and a linear sampler. Changing level cannot release GPU memory: tier 3 in rgba8 at 256 layers is about 358 MB, counting the mips it allocates and never uses.
decisive.evidence: texture-manager.ts:5-7 (TIER_SIZES, MAX_LAYERS_PER_TIER), :18 (GROWTH_STEPS up to 256), :684-702 (resize to the tier square), :707-714 and :733-740 (overflow or primary tier full: throw), :216-218 (linear sampler), :258 and :477 (mips allocated); prelude.wgsl:153-171 (LOD 0 only); prim-params-schema.ts:32 ('Quad has no schema'); quad.wgsl:5-7 (uv = position + 0.5); hyperion.ts:675-680 (compact() calls a shrinkUnusedTiers that does not exist).
decisive.roundFix: Not fixed. Step 8 only makes tier images draw upright (16f5a9c, prelude.wgsl:191-198) and documents the limits in the loadTexture JSDoc. The step-8 plan lists texture unloading and tier mips as out of scope (2026-10-14-step8-sprite-light-plan.md:48). The masterplan has only 'sized binding arrays' (§17.3 #12), with no schedule.
decisive.workaround: Slice all art into square images of at most 512 px, one layer each. Budget at most 255 per size class per session. Destroy and re-create the engine between levels, which in Mode A needs a fresh canvas.

decisive.issue: Mirrored sprites disappear. Every entity pipeline culls back faces (cullMode 'back' with the default frontFace 'ccw'), so a negative scale, the usual way to flip a 2D character, reverses the winding and the quad is not drawn. Its occluder and selection seeds are not drawn either. There is no per-entity UV flip.
decisive.gameImpact: A character turned to face left vanishes, and a rig flipped with scale(-1, 1) loses every child sprite. Lines and beziers behave the same way.
decisive.evidence: forward-pass.ts:271 (uber transparent pipeline) and :285 (opaque pipelines); occluder-seed-stage.ts:96; selection-seed-pass.ts:107; no frontFace anywhere in ts/src. The defect is recorded in the round plan §2, line 72, and in the step-8 plan, line 4670.
decisive.roundFix: Not fixed. Step 8 sets cullMode 'none' only on the light pipeline (light-accum-stage.ts:164-166) and records the entity defect in §4 as point '(1b)'. No step owns it.
decisive.workaround: Ship pre-mirrored copies of the images, which doubles the layers they use under robustness-1.

decisive.issue: A single exception anywhere in the frame stops the engine for good. GameLoop.frame calls tickFn outside any try/catch, so requestAnimationFrame is never armed again. _running stays true, so start() does nothing. A throw from Hyperion.tick, renderer.render, any render-graph pass (plugin overlays included) or a WASM trap in Mode C is fatal. Mode A's render worker loop has the same flaw.
decisive.gameImpact: A bug in a plugin pass, a bad parameter that makes a pass throw, or a Rust panic freezes the game for good, with no event the game can catch to restart the loop.
decisive.evidence: game-loop.ts:166-176 (tickFn not isolated, rAF armed after it) and :88 (start() returns when already running); render-graph.ts:210-225 (catch, then rethrow); renderer.ts:1090-1096 (rethrow); render-worker.ts:70-80 (no catch); no panic hook in crates/hyperion-core (no set_hook or console_error_panic_hook).
decisive.roundFix: Not fixed by any step. Round step 1 isolated only hooks (game-loop.ts:179-220).
decisive.workaround: Wrap your own code defensively. Watch stats.tickCount for a stall, then destroy and re-create the engine.

decisive.issue: GPU device loss is not recovered. The renderer logs the loss and calls config.onDeviceLost. No API rebuilds the renderer or re-uploads textures, and production builds have no ECS snapshot (snapshot and restore are dev-tools only). In Mode A the loss stays inside the render worker. The masterplan still says 'device.lost recovery trasparente'.
decisive.gameImpact: After a driver reset, a GPU process crash or GPU switching, the canvas freezes or goes black while the simulation keeps running. Recovering means rebuilding the whole world from the game's own state, or reloading the page.
decisive.evidence: renderer.ts:270-273; lib.rs:807-835 (#[cfg(feature = "dev-tools")] on engine_reset/snapshot_create/snapshot_restore); render-worker.ts:37 (createRenderer without a callback); hyperion-masterplan.md:232, 247; no uncapturederror handler in the engine (only the harness has one, demo/probe-checks.ts:110).
decisive.roundFix: Partial. Step 10 forwards Mode A's device lost (worker → bridge → config.onDeviceLost) and corrects masterplan lines 232 and 247 (round plan §3, row 10). Recovery itself remains missing after the round.
decisive.workaround: In onDeviceLost, save the game state and reload the page, or destroy and re-create the engine (with a new canvas in Mode A) and respawn the world.

decisive.issue: Startup failures are silent, and some hang. (a) Mode A transfers the canvas with transferControlToOffscreen before it knows WebGPU works in the worker. If the render worker fails, the fallback to Mode B calls createRenderer on the transferred canvas, the error is swallowed, and the canvas stays blank with no message. (b) Any main-thread createRenderer failure is swallowed without a log. (c) Mode B's ready promise can never reject, and no bridge listens to worker onerror, so a worker or WASM load failure leaves Hyperion.create pending forever. (d) The 'auto' mode chooses Mode A by user-agent sniffing.
decisive.gameImpact: On some Chromium configurations, or after a CDN hiccup that loses the .wasm, players get a blank canvas or a loader that never finishes, and the engine reports nothing the game can surface.
decisive.evidence: worker-bridge.ts:223 (transfer before any worker check); hyperion.ts:174-201 (fallback chain), :212-216 (catch { renderer = null }, no log); worker-bridge.ts:117-120 (Mode B ready has only a resolve) and :131-132 (an 'error' message is only logged); no onerror in ts/src; capabilities.ts:31-36 (webgpuInWorker guessed from the UA). In M12 Safari 27 did not hit the fallback defect, because it runs WebGPU in the worker (README §M12).
decisive.roundFix: Not fixed. Step 10 covers only the empty world and device-lost forwarding.
decisive.workaround: Pin preferredMode to 'B' or 'C'. Put a timeout around Hyperion.create. Check renderer availability indirectly, for example compressionFormat is null when there is no renderer.

decisive.issue: Modes A and B have no flow control and no working supervision. The main thread posts a tick message every requestAnimationFrame whether or not the previous tick is done (TickSequencer counts ticks in flight but never gates them). The 10-tick spiral cap applies per message, not per unit of real time. The supervisor reports a single heartbeat timeout and never resets: no restart, no A→B→C degradation, and onModeChange is never called. Mode B always draws a state at least one frame old.
decisive.gameImpact: When the simulation is heavier than a frame (physics, many entities, a slow device), the worker's message queue and the input-to-display latency grow without bound instead of the game slowing down. A crashed worker leaves a frozen game, the queued critical commands keep accumulating, and the only trace is a console warning. A pause longer than 3 s raises a false timeout and silences later ones.
decisive.evidence: worker-bridge.ts:174-177 and :342-345 (one postMessage per tick); tick-sequencer.ts:15-41; engine.rs:207-218 (cap per update call); supervisor.ts:33-52 (reset() has no caller); worker-bridge.ts:101-106 and :215-220 (TODO(Phase 5): only console.warn); engine-worker.ts:68-89 (no try/catch around engine_update). The masterplan promises restart and degradation (hyperion-masterplan.md:124, 191).
decisive.roundFix: Not fixed: no step covers it.
decisive.workaround: Keep the per-tick simulation cost well under one frame on the slowest target, or use Mode C, which is synchronous and slows down instead of queueing.

decisive.issue: The simulation runs at a hard-coded 60 Hz and nothing interpolates between ticks. config.fixedTimestep is ignored, interpolation_alpha() is never exported, and every frame shows the latest tick unchanged. On frames where no tick ran, the engine still copies and re-uploads the full state.
decisive.gameImpact: Motion and camera follow judder whenever the display rate is not exactly 60 Hz: at 120 Hz each state stays for 2 frames (Chrome ran rAF at 120 Hz on the M2), at 75 or 144 Hz the cadence is uneven, and even at 60 Hz timing jitter gives 0 or 2 ticks per frame. A camera moved from TS every frame drifts against sprites stepped at 60 Hz. Physics cannot run at another rate.
decisive.evidence: engine.rs:19 (FIXED_DT), :207-218, :406-411 (interpolation_alpha in Rust only); config.fixedTimestep is resolved (types.ts:127) and read nowhere else; hyperion.ts:876-909 (the state is rendered as is); README:18 (rAF at 120 Hz in Chrome on the M2).
decisive.roundFix: Not fixed, and not in the masterplan.
decisive.workaround: None inside the engine. A game could compute its own interpolation and drive it with positionImmediate for the few entities whose motion matters.

decisive.issue: Every frame copies the whole SoA (about 128 bytes per entity) and allocates in the hot path, in every mode. This breaks the masterplan's 'no GC pressure in the game loop' constraint. The engine worker allocates 6 new typed arrays per tick. The Mode A main thread copies all of them again. Mode C copies every column out of WASM memory each frame. Each command allocates a payload typed array and a queue entry. With any particle emitter alive, the renderer builds a Map of N tuples every frame. Rust builds a HashMap of every mapped entity each frame, and fills a legacy matrix buffer that TS never reads.
decisive.gameImpact: At 100k entities that is about 12.8 MB of fresh buffers per frame (twice that in Mode A), and about 1.3 MB at 10k. The likely result is GC pauses and jank on mid-range and mobile devices. CPU frame cost has never been measured. The only data point is 100k static quads at 120 fps in Mode B on an M2 Pro.
decisive.evidence: worker-render-state.ts:135-155; worker-bridge.ts:279-300 (Mode A copies), :494-499 and :519-524 (Mode C copies); backpressure.ts:166-190 and :403-476 (new Float32Array per command); renderer.ts:1119-1130 (particle Map); engine.rs:228-229 (per-frame HashMap) and :242 with render_state.rs:258-263 (legacy collect); engine_render_state_* exports are only declared in TS (worker-bridge.ts:405-407); hyperion-masterplan.md:71; bench-head.json (fps 120 at N = 100000).
decisive.roundFix: Not fixed.
decisive.workaround: Keep entity counts well below the cap on low-end targets, avoid particle emitters in large scenes, batch commands, and profile GC in the target browsers.

decisive.issue: The ring buffer is fixed at 64 KB, and the related config is ignored: commandBufferSize, backpressure 'drop' and onOverflow are never read. About 3 855 SetPosition commands, or roughly 1 000 fully configured sprite spawns, fit per frame. Beyond that the queue defers the rest round-robin, with a single dev-only warning. Spawn commands drain before any setter, and a spawned entity is drawable at once as a white unit quad at the origin. There is no visibility toggle to spawn an entity hidden.
decisive.gameImpact: A level load that spawns thousands of entities in one frame flashes white quads at the origin for several frames while positions, scales and textures trickle in. TS-driven motion above about 3.8k entities per frame quietly updates each entity at a fraction of the frame rate.
decisive.evidence: worker-bridge.ts:12 (RING_BUFFER_CAPACITY = 64 * 1024); types.ts:125-126 (resolved but unused, no consumer in ts/src); ring-buffer.ts:97-125 (payload sizes) and :222-226 (5 + payload bytes); backpressure.ts:269-286 (criticals first; setters wait while any critical remains); command_processor.rs:530-544 (default quad, white texture, origin, scale 1); components.rs:64, 91, 489-492; no visibility command among types 0-16 (ring_buffer.rs:35-52); ring-buffer-bench.test.ts:36 (the bench used 1 MB).
decisive.roundFix: Not fixed.
decisive.workaround: Spawn large levels in chunks of under about 1 000 entities per frame behind a DOM loading overlay. Move entities with velocity or physics in Rust instead of per-frame SetPosition.

decisive.issue: The default 'auto' mode picks Mode A on any Chromium user agent (Electron included), and Mode A is a reduced engine. The main-thread camera never reaches the render worker, which keeps a fixed orthographic camera. loadTexture throws. Particle emitters return null, and bloom and outlines throw. Probes are unavailable. Today the empty world and device lost are also broken in Mode A.
decisive.gameImpact: A game shipped with default settings would be unable to scroll the camera or show any textured sprite in Chrome and Electron, and nothing would fail loudly enough to be noticed early.
decisive.evidence: capabilities.ts:31-36 and :47-50; render-worker.ts:18, :40-41, :65-66 (worker camera fixed at init and resize); hyperion.ts:862-916 (tick sends only the listener position, no camera); hyperion.ts:564 (no renderer: throw) and :847 (null emitter); worker-bridge.ts:272 and render-worker.ts:72 (empty world); README §M6 (?mode=auto picks A on Chrome/macOS).
decisive.roundFix: Partial. Step 10 fixes the empty world and forwards device lost. Step 8 declares 'textures do not load in Mode A' a limitation (round plan §2, line 70). Camera sync, textures, particles and effects in Mode A stay missing.
decisive.workaround: Always set preferredMode: 'B', or 'C' where there is no SharedArrayBuffer.

decisive.issue: The verified platform matrix is narrow, and there is no CI. The current code runs on hardware only on an Apple M2 Pro: Chrome in Modes A, B and C, and Safari last verified before steps 6-8. The AMD iGPU on Linux was verified in Modes B and C up to phase 5b, and the RTX 4060 only for compute timings. Nothing ran on Windows/D3D12, Firefox, Android, iOS, Electron or Tauri, or on an ASTC device. The deployment guide's Electron and Tauri setup is untested. It contradicts the detection code: SharedArrayBuffer is detected only when crossOriginIsolated, so a page loaded with loadFile would run in Mode C. GPU checks are run by hand through MCP on one Mac.
decisive.gameImpact: A web and desktop release depends on platforms where no frame of the engine has ever been looked at. Windows and Chromium on D3D12 is the main desktop market. Driver-specific failures of the kind found on Metal and AMD (subgroup widths, indirect-first-instance, compressed copies) are likely to exist elsewhere.

decisive.issue: No sprite sheets or texture atlases. A quad always samples its whole texture layer, so frame animation needs one texture per frame.
decisive.gameImpact: Character, enemy and VFX animation, the core of an action-adventure or platformer, cannot use standard sprite-sheet or atlas assets (TexturePacker, Aseprite). Swapping a texture per frame burns through 255 layers per tier, and they can never be freed.

decisive.issue: The texture pipeline caps and distorts art. Every PNG/JPEG is resized to a square of at most 512 px, sampled linearly at LOD 0 only, limited to 255 textures per tier per session, and never unloaded.
decisive.gameImpact: HD backgrounds and large tilesets lose resolution. Non-square art is stretched unless the entity's scale restores the aspect. Pixel art is blurred twice: a high-quality resize up to the tier size, then linear filtering. Zoomed-out sprites alias because mips are never sampled. A game with many levels runs out of layers, because nothing frees them.
decisive.evidence: ts/src/texture-manager.ts:5 (tier sizes 64-512), :684-701 (resizeWidth = resizeHeight = tier size), :216-219 (only a linear sampler), :7 and :733-740 (throws when a tier is full), :882 (destroy() is the only release); ts/src/shaders/primitives/prelude.wgsl:151-167 (textureSampleLevel at 0.0); ts/src/hyperion.ts:545-561 (the loadTexture JSDoc states the resize and the cap)
decisive.roundFix: No. Step 8's plan lists texture unloading, textures in Mode A and tier mips as out of scope (docs/plans/2026-10-14-step8-sprite-light-plan.md:48), and no later step owns them. Masterplan §15.2, sized binding arrays (hyperion-masterplan.md:718-726), would remove the tiers, but it depends on browsers and exists only as a design artifact (ts/src/shaders/basic-binding-array.wgsl).
decisive.workaround: Slice large images into square tiles of at most 512 px by hand, pre-scale pixel art to the tier size with nearest-neighbour, and keep the total under 4×255 textures. Otherwise, engine work on TextureManager: sizes, aspect, a sampler choice, mip generation and a free list of layers.

missedBlockers.issue: Screen-space SDF lighting: casters outside the view cast no shadow. A lit scrolling platformer will show popping shadows unless it opts in, if 8c implements it.

check.summary:
Verified read-only at feat/step8-sprite-light 4d1940f against the code, round plan §2-§5, the step-8 plan scope (:48) and hyperion-masterplan.md. Of 75 issues: 50 confirmed, 25 partly, 0 refuted. After verification 5 blockers remain, from two themes. (1) The texture/content model: no UV sub-rect on any colour primitive (no atlas, sprite sheet or tileset), PNG/JPEG resampled to 64-512 px squares, 255 images per array per session, linear LOD 0 only, nothing unloadable (texture-manager.ts:5-7, :686-701, :709-740, :883; quad.wgsl:5-7). No round step touches it (step 8 only turns images upright), so it is THE blocker after the round (rendering-1, gameplay-1, robustness-1, roadmap-2). (2) Physics unreachable from TS (PhysicsAPI._init never called, ts/wasm built without physics-2d; gameplay-3): fixed by step 8b if it meets its exit criteria.

Downgraded: mirrored sprites culled (blocker to major: four cullMode lines, recorded as §4 (1b) for step 9 but not committed); the production build (blocker to major: npm run build fails, probably a one-line Vite fix, but the bundle has never run); the licence (to minor: one file, a legal stop only for third parties); roadmap-level blockers (to major: the masterplan defines a rendering primitive, so the game layer is expected TS work); the whole Mode A cluster (major to minor: it fails loudly and preferredMode 'B' avoids it; Mode A stays experimental after step 10). Also minor: animation system, save system, tick flow control, per-frame allocations (100k at 120 fps measured in Mode B on the M2), ring-buffer size, dev tools, CI, versioning, no-op config options, the Firefox premise (Gecko maps indirect-first-instance: [Mozilla Bug 1743667 commit mirror](https://source-hub.etos-pro.ru/mozilla/gecko-dev/commit/0b48a2d1e1c647708029518db768f4fb1c7d4205)). Missed by all six (major): no extension point for custom effects, materials or post-processing; screen-space SDF shadows from off-screen casters pop in at the view edge while scrolling (8c may add only an opt-in padding). Minor caveat: the opaque path has no alpha cutout, so every sprite with transparency must be .transparent().

What the round delivers: step 8 sprite lights and upright tier images; 8b physics events and queries in every mode plus a physics build for apps; 8c the point/spot march stopping at the SDF exit, maybe an opt-in padding; step 10 the Mode A empty world, Mode A device-loss forwarding and the masterplan fix; step 9 docs, reviews and Mac Chrome plus Safari A/B/C legs; the audio step the WebKit suspend fix and a first-gesture unlock. Not touched: the texture model, flip/tint/visibility, interpolation or tick rate, input, text/UI, particles, music, tilemaps/levels, custom effects, bundle/packaging/licence/user docs/CI, fault handling, device-loss recovery, WebGL fallback, and Windows/mobile/Firefox/desktop-shell verification.

Post-round readiness. Usable with caveats: Mode B/C on desktop Chrome and Safari (macOS-verified only), GPU-driven rendering up to 100k entities, transparent sort, hierarchy/prefabs, fixed 60 Hz simulation, 2D lighting with soft shadows and sprite lights (about 2-4 ms at 1080p on desktop GPUs), Rapier physics after 8b (gravity/units/shape/velocity caveats), SFX audio. Experimental: Mode A, KTX2/Basis, MSDF text, GPU particles, dev tools, mobile, Firefox, Windows, Electron/Tauri. Missing: sprite sheets/atlases, texture unload, tint/alpha/visibility, working flip, animation, tilemaps/level import, interpolation, gamepad/multi-touch, in-canvas UI/text, music streaming/buses/fades, state readback, device-loss recovery, WebGL fallback, custom effects, an installable package and user docs. Verdict: fit for a technical prototype or vertical slice on desktop (Mode B, DOM UI, art authored to tier squares, physics after 8b). It is not ready for a complete complex game without an engine track first: texture model with UV rects and unload, flip/tint, interpolation, input, build/packaging, fault handling and recovery. That comes on top of the game layer the team would write anyway.
